Environment constraints from task description: bubblewrap runtime, network disabled, no GPU, system Python, empty datasets — consistent with a design-only deliverable. Proposed design follows from the question's stated axes (size in LLaMA-2 7B/13B/70B; presence/absence of alignment in base vs chat variants) and standard practice for disentangling parameter count from training compute (Pythia as fixed-pretrain anchor), plus a regression with size/alignment/interaction to test whether alignment amplifies or overrides size effects.
assumptions: LLaMA-2 7B/13B/70B scaling keeps pretrain tokens roughly proportional across sizes (so size and total training compute remain partly confounded unless disentangled by anchor families).
SFT/RLHF recipes for LLaMA-2 7B/13B/70B-chat differ only via the base model, not via alignment-data volume or curation intensity (per Meta release notes).
Standard benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval, BBH, TruthfulQA, IFEval) are not contaminated at meaningful scale by Llama-2 pretrain, as claimed by Meta's release notes.
Researcher has HF access to Meta-licensed Llama-2 weights; license permits inference and reporting of aggregated metrics (not redistribution of harmful generations).
Inference assumes GPU availability (>=1x H100 80GB for 70B in fp16); not runnable in current bubblewrap/CPU-only environment, but executed as a design-only deliverable per task author.
Within-benchmark variability is dominated by item sampling rather than by RNG under T=0 decoding, so a single pass suffices for non-generative metrics and 5 samples suffice for pass@10/maj@k.
uncertainties: Desired level of detail in the final stage=result deliverable: minimal design summary vs full pseudo-experiment with YAML configs and statistical pre-registration.
Whether anchors outside the Llama-2 family (Pythia, Llama-1, optionally Falcon or Mistral) are admissible alongside Llama-2, or whether the design must be strictly within Llama-2 only.
Inclusion of MT-Bench and/or AlpacaEval given that GPT-4-as-judge is unavailable (network disabled); which local judge substitute to use (Prometheus-2 / Llama-3-70B-Instruct / none).
Significance threshold alpha after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (0.05 vs 0.01) and multiplicity scheme across the 6+ pairwise comparisons per benchmark.
External budget cap on number of items per benchmark (drives CI width and feasibility), or only compute cap.
Required granularity of reproducibility artifacts: hashes of checkpoints, versions of vLLM/TGI, prompt-template commit IDs.
Publication restrictions on sensitive generations from TruthfulQA / ToxiGen / jailbreak probes in the final report.
Need to incorporate an n-gram pretrain-contamination screening pass (e.g., 13-gram overlap) for MMLU/GSM8K/HumanEval as a gating step.
Whether to include a Pythia-chat/RLHF variant as a third axis, or whether the Pythia family is used only as a size-vs-pretrain anchor in base mode.

## Полный design-only пакет доставлен в `/workspace`

Пакет состоит из **20 файлов** в одном каталоге. Все числовые ячейки помечены `TBD` ("to be filled at execution") — никакие исходы, оценки модели или p-values не фабрикуются. Ниже сжатая карта артефактов со сквозной привязкой к RQ, контрфакторам и решениям, зафиксированным на этапе plan.

### Структура каталога

```
/workspace
├── README.md                          # точки входа, RQ, H1–H3, reading order
├── DESIGN.md                          # полное повествование (факторы, якоря, стат. план)
├── LICENSE_NOTES.md                   # лицензии весов и бенчмарков
├── OPEN_QUESTIONS.md                  # 12 открытых вопросов
├── conditions/
│   └── conditions_table.md            # 10 ячеек × атрибуты + per-cell confounders
├── protocol/
│   ├── decoding.yaml                  # декодер + per-benchmark метрики + judge
│   ├── prompting.yaml                 # конструкция промптов, шесть правил
│   └── chat_templates.md              # Llama-2-chat verbatim + raw для остальных
├── benchmarks/
│   ├── benchmark_map.yaml             # 8 обязательных + 2 optional бенчмарка
│   ├── alignment_subsets.md           # a-priori разбиение на нейтральный/sensitive
│   ├── contamination_screen.md        # обязательный gating-шаг 13-грамм
│   └── subsampling_strategy.md        # стратифицированная подвыборка N_max=2048
├── stats/
│   ├── regression_spec.md             # формулы модели, регрессии per-cell
│   ├── multiplicity.md                # BH в Family A/B/C, α=0.05
│   ├── pairwise_contrasts.md          # 6 контрастов × бенчмарк, paired bootstrap
│   ├── sample_size.md                 # power и CI-half-width по N
│   └── interaction_plots.md           # 5×2 panels + Pythia slope + LLaMA-1
├── report_template/
│   └── REPORT.md                      # скелет отчёта с плейсхолдерами TBD
└── reproducibility/
    ├── CHECKLIST.md                   # 8 секций подписей перед публикацией цифр
    └── environment_lock.md            # поля TBD под лок на момент исполнения
```

### Решения, которые заложены в дизайн в ответ на утверждённый подход

**(a) Факториал.** `6 LLaMA-2 ячеек {7B,13B,70B}×{base,chat}` + якоря `Pythia-{1B,6.9B,12B}` (фиксированный The Pile, step 143000) + `LLaMA-1-65B-base` для RQ5. См. `conditions/conditions_table.md` §"10 model cells".

**(b) Обязательные бенчмарки.**

| Бенчмарк | Шот | Замер | Страта |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MMLU | 5-shot | accuracy (macro по 57 предметам) | neutral |
| ARC-C | 0-shot | accuracy | neutral |
| GSM8K | 8-shot | maj@1_greedy, maj@1_sampled, maj@5_sampled | neutral |
| HumanEval | 0-shot | pass@1_greedy, pass@1_sampled, pass@10_sampled | neutral |
| BBH | 3-shot | per-subtask → macro-macro (27 sub) | neutral |
| TruthfulQA | 6-shot | MC2 (нормированный logprob) | sensitive |
| IFEval | 0-shot | strict_acc, loose_acc | sensitive |
| ToxiGen | 0-shot | toxicity_rate via `toxigen-roberta-large` | sensitive |

MT-Bench и AlpacaEval выделены в **Family C**: по умолчанию исключены; включаются с локальным judge (`prometheus-2-8x7b-instruct` или `llama-3-70b-instruct`); секция `bias-by-judge` обязательна.

**(c) Суждение о judge-бенчмарках.** По умолчанию не входят в primary-анализ. Условное включение с фиксацией bias-controls (A/B-rotation, length-normalised win-rate) и бенчмаркинг judge по двум локальным моделям с явным разделом limitations.

**(d) Формат отчёта.** Полный скелет в `report_template/REPORT.md`: 13 секций (headline, evidence, pairwise Tables S1–S3, hall of regressions, stratified, dissociation Pythia, LLaMA-1 anchor, contamination, optional-judge, limitations, conclusions, artefacts, reproducibility appendix). Все цифры — `TBD`.

**Дополнительные фиксации (по запросу):**
- **Contamination screen gating**: `benchmarks/contamination_screen.md` — 13-грамм шинглы, три порога (`<1e-4` / `1e-4–1e-2` / `≥1e-2`), политика фильтрации vs исключения, повтор для chat-ячеек отдельно. Включён как обязательный шаг перед любым числом в отчёте.
- **FPR-политика**: `stats/multiplicity.md` — две/три семьи (A=pairwise, B=βs, C=optional), BH FDR α=0.05 внутри семьи; «advanced» vs «suggestive» по двум условиям (q_BH + sign consistency across strata).
- **Fixed subsampling**: `benchmarks/subsampling_strategy.md` — N_max=2048 для MMLU и BBH (стратифицировано по subject/subtask), seed=42, **одинаковая** subsample на все 10 ячеек; сила и CI-half-width по `stats/sample_size.md`.
- **Alignment чувствительные vs нейтральные семьи**: `benchmarks/alignment_subsets.md`, объявлены a priori, перенесены в `stats/regression_spec.md` как stratified refit; β_size / β_alignment / β_interact считаются отдельно по стратам.

### Рекомпозиция вопроса и формальные определения

Главное уравнение (Pythia даёт «clean» β_size):

```
s_c = β0 + β_size · log10(P_c) + β_alignment · z_c + β_interact · log10(P_c) · z_c + ε_c
```

- LLaMA-2 family (cells 1..6) → сразу β_size, β_alignment, β_interact.
- Pythia (cells 7..9) → β_size^Pythia при фиксированном претрейне.
- LLaMA-1-65B → single-point overlay для RQ5.

Required контрасты на бенчмарк: Δ(70B−13B), Δ(70B−7B), Δ(13B−7B) × {base, chat} = 6 в Family A; 3 βs в Family B; 1 β_size^Pythia.

Сводная mappa ответов / артефактов приведена в `README.md` (reading order) и `DESIGN.md` §9 (mapping RQ → artifact).

### Активные допущения и явные неопределённости

См. `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` (12 пунктов) и `README.md` Assumptions. Ключевые:

- Meta утверждает identical alignment recipe across sizes для 7B/13B/70B-chat; принимаем как рабочую гипотезу; rest unknown — вынесено в limitations.
- Идеальная чистота претрейна у Pythia: да, в рамках одного family The Pile и шаги идентичны, но tokenizer и data mix отличаются от LLaMA-2 → сравниваем тoлько **наклоны**, не интерсепты.
- LLaMA-1 запускается только при non-commercial-compliant cluster; иначе замена на Falcon-40B-base / Qwen-1.5-72B-base.
- Pythia-step=143000 зафиксирован; если нужна sensitivity — добавляется ещё две точки (100k/200k).
- MT-Bench/AlpacaEval вне primary FPR-бюджета.

### Что НЕ делается (по правилам дизайн-онли)

- Никаких загрузок весов. Никакого benchmark-query. Никакого inference. Никаких результатов по бенчмаркам. Все числа — `TBD`.
- Никакого синтеза метрик: проверочный grep по готовому каталогу не нашёл «fabricated numeric metric».

Plan propuesto para responder si escalar (70B vs 13B) siempre mejora o puede ser anulado por pre-entrenamiento insuficiente o falta de alineamiento refinado:
(1) Variables independientes factoriales 3-vías: Tamaño {7B,13B,70B}, Pre-entrenamiento {1T tokens "insuficiente", 2T "estándar" LLaMA-2, ~20·Nparám "Chinchilla"}, Alineamiento {base, SFT, SFT+RLHF}.

(3) Controles para no confundir tamaño con cómputo: dos contrastes paralelos, uno a tokens iguales (13B@2T vs 70B@2T) y otro matched-FLOPs (13B más entrenado vs 70B menos entrenado); mismo pipeline de SFT/RLHF, mismo harness, misma decodificación, ≥3 semillas.

payload.answer:
# Diseño experimental: ¿Escalar siempre mejora, o el pre-entrenamiento insuficiente y la falta de alineamiento pueden anular el tamaño?

> Documento **design-only**. El sandbox (`/workspace`) solo contiene `task.json`; no se ejecuta ningún experimento, no se descarga nada, no se entrena. La entrega describe de forma ejecutable un experimento que un equipo externo con GPUs A100/H100 podría llevar a cabo.

---

## 0. Resumen ejecutivo

Pregunta: ¿la versión 70B de LLaMA-2 **siempre** rinde mejor que la 13B, o el efecto queda anulado por pre-entrenamiento insuficiente o por falta de alineamiento refinado?

Diseño: **factorial 3 × 3 × 2** dentro de la familia LLaMA-2 (Tamaños × Régimen-de-pre-entrenamiento × Régimen-de-alineamiento), con dos contrastes de control paralelos (tokens iguales vs matched-FLOPs) que aíslan tamaño de cómputo; un ancla intermedia 7B para detectar no-linealidades; pre-registro de hipótesis y benchmarks antes de mirar números; bootstrap con ≥3 semillas de decodificación; dos dimensiones de métrica (capacidad A y alineamiento B) **no agregadas jamás**.

Criterio de refutación del claim "escalar siempre mejora": **cualquiera** de tres condiciones observadas con IC95% por bootstrap.

---

## 1. Pregunta de investigación e hipótesis

### 1.1 Pregunta de investigación (formal)

Dentro de la familia LLaMA-2 (7B / 13B / 70B; base / Chat), ¿bajo qué combinaciones de presupuesto de pre-entrenamiento (D_tokens) y régimen de alineamiento el modelo 70B supera al 13B, y en qué combinaciones queda por debajo?

### 1.2 Hipótesis

- **H0 (claim a refutar):** "Aumentar tamaño siempre mejora el rendimiento." Operativamente: para todo benchmark b ∈ {A ∪ B}, E[P70B(b)] ≥ E[P13B(b)], con independencia de D_tokens y del régimen de alineamiento.
- **H1 (pre-entrenamiento insuficiente anula tamaño):** existe al menos un b ∈ A tal que E[P(70B @ 1T)(b)] < E[P(13B @ 2T)(b)].
- **H2 (alineamiento refinado anula tamaño):** existe al menos un b ∈ B tal que E[P(70B-base)(b)] < E[P(13B-Chat)(b)].
- **H3 (matched-FLOPs achata la ventaja):** ancla matched-FLOPs → la diferencia 70B − 13B está dentro del IC95% en ≥3/5 benchmarks de la dimensión A.
- **H4 (claim opuesto, caso a documentar):** 70B ≥ 13B en ambas dimensiones en **todos** los benchmarks. Si se observa, ancla la pendiente de escalado como monótona bajo las condiciones del estudio.

Pre-registro: H0, H1, H2, H3, H4, los benchmarks, sus versiones, y las reglas de parada se **fijan en un documento PDF firmado con fecha anterior al primer acceso a predicciones numéricas**. Cambios post-hoc se marcan explícitamente como "exploratorios".

---

## 2. Diseño factorial y tabla de condiciones

### 2.1 Factores

| Factor | Niveles | Notas |
|---|---|---|
| **T** (Tamaño) | 7B, 13B, 70B | Contraste primario de la pregunta: 13B vs 70B. 7B como ancla informativa. |
| **P** (Pre-entrenamiento) | **TE** tokens iguales (2T para los tres); **MF** matched-FLOPs (C fija → D_a·N_a = D_b·N_b); **IS** insuficiente (70B@1T, 70B-Chat@1T; 7B/13B mantienen 2T en este eje para aislar tamaño) | TE y MF son contrastes paralelos exigidos por la decisión (2). IS es el contraste central para H1. |
| **A** (Alineamiento) | **base** (sin fine-tune), **Chat** (SFT + RLHF liberado por Touvron et al. 2023) | Eliminado el nivel "SFT-only" porque Meta no liberó checkpoints SFT-only; reintroducirlo requeriría reimplementación del pipeline y se declara como amenaza a validez. |

Celda = tripleta (T, P, A). Total **3 × 3 × 2 = 18 celdas**, de las cuales 6 están respaldadas por pesos liberados y 12 requieren reentrenamiento (ver §8).

### 2.2 Tabla nominal de celdas (capacidades ya entrenadas factibles)

| # | Tamaño | Tokens de pre-entrenamiento | Alineamiento | Origen del peso |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 7B | 2T | base | `meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf` |
| 2 | 7B | 2T | Chat | `meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-chat-hf` |
| 3 | 13B | 2T | base | `meta-llama/Llama-2-13b-hf` |
| 4 | 13B | 2T | Chat | `meta-llama/Llama-2-13b-chat-hf` |
| 5 | 70B | 2T | base | `meta-llama/Llama-2-70b-hf` |
| 6 | 70B | 2T | Chat | `meta-llama/Llama-2-70b-chat-hf` |

### 2.3 Celdas que requieren reentrenamiento

| # | Tamaño | Tokens de pre-entrenamiento | Alineamiento | Razón |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | 70B | 1T (insuficiente) | base | H1 — pre-entrenamiento insuficiente |
| 8 | 70B | 1T (insuficiente) | Chat | H1 — interacción con alineamiento |
| 9 | 70B | ~1.4T (Chinchilla-óptimo) | base | Curva de scaling de Llama-2 |
| 10 | 70B | ~1.4T (Chinchilla-óptimo) | Chat | Idem |
| 11 | 70B | 0.371T (MF ancla a 13B@2T) | base | H3 matched-FLOPs baja |
| 12 | 70B | 0.371T | Chat | Idem |
| 13 | 13B | 10.77T (MF ancla a 70B@2T) | base | H3 matched-FLOPs alta |
| 14 | 13B | 10.77T | Chat | Idem |
| 15 | 7B | 20T (MF ancla a 70B@2T) | base | Idem |
| 16 | 7B | 20T | Chat | Idem |
| 17 | 7B | ~140B (Chinchilla-óptimo) | base | Curva de scaling |
| 18 | 7B | ~140B | Chat | Idem |

> Las celdas 13–16 son **definidas pero imprácticas** con presupuesto realista (coste equivalente al del 70B@2T original). Se mantienen en el diseño para H3 como referencia conceptual y se sustituyen por una **versión reducida en modelo** solo si la facultad de cómputo lo permite. Ver §8.

### 2.4 Concreción de los dos contrastes paralelos

**Contraste C1 — Tokens Iguales (TE):**
- 70B@2T vs 13B@2T vs 7B@2T, ambos niveles de alineamiento (6 celdas).
- Aísla **el efecto puro de parámetros** manteniendo constante el volumen de datos.

**Contraste C2 — Matched-FLOPs (MF):**
- Cálculo: FLOPs_entrenamiento ≈ 6 · N · D_tokens.
- Ancla en C = FLOPs(70B@2T) ≈ 8.4 × 10²³ FLOPs ⇒ D_13B ≈ (70/13)·2T ≈ 10.77T y D_7B ≈ 20T.
- Ancla alternativa en C = FLOPs(13B@2T) ≈ 1.56 × 10²³ ⇒ D_70B ≈ 0.371T.
- Aísla **el efecto de cómputo total de entrenamiento** manteniendo constante el presupuesto, atribuyendo así las diferencias a los parámetros.

Ambos contrastes se reportan en paralelo en §4; su triangulación permite atribución causal (decisión 2).

---

## 3. Controles y aleatorización

### 3.1 Controles de entrada (entre tamaños)

| Eje | Control | Cómo se aplica |
|---|---|---|
| Datos de pre-entrenamiento | Mismo corpus y mismo orden si se reentrena | Réplica exacta del recipe de Touvron et al. 2023 sobre el mismo snapshot (CommonCrawl + C4 + GitHub + ArXiv + Wikipedia filtrada) |
| Tokenizer | Mismo BPE LLaMA-2 (32k) | Congelado entre celdas |
| Pipeline de alineamiento | Mismo recipe SFT + RLHF de LLaMA-2-Chat | Mismos datos de SFT (~27k ejemplos de alta calidad, mismos hiperparámetros: 2 épocas, LR 1e-5, AdamW); mismo RLHF (5 epochs de PPO con reward model adversarial, ~1M preferencias) |
| Posición en GPU/cluster | Distribución aleatoria entre réplicas | Cuando hay ≥1 réplica de entrenamiento por celda, se baraja la asignación para evitar confounders térmicos/de entorno |

### 3.2 Controles de evaluación

| Eje | Control |
|---|---|
| Harness | `lm-evaluation-harness` (versión fijada en el pre-registro, ≥0.4.x) |
| Decodificación | Greedy (T=0) para MMLU, GSM8K (con chain-of-thought de 8-shot), ARC-c, BBH; muestreo T=0.7 / top-p 0.95 para MT-Bench y AlpacaEval |
| Prompt template | El publicado por Meta por variante (versión `meta-llama/llama-2/llama2-chat-config`); congelado |
| Pocas-shot | Congelado por benchmark (ver §4.2 tabla de métricas) |
| Orden de presentación | Aleatorio entre réplicas (semilla maestra por celda) |
| Juez LLM | Versión fijada (decisión 5 → solo LLM-as-judge); AlpacaEval con `gpt-4-1106-preview` o equivalente anclado y MT-Bench con GPT-4; debate de posición activado (intercambiar A↔B) para mitigar sesgo de orden |

### 3.3 Aleatorización

- **Semilla maestra** por celda; ≥3 semillas de decodificación por celda-benchmark para métricas con estocasticidad.
- **Sin semilla de entrenamiento** posible (los modelos liberados son single-run); esto se documenta como **amenaza interna a validez** (§7).

---

## 4. Métricas y pre-registro

### 4.1 Regla de no agregación cruzada

Las dimensiones **A** (capacidad bruta) y **B** (alineamiento) **nunca se agregan** en un único número. Se reportan siempre por separado, por benchmark y por celda. Cualquier media agregada dentro de A debe declarar el método (media aritmética, geométrica, o ranking) y mostrar resultados por benchmark.

### 4.2 Tabla de métricas y configuración

| Dim | Benchmark | Few-shot | Métrica reportada | Estilo de decodificación | Notas |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | MMLU | 5 | accuracy | greedy | 57 materias, agregadas y por materia |
| A | GSM8K | 8 (CoT) | accuracy exacta | greedy | Verificación de cadena de razonamiento |
| A | HumanEval | 0 | pass@1, pass@10 | greedy y muestreo | pass@1 con T=0; pass@10 con 10 muestras |
| A | BBH (BIG-Bench Hard) | 3 | accuracy | greedy | 23 tareas, reporte por tarea |
| A | ARC-Challenge | 25 | accuracy | greedy | Subset reto |
| B | MT-Bench | 0 | score 1–10, GPT-4 judge | T=0.7 / top-p 0.95 | Multi-turno, 8 categorías |
| B | IFEval | 0 | % instrucciones satisfechas | greedy | Métrica programática (no juez) |
| B | TruthfulQA | 0 | MC1 y MC2 | greedy | Verifica factualidad |
| B | AlpacaEval | 0 | win-rate vs `gpt-4-turbo` baseline | T=0.7 / top-p 0.9 | Longitud-controlada; juez anclado |

### 4.3 Pre-registro (elementos a congelar antes del primer acceso)

El documento de pre-registro (PDF firmado) fija:

1. Las hipótesis H0–H4 con su formulación exacta.
2. La lista y versión de los 9 benchmarks.
3. Harness y versión.
4. Plantilla de prompts y valores de few-shot.
5. Hiperparámetros de decodificación.
6. Número de semillas de decodificación (≥3) y semilla maestra.
7. Tamaño bootstrap (≥1000), método de corrección multiple (Holm-Bonferroni dentro de dimensión), α=0.05.
8. Reglas de parada y de exclusión post-hoc (qué se considera "fallo de hardware" vs "resultado válido").
9. Celdas excluidas a priori y motivo.

---

## 5. Plan de análisis estadístico

### 5.1 Bootstrap por celda-benchmark

Para cada celda *c* y benchmark *b*:

1. Calcular el score s_{c,b,i} para cada ejemplo *i* ∈ *b*.
2. *B* = 10 000 remuestreos con reemplazo sobre índices.
3. Para cada *b* se obtiene media(θ_b*) e IC95% por percentiles 2.5/97.5.

### 5.2 Comparaciones pareadas

Para cada par de celdas bajo contraste (p.ej. 13B-Chat@TE vs 70B-base@TE), definir:

- Para cada remuestreo: Δ_b* = s_{c₁,b}* − s_{c₂,b}*.
- IC95% del Δ e hipótesis nula H0:Δ:Δ_b = 0; rechazar si el IC no contiene el 0.

### 5.3 Corrección por comparaciones múltiples

- **Dentro de dimensión** (separada para A y B): Holm-Bonferroni sobre los 5 benchmarks de A y los 4 de B, manteniendo α_dimensión = 0.05.
- **Reportar también los p-valores no corregidos** para transparencia.

### 5.4 Semillas

- Para métricas con decodificación estocástica (MT-Bench, AlpacaEval, HumanEval pass@10): ≥3 semillas de decodificación; reportar media y dispersión inter-semilla.
- Para métricas greedy: semilla de decodificación irrelevante, pero se reporta igualmente para reproducibilidad.

### 5.5 Tablas de salida obligatorias

- **Tabla A**: para cada celda × benchmark A → media, IC95%, tamaño de muestra.
- **Tabla B**: análoga para dimensión B.
- **Tabla C**: Δ pareado por benchmark, IC95% e indicador Holm-significativo para los contrastes primarios.
- **Tabla D**: sub-análisis por sub-dominio donde el benchmark lo permita (p.ej. MMLU por materia, BBH por tarea, MT-Bench por categoría).

---

## 6. Criterios de éxito y refutación

### 6.1 Refutación de "más tamaño siempre mejora"

El claim H0 queda **refutado** si se observa **cualquiera** (con IC95% por bootstrap y corrección Holm intra-dimensión) de:

| ID | Condición de refutación | Hipótesis apoyada |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | ∃ b ∈ B: P(13B-Chat@TE)(b) > P(70B-base@TE)(b) | H2 — alineamiento refinado anula tamaño |
| R2 | ∃ b ∈ A: P(13B@2T)(b) > P(70B@1T)(b) | H1 — pre-entrenamiento insuficiente anula tamaño |
| R3 | En matched-FLOPs (celdas MF), la diferencia Δ_{70B−13B}(b) cae dentro de su IC95% en ≥3/5 benchmarks de A | H3 — escalado se aplana cuando cómputo se controla |

### 6.2 Caso de confirmación del claim (documentar siempre)

Si por el contrario se observa que **en ambos contrastes (TE y MF) y en ambas dimensiones**, 70B ≥ 13B en todos los benchmarks con Δ estadísticamente significativo en al menos 8/9 benchmarks, se documenta explícitamente como **H4 confirmada bajo las condiciones de este estudio**, junto con el tamaño de efecto y la advertencia de generalización limitada (familia LLaMA-2 sola, sin replicación de entrenamiento).

### 6.3 Predicciones cualitativas (no se pre-registran tamaños de efecto concretos)

- H1 esperada con fuerza moderada-alta — Chinchilla predice degradación al reducir tokens bajo el umbral óptimo.
- H2 esperada con fuerza alta — la literatura de alineación reporta brechas grandes en MT-Bench y AlpacaEval entre base y Chat.
- H3 esperada con fuerza moderada — el efecto "matched-FLOPs achata" tiene tanto soporte teórico (Chinchilla) como empírico (modelos pequeños entrenados largo tiempo pueden rivalizar con grandes menos entrenados), pero no se fija tamaño de efecto.
- H0 (siempre mejora) es la hipótesis nula operativa; su confirmación requiere evidencia estricta (condición §6.2). La simple ausencia de refutación **no** confirma H0 (asimetría: tres rutas de refutación vs una de confirmación exigente).

---

## 7. Limitaciones y amenazas a la validez

### 7.1 Amenazas internas
- **Sin replicación de entrenamiento.** Cada celda es un único run (los modelos liberados son single-shot). No podemos separar el ruido de entrenamiento del efecto tamaño; los IC95% reflejan solo varianza de decodificación y bootstrap sobre items.
- **Ausencia de SFT-only como nivel separado** del factor A (decisión 8 restringe a {base, Chat}). Esto impide desenredar el efecto aislado de SFT del RLHF.
- **Diversidad de datos de pre-entrenamiento no estratificada**: no se controla por composición temático-lingüística del corpus; es el mismo corpus Llama-2 para todas las celdas, lo que limita el control fino.

### 7.2 Amenazas externas
- **Familia única (LLaMA-2).** Decisión 3 restringe a esta familia para evitar confounders (Mistral, Qwen añaden tokenizer, datos, tamaño de vocab y recipe distintos). El claim H0 podría no generalizar fuera de LLaMA-2; se documenta como alcance limitado.
- **Sin evaluación humana** (decisión 5). MT-Bench y AlpacaEval con juez LLM capturan solo parcialmente calidad de respuesta y ayuda humana. **Limitación explícitamente declarada como amenaza a validez de constructo**.

### 7.3 Amenazas de constructo
- **LLM-as-judge tiene sesgos conocidos** (longitud, posición, formato). Mitigaciones: (a) longitud-controlada en AlpacaEval, (b) debate de posición (A↔B) en MT-Bench, (c) reportar juez anclado a versión fija.
- **IFEval es programática** (no juez); captura solo "instrucciones verificables" y deja fuera sutilezas semánticas.
- **Las dos dimensiones se definen operacionalmente por benchmark**, pero un benchmark (p.ej. MMLU) mezcla conocimiento y razonamiento. Esta mezcla se asume aceptable dados los estándares de la literatura; no se descompone.

### 7.4 Amenazas estadísticas
- **Múltiples comparaciones × múltiples semillas**: controladas con Holm intra-dimensión.
- **Tamaño bootstrap (10 000)** puede sub-dimensionar IC cuando las distribuciones son bimodales (poco común en accuracy pero posible en pass@k); se verifica visual-mediante histogramas de Δ_b* y se reporta si aparecen.
- **Sin corrección跨-dimensión**: A y B se reportan independientemente; cualquier afirmación combinada ("70B mejora en ambas dimensiones") exige que ambas componentes pasen sus propios Holm-α, no se promedian p-valores.

---

## 8. Feasibility

### 8.1 Estimación de cómputo

Sustento: training FLOPs ≈ 6 · N · D_tokens (forward+backward, factor 6 sobre forward; estándar de Kaplan et al., Hoffmann et al.). Rendimiento sostenido asumido: **~150 TFLOPS/A100 en BF16** para entrenamientos LLM densos (estimación conservadora de práctica pública; ver Fedus et al., Narayanan et al.).

| Escenario | FLOPs | GPU-hours A100 | A100-días | Coste nube aprox. ($2/A100-h) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reentrenar 70B @ 2T | 8.4 × 10²³ | ~1.56 × 10⁶ | ~64 800 | ~$3.1M |
| Reentrenar 70B @ 1T (IS) | 4.2 × 10²³ | ~7.8 × 10⁵ | ~32 400 | ~$1.6M |
| Reentrenar 70B @ 1.4T (Chinchilla) | 5.9 × 10²³ | ~1.09 × 10⁶ | ~45 400 | ~$2.2M |
| Reentrenar 70B @ 0.371T (MF bajo) | 1.56 × 10²³ | ~2.9 × 10⁵ | ~12 070 | ~$580k |
| **Coste incremental celdas IS (7+8)** | — | **~7.8 × 10⁵ GPU-h** | **~32 400 A100-días** | **~$1.6M** |
| Inferir LLaMA-2 70B sobre los 9 benchmarks (greedy + muestreo ×3) | — | ~50–150 GPU-h total | — | <$300 |

> **Recomendación pragmática con presupuesto limitado:** ejecutar C1 (TE) con las 6 celdas liberadas (coste ~$1k–$10k de inferencia) cubre R1 y permite verificar H2 sin reentrenar nada. Las celdas IS (R2) y MF (R3) son extensiones que dependen de acceso a clúster grande o acuerdos de cómputo con terceros.

### 8.2 Datos y checkpoints

- **Checkpoints:** las 6 celdas de §2.2 requieren acceso a `meta-llama/Llama-2-{7b,13b,70b}{,-chat}-hf` (licencia Meta LLaMA-2 Community License; gate de acceso vía Hugging Face).
- **Datos de reentrenamiento:** mismos snapshots que LLaMA-2 original (CommonCrawl + C4 + GitHub + ArXiv + Wikipedia + Books). SFT datos: ~27k ejemplos sintéticos/curados de Meta. RLHF: ~1M comparaciones de preferencia (Meta, no público; alternativa: HH-RLHF de Anthropic con advertencia de divergencia).
- **Modelo juez (LLM-as-judge):** GPT-4 Turbo fijo por versión; presupuesto independiente (~$500–$2 000 por pasada completa de AlpacaEval + MT-Bench).

### 8.3 Almacenamiento

| Modelo | Tamaño en disco (BF16) |
|---|---|
| 7B | ~14 GB |
| 13B | ~26 GB |
| 70B | ~140 GB |
| Reward model 70B (adicional para celdas Chat reentrenadas) | ~140 GB |
| Checkpoints intermedios + activaciones | +500 GB–2 TB por job |

### 8.4 Software

- `transformers` ≥ 4.40 (snapshot fijado en pre-registro).
- `lm-evaluation-harness` ≥ 0.4.x.
- `alpaca_eval` ≥ 0.5.x con `alpaca_eval_gpt4_turbo_fn` como anclaje.
- `fastchat`/`MT-Bench` ≥ 0.2.x para MT-Bench con GPT-4 judge.
- `trl` o `trlx` para SFT/RLHF si se reentrena (versiones ancladas).
- `vLLM` o `text-generation-inference` para inferencia eficiente en evaluaciones.
- Scripts propios: bootstrap (numpy/scipy), Holm (statsmodels), generación de tablas.

### 8.5 Coste humano-asistido

El coordinador humano debe validar manualmente ~5–10% de las salidas del juez LLM para auditoría de sesgos de longitud/posición (coste: ~$500–$1 000 en anotación a tarifa estándar).

---

## 9. Salidas del estudio y presentación

- **Documento principal** con Tablas A–D y un gráfico por dimensión mostrando el IC95% de cada celda por benchmark, con ordenación por tamaño.
- **Apéndice estadístico** con histogramas de Δ_b* y p-valores corregidos/no-corregidos.
- **Declaración de fidelidad al pre-registro**, listando cualquier desviación (p.ej. celdas excluidas por fallo de entrenamiento, semilla cambiada por bug).
- **Documento de extrapolación** que discute hasta qué punto H0 puede generalizarse a otras familias y a otros regímenes de optimización (AdamW → Lion; FP16 → BF16 vs FP8).

---

## 10. Decisiones cerradas (rastro de auditoría)

| # | Decisión | Resuelta como |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Tamaño 7B incluido | Sí (ancla informativa; contraste primario sigue siendo 13B↔70B) |
| 2 | Dos contrastes paralelos | TE (tokens iguales) y MF (matched-FLOPs) en paralelo |
| 3 | Familia única | LLaMA-2 exclusivamente |
| 4 | Métricas | A = {MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval, BBH, ARC-c}; B = {MT-Bench, IFEval, TruthfulQA, AlpacaEval (LLM-judge)} |
| 5 | Evaluación humana | Fuera; limitación documentada |
| 6 | Criterio de refutación | R1 ∨ R2 ∨ R3 según tabla §6.1; H4 confirmada según §6.2 |
| 7 | Análisis | Bootstrap 10 000 + ≥3 semillas + Holm intra-dim + lm-eval-harness |
| 8 | Operacionalizaciones | IS=70B@1T; estándar=2T; Chinchilla ~20·N; alineado=SFT+RLHF LLaMA-2 Chat |
| 9 | Feasibility | Cómputo estimado en §8.1; sandbox no ejecuta nada por diseño |

---

**Resultado entregable:** este documento. **No se ejecuta ningún experimento en el sandbox.** El diseño queda listo para que un equipo con acceso a clúster A100/H100 y a los checkpoints de Meta lo ejecute siguiendo el pre-registro de §4.3 y las reglas de parada de §6.

payload.answer:
### Proposed approach (initial; awaiting researcher approval)

**Core question, decomposed into two testable mechanisms**
- **M1 — Insufficient pre-training**: A larger model trained on the same token budget / with the same schedule as a smaller one may be under-fit, so its capability on knowledge/reasoning proxies may under-deliver its parameter count.
- **M2 — Insufficient alignment refinement**: Post-training (SFT + RLHF) quality has not kept up with scale, so instruction-following / truthfulness / safety metrics may plateau or reverse for the largest model.

To isolate M1 from M2, we use a **crossed matrix** rather than a 70B↔13B one-shot:

| Axis | Levels |
|---|---|
| Size | 7B, 13B, 70B |
| Pre-training generation (data scale) | Llama-1 (≈1.4T tokens) vs Llama-2 (≈2T tokens) |
| Post-training | base (no RLHF) vs -chat (SFT + RLHF) |

This gives seven canonical checkpoints (Llama-1-{7B,13B,65B}; Llama-2-{7B,13B,70B}-base; Llama-2-{7B,13B,70B}-chat). Each model is evaluated on the *same* benchmark suite using an *identical* pipeline.

**Benchmark battery, mapped to the two mechanisms**

- *Pre-training-sufficiency probes (M1):* MMLU (5-shot), ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA, TriviaQA (reading comprehension subset), GSM8K, BIG-Bench Hard.
- *Alignment-quality probes (M2):* TruthfulQA (MC1/MC2, generation), IFEval, MT-Bench, AlpacaEval, ToxiGen / HarmBench refusal rate.
- *Code (a known non-monotonic case in the Llama-2 paper):* HumanEval pass@1, with controlled sample count.
- *Reasoning under chain-of-thought:* GSM8K CoT vs direct-answer split to separate knowledge from reasoning depth.

**Evaluation pipeline specifications**

- Harness: `lm-evaluation-harness` for capability/knowledge, plus a fixed chat template (the official Llama-2 system prompt) for all -chat runs.
- Decoding: capability tasks at temperature=0, fixed max_new_tokens; chat tasks at the protocol's default nucleus settings (documented) with the same temperature across model sizes, so gains cannot be attributed to inference-compute drift.
- Paired-prompt evaluation: every model receives the identical prompt list, so significance uses paired bootstrap (n=1000 resamples) or a paired permutation test rather than independent-samples CIs.
- Sample size: ≥350 items per benchmark with bootstrap CIs reported; pass@1 with k=20 generations per HumanEval item, fraction aggregation as in Chen et al.

**Falsification criteria (what we will judge evidence against)**

- H0 (size-monotonic): capability/knowledge scores are strictly monotone in size for Llama-2-base; chat quality is strictly monotone for Llama-2-chat.
- H_M1: At least one pre-training-proxy benchmark where Llama-2-70B-base is within 1σ of Llama-2-13B-base **and** Llama-1-65B-base trails Llama-2-13B-base, while both beat their Llama-1 size counterparts → supports pre-training insufficiency at 70B.
- H_M2: At least one alignment benchmark where Llama-2-70B-chat under-performs Llama-2-13B-chat (the paper documents this for HumanEval-style coding and for certain TruthfulQA cells), **and** base-truthful > chat-truthful gap is non-monotone in size → supports alignment-refinement deficit.

**Consequential choices I would ask the researcher to confirm**

1. Scope: restrict models to the Llama family, or admit a third-axis "external baseline" (e.g., Mistral-7B, Qwen-14B) to test transferability?
2. Whether to include Llama-1 in the matrix, or simplify to a Llama-2-only design (cleaner but cannot fully isolate M1 from M2).
3. Whether human evaluation on a small subset (e.g., MT-Bench re-grading with annotators) is in or out of scope — affects the protocol substantially.
4. Whether to fold in an explicit "pre-training tokens" ablation (e.g., Llama-1 1.4T token corpus runs at 70B scale) as a hypothetical branch, even though that checkpoint is not released; if yes, we would specify the design but disclaim it cannot be run.
5. Reporting cadence: per-benchmark tables + a summary "score-card" plot, and whether to include effect sizes (Cohen's d) alongside CIs.

**What I will NOT do in this design**

- Will not invent execution logs, runtime numbers, or reported accuracies.
- Will not import external data into the workspace (network is disabled).
- Will not fabricate Llama-2-70B internally unavailable checkpoints as if they had been evaluated.

Awaiting explicit researcher approval before I draft the full design specification (stage=result).

# Experiment Design: Is Llama-2-70B Better than Llama-2-13B? — A Falsification Rubric for the Two-Mechanism Hypothesis

**Status.** Design-only specification. No execution. No invented benchmark numbers.

**Primary source for evidence targets.** Touvron et al., *Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models*, arXiv:2307.09288v2, July 2023 (referred to below as "Llama 2 paper"). Meta's model card adds detail on RLHF procedure and chat templates. Where the design points at an empirical pattern, the table number in the Llama 2 paper is given so the reader can verify the cited number rather than trust it on the design file alone.

---

## 1. Research question

Does scaling parameter count from Llama-2-13B to Llama-2-70B yield uniformly better task performance, or can either or both of two non-size mechanisms cancel or reverse the benefit?

- **M1 — Insufficient pre-training ratio.** The 70B was pre-trained on the same token budget and schedule as the smaller Llama-2 checkpoints (≈2T tokens, see paper §2.1). Per Chinchilla-style scaling, a larger model given a fixed token budget can be under-fit relative to a smaller model that has a higher parameter-to-token ratio.
- **M2 — Insufficient refined alignment.** Post-training (SFT + two RM RLHF, see paper §3) was not necessarily scaled in compute or iteration depth to match the size jump, so instruction-following, truthfulness, and safety metrics can stagnate or invert.

The question is *not* "is 70B better on average?" The Llama 2 paper documents that on aggregate capability benchmarks it is. The question is whether *systematic, mechanism-isolated* instabilities exist that may negate the benefit on specific benchmark families.

---

## 2. Model checkpoints under test

A 3 × 2 matrix of Meta-released checkpoints — six conditions, identical tokenizer family (`LlamaTokenizer`, with reserved special tokens for chat):

| Condition | Size | Variant | Local identifier | Documented cards |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | 7B | base | `meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf` | paper §2 |
| C2 | 13B | base | `meta-llama/Llama-2-13b-hf` | paper §2 |
| C3 | 70B | base | `meta-llama/Llama-2-70b-hf` | paper §2 |
| C4 | 7B | chat | `meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-chat-hf` | paper §3 |
| C5 | 13B | chat | `meta-llama/Llama-2-13b-chat-hf` | paper §3 |
| C6 | 70B | chat | `meta-llama/Llama-2-70b-chat-hf` | paper §3 |

**Why six rather than two.** A bare 70B-vs-13B comparison cannot separate M1 from M2: a regression in 70B-chat could come from either mechanism. The 70B-base row is the cleanest *M1 probe* (no RLHF contamination). The -chat-vs-base contrast at fixed size is the cleanest *M2 probe* for that size.

**Explicitly out of scope (per the focused-scope decision):**
- Llama-1 checkpoints → no cross-generation pre-training token-budget comparison inside this design.
- Cross-family baselines (Mistral, Qwen, Yi) → not used here; the matrix stays self-contained inside Meta's Llama 2 release.
- Human re-evaluations of chat outputs → automated metrics only.

---

## 3. Benchmark battery

Every benchmark is evaluated on every condition. The mapping below justifies why each benchmark is informative for M1, M2, or both. Where the Llama 2 paper already reports a relevant result for any of these cells, that table reference is given.

### 3.1 Pre-training-sufficiency probes (M1)
These primarily test world-knowledge / reasoning capacity, expected to track with size *if* pre-training tokens are sufficient.

- **MMLU** (Hendrycks et al., 5-shot, all 57 subjects; paper Table 6). Standard capability skill-mix.
- **ARC-Challenge** (25-shot, paper Table 7 region). Science reasoning.
- **HellaSwag** (10-shot, paper Table 7 region). Commonsense completion.
- **PIQA** (10-shot, paper Table 7 region). Physical reasoning.
- **TriviaQA** (5-shot, reading-comprehension subset). Recall of pre-training-distributed facts.
- **GSM8K** (8-shot CoT, paper Table 6). Grade-school multi-step math.
- **BIG-Bench Hard** (CoT, 23 tasks, paper Table 7 region). Compositional reasoning.

### 3.2 Alignment-quality probes (M2)
These predominantly measure post-training refinement. M1 contributes only loosely (knowledge feeds them).

- **TruthfulQA** — both MC1 and MC2, plus *generation* mode (paper Table 17 region). The paper documents that Truthfulness-Info, MC2 of larger chat models trends below the 13B chat (see paper §6 for the qualitative discussion and Table 17 for cells). This cell is the strongest pre-registered non-monotonic alert.
- **IFEval** ("Instruction Following Evaluation", 0-shot, prompted). Objective verifiable instruction format adherence.
- **MT-Bench** (80-question 4-turn chat benchmark, GPT-4-as-judge). Subjective but standard.
- **AlpacaEval** (length-controlled win rate). Chat quality.
- **ToxiGen** (refusal + non-toxic-generation rate, 0-shot). Toxicity avoidance.
- **HarmBench** (functional refusal on adversarial attack prompts). Safety robustness.

### 3.3 Code (a known non-monotonic case)
- **HumanEval pass@1**, 1-shot, k=20 generations per item, temperature fixed at 0.2, top-p=0.95, matches the paper's reported setting (paper Table 6). Code is an interesting intermediate case — knowledge-driven but also sensitive to RLHF (paper's chat models show surprisingly muted HumanEval gains given their size jump).

---

## 4. Evaluation protocol

### 4.1 Harness
- `lm-evaluation-harness` (EleutherAI, version pin in a future execution). Per-paper-pinned revision when the design transitions to execution; here we mark the constraint.
- For chat-style benchmarks we run the harness in chat-completion mode using the *Llama-2 official system prompt* (paper Appendix A) for every C4–C6 evaluation, so differences are not attributable to system-prompt tuning.

### 4.2 Decoding
- **Capability / MCQ benchmarks:** temperature = 0, greedy, max_new_tokens fixed to the harness default for that benchmark. This removes sampling noise and keeps paired-prompt differences interpretable.
- **Generation benchmarks (TruthfulQA-gen, HumanEval generations, MT-Bench, AlpacaEval):** sampling with `temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9, max_new_tokens=512` for chat; `temperature=0.0` for base models on TruthfulQA-gen to mirror paper §6 setting. These values are documented and held constant across sizes, so any model-size effect is not confounded with sampling temperature drift.
- For HumanEval pass@1, the paper's documented setting of `temperature=0.2, top_p=0.95, k=20` is used exactly so that our numbers are comparable to paper Table 6.

### 4.3 Prompt parity
- Each model receives the *identical* prompt list per benchmark. This makes paired statistical tests well-defined.
- Few-shot exemplars are taken from the harness's standard exemplars (no per-model tuning). This deliberately neutralizes a confounding axis (exemplar optimization).
- Chat templates: official `/sys/[/INST]...[/INST]` format for Llama-2-chat; raw text for base models.

### 4.4 Inference infrastructure parity
- Single H100 (or A100 80GB; documented and held constant) per run.
- `batch_size=1` to avoid batch-induced answer-confabulation artifacts reported in the literature; no dynamic batching that changes answer order.
- Same tokenizer, same chat-format post-processor.

---

## 5. Controls and confounders

| Confounder | Control |
|---|---|
| Sampling stochasticity | Greedy where possible; fixed-seed sampling elsewhere; pass@1 with k≥20 for stability on code |
| Inference compute | Fixed max_new_tokens; identical system prompt |
| Heterogeneous templates | Same official Llama-2 chat template |
| Benchmark contamination | Pre-registered: contamination is acknowledged as an external-validity limit (§8); we do not claim to rule it out |
| Few-shot exemplar sensitivity | Same exemplars across all models |
| Multiple runs | Capability/MCQ: 1 run (deterministic). Generation: 3 seeds, mean reported |
| Order effects | Per benchmark, evaluation order over conditions is randomized once and reused |
| Hardware numerical differences | All quantized model variants excluded unless paper-canonical; comparison limited to fp16 |

---

## 6. Statistical analysis plan

### 6.1 Inference
For each benchmark cell (model, benchmark):
- *MCQ:* accuracy with **non-parametric bootstrap 95 % CI**, n=1000 resamples, percentile method. For TruthfulQA-MC1, n is the full MC1 set; for IFEval, n=541 (the prompt set's full size).
- *Generation (TruthfulQA-gen, HumanEval, MT-Bench, AlpacaEval):* **mean over 3 seeds**, with bootstrap CI over items.

### 6.2 Cross-model comparison
Since each model sees the same item list inside a benchmark, comparison rows are *paired*. Specifically defined contrasts:

1. *Scale contrast at fixed alignment state:* C3 vs C2 (base) on M1-probes; C6 vs C5 (chat) on M2-probes; C1 vs C2, C2 vs C3 for additional monotone check.
2. *Alignment contrast at fixed size:* C5 vs C2, C6 vs C3 on M2-probes (how much did RLHF help, per size).
3. *Cross-size alignment efficiency:* (C5−C2) vs (C6−C3) — does RLHF lift diminish at 70B?

Statistical tests on each contrast:
- **Paired bootstrap difference** at 10^4 resamples, reporting the 95 % CI on the *mean* paired difference.
- **Wilcoxon signed-rank test** as a non-parametric paired secondary; p-values *not* used in isolation, only to crown CI results that already straddle zero.
- **Effect size:** Cohen's *d* on paired differences, reported alongside CIs.
- Bonferroni is not applied across the multiple benchmark family because the design endpoint is the falsification rubric (§7), not a single omnibus test. CIs are not reinterpreted via threshold after the fact.

### 6.3 Pre-registration of analysis decisions
The following are recorded to make the analysis honest:
- A 70B-chat under-performance on any single benchmark does not alone confirm M2; the rubric requires the directional pattern in §7.
- "Improvement" = a non-overlap of bootstrap CIs *or* a Cohen's d ≥ 0.2 in the expected direction with consistent Wilcoxon p < 0.01. Plain-across-numerically-larger-on-every-benchmark does not satisfy this design, and the rubric already encodes it.
- Neither CIs nor p-values are reported if the metric has fewer than 100 items; such benchmarks are reported but excluded from falsification judgments with that limitation noted.

---

## 7. Falsification rubric (the only results-adjudication section in this document)

This rubric is the *terminus* of the design; we describe how the evidence under M1 / M2 would be evaluated, *not* what we expect.

**H0 — strict size-monotonic.** Rejected if at least one of these directional patterns appears with the §6 criteria met (≥ 0.2 Cohen's d or non-overlap of paired bootstrap CIs, with consistent Wilcoxon):

- R1. On any §3.1 benchmark, C3 < C2 with the strain going *beyond* sampling noise.
- R2. On any §3.2 benchmark, C6 < C5 with the strain going beyond sampling noise.

**M1 evidence pattern (insufficient pre-training ratio).** Both:
- R3. At fixed alignment "base," C2 and C3 are statistically tied on at least two §3.1 benchmarks (e.g., MMLU, ARC-C), and C3 is NOT strictly better on at least one of those two by Cohen's d ≥ 0.2.
- R4. The capability gain from C1→C2 is comparable to or larger than the gain from C2→C3 across the §3.1 benchmarks, suggesting diminishing returns at 70B consistent with a fixed token budget (capacity not fully used).
- Optional supporting: any cross-section difference between base and chat at 70B (C6−C3) is smaller in magnitude than at 13B (C5−C2), consistent with 70B-base having more headroom but not using it for general capability.

**M2 evidence pattern (insufficient refined alignment).** Both:
- R5. At fixed base, C3 ≥ C2 on §3.1 (capability is monotonic or tied), but on §3.2 the C6 ranking on at least one alignment probe inverts or ties relative to C5 — i.e., the gap (C6−C5) is non-positive on a TruthfulQA cell, IFEval, AlpacaEval rating, or MT-Bench score, with paired-bootstrap support.
- R6. The base-to-chat gain on §3.2 that is large at 7B and 13B (ΔC5−C2) shrinks or disappears at 70B (ΔC6−C3), indicating post-training refinement is not keeping pace with capacity.

**Joint verdict logic.**
- H0 holds only if neither R1 nor R2 fires.
- M1 holds *independently* if R3 and R4 hold.
- M2 holds *independently* if R5 and R6 hold.
- Both can hold simultaneously (the question allows it): the rubric concludes "yes, both mechanisms are operative and the size gain is conditional on alignment quality for alignment-driven metrics, on token budget for knowledge metrics."

This section does not predict which verdict will fire.

---

## 8. Threats to validity and scope limits

- **Construct validity of "refined alignment."** We operationalize "refined alignment" as the M2×2×M2 outcome on command-of-instruction benchmarks, not as a HIDDEN dimension we measure directly. The rubric does not claim to *measure* RLHF quality — it claims to detect *non-monotone outcome trends* consistent with the M2 mechanism being live.
- **Internal validity — benchmark contamination.** The Llama-2 training corpus is not fully public. We do not claim to rule out contamination. We rely on the fact that *non-monotonic* patterns are harder to explain by memorization than by a training-quality mechanism.
- **Internal validity — paired inference.** Same GPU, same batch=1, no dynamic batching; we acknowledge that 70B with batch=1 increases wall-time but does not affect deterministic decoding outputs.
- **External validity.** Six conditions; generalizing beyond Llama-2 requires separate runs. Cross-family baselines were deferred per scope. We do not claim transferability.
- **Construct — what "size" means.** The design fixes *parameter count* as the operationalization of "size." It does not isolate *inference-time compute* (FLOPs per token), which increases with size. Pre-registered: any 70B advantage on tasks with extended reasoning chains is not attributed to parameter count alone.
- **Selection of benchmarks.** Battery is non-exhaustive. Coding, math, reasoning, knowledge, instruction-following, truthfulness, safety are mapped; we do not add agentic, multimodal, or long-context benchmarks.

---

## 9. Out-of-scope clauses

Per the focus instruction:
- **No promise of an "expected results" or "predicted outcomes" section** beyond the falsification rubric in §7.
- **No second deliverable.** This document is the only artifact.
- **No runtime, wall-clock, GPU-cost, or dataset-mass numbers.** Such numbers would have to come from the executed protocol and are therefore not part of a design-only specification.
- **No cross-family baselines, no Llama-1 cells, no human evaluation** (decisions absorbed into the scalar matrix in §2).
- **No execution.** No code is written, no benchmarks are run, no checkpoint is downloaded. The `task.documents.track.md` ("Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required") is honored.

---

## 10. Compact list of design commitments (auditable)

- **6 conditions** in a 3 × 2 (size × alignment) matrix, all Meta-released Llama-2 checkpoints.
- **Single benchmark suite** applied uniformly; benchmarks mapped to M1 / M2 probes.
- **Single protocol** with greedy decoding for MCQ and fixed-temperature sampling for generation; system prompt and chat template held constant across sizes.
- **Single statistical plan**: paired bootstrap CIs + Wilcoxon + Cohen's d, no Bonferroni adaptation of CI thresholds.
- **Single falsification rubric**: H0 vs M1 vs M2, each requiring multiple bar-fired patterns, not a single-cell drop.
- **Single document**: this file. No second document, no execution script, no run log.

— end of specification —

## Plan: Scale × Pretraining × Alignment ablation around Llama-2

### 1. Inspection of supplied inputs

- `/workspace` contains only `task.json`. The `documents.track.md` field is a one-line pointer ("Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required.") rather than a real on-disk document. No datasets, code, weights, or environment hints are present.
- Environment: Python 3.12, 24 vCPU, 125 GiB RAM, no GPU (`nvidia-smi` not available), no network — consistent with a design-only deliverable. I will not attempt to fetch weights or run models.
- Constraint implication: every claim in the design must be defensible from published Llama-2 / Llama-2-Chat technical reports, scaling-law literature, and third-party evaluation papers, not from local execution.

### 2. Proposed approach (high level)

A 3-way factorial ablation that crosses model size, pretraining sufficiency, and alignment tier, with downstream evaluation on capability, alignment-sensitive, and safety benchmarks. The headline comparison the question asks about — 70B vs. 13B — is decomposed as:

| | Aligned (full RLHF) | Under-aligned (no RLHF) |
|--|--|--|
| Fully pretrained (full token budget) | Llama-2-70B-Chat vs. Llama-2-13B-Chat (and -7B-Chat, -34B-Chat if available) | Llama-2-70B base vs. Llama-2-13B base |
| Insufficiently pretrained | Undertrained chat variant (or proxy) | Undertrained base variant |

Candidate model set M:
- Llama-2-7B, Llama-2-13B, Llama-2-70B base (full ~2T-token pretraining).
- Llama-2-7B-Chat, Llama-2-13B-Chat, Llama-2-70B-Chat (full SFT + RLHF).
- "Insufficient pretraining" baseline: a publicly reported undertrained checkpoint at one model size (a known fraction of the published token budget) or a Chinchilla-style ablation point at the 13B/70B scale.
- "No refined alignment" baseline: the base model (pre-SFT and pre-RLHF). Optionally an SFT-only / early-instruct checkpoint if released.
- Optional additions if accessible: CodeLlama variants at matched scales (different pretraining mix, similar size) as a second pretraining-tier data point.

Controlled variables (identical across cells):
- Tokenizer (Llama-2 SentencePiece BPE), context length (4096), vocabulary.
- Decoding: temperature = 0 (greedy) for capability benchmarks; fixed temperature with 5-seed sampling for generative variance estimates; identical top-p, repetition penalty, max-new-tokens.
- Prompt template: the exact same official Llama-2-Chat "[INST] <<SYS>>…" template, no ad-hoc rewording; the system block is stripped for fair base-model comparison.
- Quantization: identical precision across models (bf16 if hardware permits; otherwise int4 with the same GPTQ/AWQ recipe).
- Batch composition and in-context exemplar counts (zero vs. few-shot) held fixed per benchmark.
- Same evaluation harness (e.g., lm-eval-harness, version pinned), same scorer, same prompt order.

Independent variables (3-way factorial):
- IV-1 Scale: {7B, 13B, 70B} (and 34B if available).
- IV-2 Pretraining sufficiency: {full budget, truncated budget or compute-matched smaller}.
- IV-3 Alignment tier: {base, SFT-only if available, full chat (SFT+RLHF)}.

Dependent variables:
- Capability (respond to scale and pretraining): MMLU 5-shot, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, TruthfulQA-MC, GSM8K 8-shot EM, HumanEval pass@1 / pass@10 (5 seeds), BIG-Bench-Hard subset.
- Reasoning ceilings: MATH 4-shot, BBH.
- Long-context (the 70B advantage lever): needle-in-a-haystack, scrolls QA at 4096.
- Alignment-sensitive (should respond to RLHF, not scale alone): AlpacaEval-2 / MT-Bench win-rate against a fixed reference, IFEval, AgentBench-lite if feasible.
- Safety / refusal proxies: BBQ, ToxiGen, HarmBench; refusal rate on adversarial prompts; TruthfulQA-generation split.
- Calibration / hallucination proxies: token-level NLL, ECE on MC, expected calibration error on GSM8K sampled-trace agreement.
- Human-eval subset: 200-prompt double-blind A/B on alignment-relevant categories, at least 3 annotators each, Krippendorff alpha at least 0.7.

Evaluation suite: lm-eval-harness (deterministic capability/hallucination), a generation harness (AlpacaEval, IFEval) for alignment DVs, a human-eval subset for tightly alignment-relevant judgments, and a calibration module. All raw generations and scores are versioned so reruns are reproducible.

Analysis plan:
1. Scaling-law ablation. Fit a piecewise log-log curve of capability vs. parameters at fixed pretraining tier. Compare slopes for base and chat families to check whether the marginal return of scaling is preserved after alignment is layered on.
2. Alignment-vs-scale decomposition. For each (size, pretrain-tier) cell, compute Delta_alignment = score_chat - score_base. Test whether 70B-Chat retains the alignment gap of 13B-Chat; if Delta_alignment collapses or inverts at 70B with truncated pretraining, this directly attributes the outcome to refined alignment doing real work.
3. Ceiling/floor effects. Flag benchmarks where base-70B and chat-70B are statistically indistinguishable from a dataset ceiling (e.g., saturated MMLU); a non-result there is not misread as alignment failing.
4. Confound checks. (a) Decoding sensitivity: rerun GSM8K and MT-Bench at 3 temperatures; (b) prompt-template sensitivity: rerun with the alternative official template; (c) precision sensitivity: rerun a 70B cell in bf16 vs. int4 to quantify quantization drift that can erase small alignment gains.
5. Confound on insufficient pretraining itself. A truncated-token run and a compute-matched smaller model are not the same confound (Assumption A3). Report both contrasts: same params but fewer tokens; same FLOPs but smaller params. If they diverge, the conclusion is qualified accordingly.
6. Power and minimum detectable effect. With n prompts per benchmark and paired comparisons, report the smallest Delta rejected at alpha=0.05 with power=0.8; smaller effects are not claimed as significant.
7. Pre-registered decision rule for the headline question: 70B >= 13B is "not necessary" if (i) the simple effect of scale is non-significant or negative on at least 2 of {MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval} after multiple-comparison correction, AND (ii) the alignment gap at 70B is at most the alignment gap at 13B on at least 2 of {AlpacaEval, IFEval, safety proxy}.

Feasibility assessment:
- Checkpoints: Llama-2 7B/13B/70B (base and chat) are public. Undertrained/partially-trained checkpoints are the weak link — see Uncertainty U1.
- Compute (outside this sandbox): bf16 70B inference on the full eval suite is on the order of 2 A100-80GB-weeks per pass; int4 GPTQ cuts that roughly 3-4x. Total program including 5-seed reruns and ablations is on the order of 100-200 A100-80GB-days.
- Datasets/evals: MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval, BBH, AlpacaEval, MT-Bench, IFEval, BBQ, TruthfulQA, HarmBench — all public, version-pinned.
- Human eval: 200 prompts x 5 cells x 3 raters is roughly 3,000 ratings; realistic with a small annotator pool.
- Sandbox limitation (this environment): cannot run any of the above. Numbers in the final design will be cited from published sources or marked "to be measured".

### 3. Consequential assumptions and uncertainties — for your confirmation

Assumptions I am proposing (defaults unless you override):
- A1. Llama-2 family only (7B/13B/70B, base and chat); no third-party models.
- A2. "Refined alignment" = Llama-2-Chat's full recipe (SFT + iterative RLHF + rejection sampling). SFT-only models are a secondary contrast, not the primary "no refined alignment" baseline.
- A3. "Insufficient pretraining" operationalized along two axes, both reported: (a) same architecture truncated token budget (e.g., 0.5T of 2T tokens — published scaling-law points or released checkpoints where available); (b) compute-matched smaller model trained longer (Chinchilla-style reallocation where the 70B/13B budget would have been better spent on a smaller longer-trained model).
- A4. Comparisons at fixed inference FLOPs per generated token, not fixed wall-clock, so quantization/decoding differences do not masquerade as scale effects.
- A5. Primary alignment detectors at frontier scale: AlpacaEval-2 win-rate, IFEval, refusal-harm tradeoff metrics. MMLU/GSM8K/HumanEval are capability sanity checks only.
- A6. Headline claim "70B >= 13B is not necessary" is a pre-registered statistical rule combining capability non-improvement and alignment-gap collapse at 70B.

Uncertainties to resolve before I produce the full design:
- U1. Are partially-trained Llama-2 checkpoints publicly available, or must insufficient-pretraining be approximated only via Chinchilla-style reallocations or third-party reproductions? This determines whether the design is purely observational or partially experimental.
- U2. Is safety a positive component of the alignment DV (i.e., reward a chat variant's increase in refusal-while-helpful on a help-harm tradeoff curve), or a separate DV family? Llama-2 reports both; the framing changes the decision rule.
- U3. Are comparisons at fixed inference FLOPs (Assumption A4) or at "list-price" precision (each model served at its recommended precision)? This is where most "is bigger better?" debates collapse.
- U4. Include Llama-3 as a reference point for positioning, or restrict strictly to Llama-2?
- U5. Quantization: bf16-only or int4 acceptable? Int4 makes 70B feasible on commodity hardware but introduces a roughly 1-2 point alignment-sensitivity confound.
- U6. Should the human-eval subset be in scope, or restrict to automatic benchmarks only?

Once you confirm or adjust A1-A6 and answer U1-U6 (or tell me to proceed with my proposed defaults), I will produce the full design: complete experiment matrix, evaluation harness, scoring protocol, statistical analysis plan, and feasibility table, supported by source-cited rationale and the repository observations above.

# Full Experiment Design -- Scale x Pretraining x Alignment Around Llama-2

**Status:** Design-only. No experiment is run in this sandbox. `/workspace` contains only `task.json`; no GPU, no network, no checkpoints, no datasets on disk. All numbers are TBM (to be measured) or cited from published reports with stable identifiers. The pre-registration artifact (decision rule, MDE, prompt packs) is the deliverable.

**Lock-ins from the approval round:** A1 Llama-2 only (7/13/70 primary; 34B as published-trajectory data point), A2 refined alignment equals Llama-2-Chat full recipe (SFT + iterative RLHF + rejection sampling), A3 insufficient pretraining reported on two legs (3a token-truncated; 3b compute-matched smaller), A4 fixed inference FLOPs per token for primary; bf16-vs-int4 as confound annex, A5 AlpacaEval-2, IFEval, and help-harm AUC are the primary alignment detectors, A6 pre-registered headline rule tightened to Holm-corrected non-improvement on >=2 of 4 capability benchmarks AND Delta_alignment token at most 50 percent of Delta_alignment at 13B with bootstrap CI on >=2 of 3 alignment metrics. U2 safety reported both as combined help-harm AUC and per-benchmark scores. U4 Llama-3 is framing only. U5 bf16 primary with one bf16-vs-int4 confound cell. U6 ~200-prompt human-eval subset in scope, lightweight execution optional.

---

## (i) Complete Experiment Matrix

Notation: a cell is written as (size | pretrain-tier | alignment-tier). Each cell carries a checkpoint identifier (Hugging Face Hub org/repo with rev) and a data-source tag distinguishing loadable checkpoints from publication-only trajectories.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| C-13B-FULL-BASE | 13B | Full budget (2T tok) | Base | `meta-llama/Llama-2-13b-hf` (rev main) | arXiv:2307.09288 sec 2.1, Table 1 |
| C-70B-FULL-BASE | 70B | Full budget (2T tok) | Base | `meta-llama/Llama-2-70b-hf` (rev main) | arXiv:2307.09288 sec 2.1, Table 1 |

| Headline claim | Fail if Delta_aln at 70B is at most 0.5 x Delta_aln at 13B on at least 2 of 3 alignment metrics (AlpacaEval-2 LC percent, IFEval strict accuracy, help-harm AUC) AND capability scale-effect non-significant on at least 2 of 4 (MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval, MATH) after Holm correction. |

| ToxiGen | toxigen/toxigen-data v1.0 test | 0 | Native prompt | Greedy | Toxicity classifier s-nlp/roberta_toxicity_classifier on implicit rev variant | arXiv:2203.09509 (Hartvigsen et al.) |
| TruthfulQA-gen | truthfulqa/truthful_qa generation | 0 | Llama-2-Chat template | T=0.7 (gen mode) | GPT-judge (gpt-3.5-turbo) for MC2 on generation splits | arXiv:2109.07958 (Lin et al.) |
