# Experimental design — parametric surrogates for DrivAerNet++ aerodynamic drag

## 1. Research question and pre-registered hypotheses

**RQ.** On the DrivAerNet++ 26-parameter design space (fastback, notchback, estateback body styles), does the predictive performance of surrogate models built from the parametric descriptors **improve with training set size** and **differ across model architectures** for aerodynamic drag prediction?

| ID | Hypothesis | Statistical target | Decision cell |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Size main effect — performance improves with n | LMM fixed effect for log10(n) on RMSE (negative) | Adjusted p < 0.01 (per architecture) |
| H2 | Architecture main effect — at a fixed n, architectures differ | Layer-1 omnibus (Friedman across 6 architectures) + at least one Holm-adjusted pairwise Layer-1 hit | at size k = K (largest): omnibus p < 0.05 |
| H3 | Size × architecture interaction — curves have different shapes | LMM interaction architecture × log10(n); Layer-2 Holm-adjusted test on per-architecture power-law exponent c | LMM Wald p < 0.01; ≥ 1 Holm-adjusted Layer-2 pair |
| H4 | LOSO robustness — pooled-vs-LOSO ranking does not invert | Spearman ρ between pooled and LOSO mean RMSE rankings; maximum rank shift per architecture | Spearman ρ ≥ 0.6 and rank shift ≤ 2 slots |

## 2. Dataset and parameterisation of unknowns

The dataset file is not present in the workspace; the design therefore proceeds symbolically and binds every dataset-dependent value to a named design parameter `Pn` with an "unspecified at design time; to be supplied from the dataset card" default that enters at a fixed workflow entry point.

| ID | Parameter | Workflow entry point (section §) | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | N_fastback, N_notchback, N_estateback, total N | §4 (schedule), §5 (folds) | unspecified at design time |
| P2 | Whether the 26 parameters are identical across body styles or partly variant-specific | §3 (preprocessor), §8 (feature-leakage check) | assume **shared**; flag sensitivity toggle if variant-specific |
| P3 | Units & scaling of the 26 parameters (lengths, ratios, zero-bounded quantities) | §3 (preprocessor) | unspecified at design time; applied as StandardScaler with optional log1p on declared zero-bounded fields |
| P4 | Whether DrivAerNet++ publishes a canonical train/test split | §5 (partitioning) | use canonical split if present; otherwise build a seed-derived stratified split and disclose the seed |
| P5 | Target variable: Cd / F_d / Cd_p and reference conditions (ρ, U, A) | §6 (metrics & units) | **Cd, dimensionless**; tagged so swapping to F_d (N) or Cd_p only changes the units row and the nRMSE reference |
| P6 | Mutually exclusive body-style labels or multi-label | §5 (LOSO, stratification) | assume **mutually exclusive**; sensitivity toggle documented if multi-label |
| P7 | Master seed for splits, subsampling, MLP init, GP optimizer | §8 (controls) | seed value to be fixed at design time (placeholder: 0) |
| P8 | Pilot budget for pre-registering hyperparameters (M1–M6) | §3, §10 | to be fixed at design time (upper bound: ≤ 10 % of N_train or ≤ 300 designs, whichever smaller) |

## 3. Surrogate model set and pre-registered configurations

Six architectures are compared. **Hyperparameters are fixed per architecture across all training sizes**; their final values are locked by a pre-registration pilot (P8) before any size-grid fit is opened. The fixed-configuration policy is a deliberate confound with the learning-curve interpretation: the curve measures "this pre-registered configuration of family X" rather than "the best achievable instance of family X at each size".

| ID | Model | Library & class skeleton | Pre-registered hyperparameters (locked by pilot P8) | Output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | Linear OLS baseline | `sklearn.linear_model.LinearRegression` | none | point |
| M2 | Degree-2 polynomial + ridge | `preprocessing.PolynomialFeatures(degree=2, interaction_only=False, include_bias=False)` → `linear_model.Ridge(alpha=α_ridge)` | α_ridge (TBD by pilot) | point |
| M3 | Anisotropic-ARD-RBF Gaussian Process | `gaussian_process.GaussianProcessRegressor(kernel=RBF(length_scale=np.ones(26), length_scale_bounds=(1e-3, 1e3)) * ConstantKernel, alpha=α_noise, normalize_y=True, n_restarts_optimizer=3)` | α_noise, kernel priors (TBD by pilot) | point + 95 % PI |
| M4 | Random Forest | `ensemble.RandomForestRegressor(criterion="squared_error", n_estimators=N_trees, max_features="sqrt", min_samples_leaf=msl, n_jobs=1, random_state=seed)` | N_trees, msl (TBD by pilot) | point |
| M5 | Gradient Boosting | `ensemble.HistGradientBoostingRegressor(loss="squared_error", max_iter=N_iter, learning_rate=lr, max_leaf_nodes=mln, l2_regularization=l2, random_state=seed)` | N_iter, lr, max_leaf_nodes, l2 (TBD by pilot) | point |
| M6 | MLP, 2 hidden layers 128 → 64, ReLU, early stopping | `torch.nn.Sequential(Linear(26,128), ReLU(), Linear(128,64), ReLU(), Linear(64,1))`; Adam; MSE loss | lr, batch, max_epochs, early-stopping patience (TBD by pilot) | point |

Pilot procedure (§10): on a stratified sub-sample of N_train at size upper-bounded by P8, run a bounded broad search (grid for tree/MLP HPs; optimizer-restart sweep for α_noise / length-scale priors for M3), record metric, lock the configuration. The pilot does **not** participate in the per-size grid.

## 4. Training-size schedule and resampling

**Schedule.** Geometric, K = 6 spacing exponents, ≈ 7 sizes including the full training pool:

> n_k = floor(N_train · 2^k / 2^K), k = 0, 1, ..., K

Identifiability floor for M2 (degree-2 polynomial over 26 features → 351 unknowns under StandardScaler + interaction expansion): n_0 ≥ N_poly minimum. When P1 implies n_0 < N_poly, drop the smallest k values until n_min ≥ N_poly. N_poly itself is a parameter (default 150); it must be ≥ ~100–200 in practice. The exact threshold is set at design time, not invented.

**Resampling.** K_repl = 10 seeded replicates per (architecture, size) cell. All M1–M6 architectures observe the **same K_repl training subsets** at every size k, so all per-cell comparisons are paired. Per-replicate PRNG is derived deterministically from master seed P7 plus a per-replicate offset.

**Held-out test set.** A single stratified-proportional holdout carved out from the dataset once (using P4 if a canonical test partition exists; otherwise a seed-controlled fallback). The same held-out set is used by every (architecture, size, replicate) cell of the primary analysis, so test statistics are paired across the full grid.

## 5. Body-style partitioning

### 5.1 Primary — pooled, stratified-proportional

- Carve the held-out test set once via stratified proportional sampling on body style from the full dataset (uses P4 if canonical; otherwise build with P7).
- N_train = remaining designs. For each replicate r and size k, draw n_k stratified proportional on body style from N_train.

### 5.2 Secondary — leave-one-style-out (LOSO), 3 × 6 matrix

- For s ∈ {fastback, notchback, estateback}: training pool = N_train ∩ ¬s; test pool = all designs with style s.
- Same K_repl replicates reused; replicates share the LOSO partitions (the LOSO test fold is a deterministic function of style labels).
- Cells: 3 held-out styles × 6 architectures = 18 LOSO cells.
- **Leakage guard:** no observation with style s appears in any LOSO training fold when s is the held-out style (§8).
- Mutually-exclusivity (P6) is the working assumption; if the dataset is multi-label, swap the partition for an "any-overlap" rule with explicit excluded-overlap zone and re-issue the LOSO matrix.

The LOSO analysis is paired with the pooled curve: 6 architectures compared on both, with the architecture-on-LOSO ordering shown alongside the pooled ordering (H4).

## 6. Evaluation metrics with units

All metrics computed on the held-out test set. Units are tagged on P5; swapping target changes only this section.

| Metric | Definition | Units | Reported for |
|---|---|---|---|
| R² | 1 − SS_res / SS_tot | dimensionless | M1..M6 |
| RMSE | sqrt(mean((y − ŷ)²)) | declared target units (P5) | M1..M6 |
| MAE | mean(abs(y − ŷ)) | declared target units (P5) | M1..M6 |
| nRMSE | RMSE / std(y_test) | dimensionless | M1..M6 |
| 95 % PI empirical coverage | mean(I{y_low ≤ y ≤ y_up}) with y_low = μ − 1.96 σ, y_up = μ + 1.96 σ | dimensionless | **M3 only** |
| Mean 95 % PI width | mean(y_up − y_low) | declared target units (P5) | **M3 only** |

Coverage and width are not reported for deterministic models — they would not be meaningful.

## 7. Statistical comparison plan

### 7.1 Layer 1 — per-size vertical separation (paired Wilcoxon)

- Within each size k, for each unordered pair of architectures (p, q) ∈ pairs(M1..M6): paired Wilcoxon signed-rank on the K_repl = 10 RMSE samples.
- 15 pairs × 7 sizes = up to 105 raw Layer-1 p-values.
- **Holm-Bonferroni correction is applied separately within each size** (across the 15 pairs at that size), preserving power at small k where fewer pairs are likely to reject.
- Report Δ_{pq,k} = median(RMSE_q − RMSE_p) per pair per size, alongside the adjusted p.
- Optional guard: per-size Friedman omnibus across 6 architectures; reject H2 only if at least one adjusted pairwise Layer-1 comparison is significant at k = K.

### 7.2 Layer 2 — curve-level shape (per-architecture power-law fit + paired test)

- Within each replicate r (1..K_repl), for each architecture m, fit
  > RMSE_m,k,r = a_m,r + b_m,r · n_k^(−c_m,r),  k = 0..K
  with a ≥ 0, b ≥ 0, c ∈ (0, 2]. Use `scipy.optimize.curve_fit` starting from a log-linear OLS fit on (log n_k, log max(RMSE − min_RMSE, ε)).
- For each unordered pair of architectures (p, q): paired Wilcoxon on {c_p,r} vs {c_q,r} across the K_repl = 10 replicates.
- 15 pairs total; **Holm-Bonferroni correction across the 15 pairs.**
- Also report Δ_a and Δ_b for the asymptotic and bulk contributions.

### 7.3 Mandatory robustness companion — Linear Mixed Model

- Model: `metric ~ C(architecture) * log10(n) + (1 | replicate)`
- Random effect: replicate (intercepts).
- Fixed effects: architecture (six levels), log10(n), interaction.
- Test for H3: Type-III Wald on the interaction term "slope differs across architectures".
- Diagnostics: residual heteroscedasticity across n; if detected, fall back to a log-transformed target within the LMM but keep the per-size Layer-1 reporting on the original (declared) units.
- The LMM is a single conditional test (Wald, df = 5 for the interaction); no further correction is applied to it.

### 7.4 Multiplicity & power notes

- Layer-1 Holm is **per size** — small-k corrections may reject few pairs; that is accepted.
- Layer-2 Holm is across the 15 architecture pairs.
- LMM interaction p is one conditional test and does not enter either Holm family.
- No cross-layer correction — each layer answers a different pre-registered question.

## 8. Controls and leakage prevention

| ID | Control | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Master seed P7 fixed; per-replicate PRNG derived deterministically (P7 + r-offset) | `numpy.random.default_rng(P7 + r); `torch.manual_seed`/`torch.cuda.manual_seed_all` set in M6 only |
| C2 | Identical preprocessor across architectures, fit on per-replicate training **only** | `sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler` fit on the K_repl × n_k training subset; the same scaler instance type (not state) is reused across M1..M6 |
| C3 | MLP early-stopping calibration fold drawn from per-replicate training pool, consistent across sizes | 80 / 20 split of per-replicate training subset, replicated at every k so the calibration subset is identical across sizes within a replicate |
| C4 | LOSO leakage guard | Assert that no observation with held-out style s appears in any LOSO training fold when s is the held-out style; assert the count |
| C5 | Feature-leakage check | Input matrix must have exactly 26 columns matching P2; raise on schema drift; strip ID and constant columns; log the parameter list used |
| C6 | Style-proportional sanity | Per replicate, body-style proportions in the train subsample must lie within ε (default 0.05) of the stratified test proportions |
| C7 | Reproducibility manifest | Per-replicate JSON: seeds, HP configs, scaler statistics, library versions, sample counts |

## 9. Feasibility and runtime budget

**Environment.** 24 CPU cores, no GPU, no network, system Python 3.12.3. ML libraries (scikit-learn ≥ 1.4; xgboost ≥ 2.0 optional; torch ≥ 2.2 optional) are **not preinstalled**. Installing them is an external dependency outside the design contract; the design assumes they are available at execution time and falls back to sklearn-only if not.

**Computational shape (order-of-magnitude only).**

- Primary pooled analysis: K_arch × K_sizes × K_repl = 6 × 7 × 10 ≈ 420 fits on the largest size is the worst case; GP typically dominates.
- LOSO: K_arch × K_styles × K_repl = 6 × 3 × 10 = 180 fits, computed on the LOSO training pools.
- Pilot: ≤ P8 designs × 6 architectures.
- Total ≈ 600 + pilot fits.

**Cost drivers (rough ranking, no numeric claims).**

| Architecture | Dominant cost component | Fit-level rough category |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Linear OLS | closed-form | negligible |
| M2 Degree-2 + Ridge | 351-feature closed-form | negligible |
| M3 GP ARD RBF | n³ kernel inversion + hyper-restarts | dominant cost on large k (parameterized at execution time) |
| M4 RF | 500 trees, embarassingly parallel across cores | modest |
| M5 GBM | 500 boosting iterations, histogram splits | modest |
| M6 MLP | epochs × mini-batches × 26 input / 192 hidden units | modest (CPU-bound; no GPU available) |

**Parallelisation policy.**

- Parallelise **across replicates**, not across sizes within an architecture. Replicates are independent and seed-isolated; sizes within a replicate share calibration fold offsets and must run serially to keep seeds deterministic.
- Use up to 10 of 24 cores for the primary pooled grid (`joblib.Parallel(n_jobs=10)`-style batching).
- LOSO fits reuse the same parallel regime on the LOSO training pools.
- One core is reserved for orchestration of the reproduci

## Inspection Report (Phase 1)

### 1) Input / repository inspection — what is actual vs assumed

**What is present (verified):**
- `/workspace` contains exactly one file: `task.json` (752 bytes).
- `task.json` fields: `question`, `context = "Design an experiment that answers the question. The researcher can clarify source-supported setup details by topic. Do not claim that an experiment was run."`, and `documents.track.md = "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."` (i.e., the brief explicitly states this is design-only).
- Python 3.12.3 is the only interpreter; `numpy`, `scipy`, `scikit-learn`, `pandas`, `matplotlib`, `torch`, `xgboost`, `lightgbm` are all **not** preinstalled.
- 24 CPUs, no GPU, network disabled (per runtime note).
- No DrivAerNet++ files anywhere on disk; `track.md` is referenced only as a string inside `task.json`, not present as a file.

**Confirmable conventions (taken from the researcher-supplied brief and `task.json`, not invented):**
- Input space dimensionality: **D = 26** parameters.
- Target: **aerodynamic drag** (scalar, presumably Cd).
- Three car-configuration categories: **fastback, notchback, estateback**.
- Goal: does surrogate quality **improve with training-set size** and **differ across architectures**.

**What must be ASSUMED (no confirmed source evidence in this workspace):**
- Exact file format / column names / physical units of the 26 parameters (lengths, angles, radii? dimensionless?).
- Sample counts per configuration (does DrivAerNet++'s parametric subset include all three with equal cardinalities? It is **not guaranteed**).
- Cd ground-truth values are scalar floats (vs. signed offsets / per-configuration baselines).
- Train/val/test splits that the dataset authors published.
- Any prepublished benchmark numbers for reference.

### 2) Proposed approach — outline only (no full design yet)

**Candidate architectures (≥ 4, span model families so the "architecture matters" question is answerable):**
- Linear baseline: **Ridge regression** (sanity ceiling for linear separability, low-variance reference curve).
- Strong tabular classical learner: **Gradient-boosted trees** (e.g., XGBoost or sklearn HistGradientBoosting — pick whichever is installable on a no-network box; **LightGBM is a fine substitute**).
- Neural MLP: a small **MLP** (≤ 3 hidden layers, GELU + dropout, output scalar). Optional: a lightweight **TabularTransformer / FT-Transformer** style model if dropout regularization is wanted — only include if compute allows.
- **Random Forest / ExtraTrees** as a second tree baseline to disentangle "any tree model" from "boosting specifically".

A 4–5 family comparison is enough; do not need to grid over widths/depths for the research question — a **single fixed, reasonable architecture hyperparameter setting per family** is the design's intent.

**Training-set size schedule (learning-curve design):**
- Train fractions roughly `f ∈ {0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.40, 0.80}` of the full parametric subset (subject to compute), drawn in a **stratified way by configuration** so each fraction keeps the fastback / notchback / estateback ratio of the full set.
- For each fraction, perform **k-fold cross-validation (k = 5 or 10)** within the train portion to estimate generalization, plus a **fixed held-out test set (~10–20%)** for absolute comparison at the end.

**Data split & CV strategy:**
- Two-level split: outer **fixed test set** (stratified by configuration, seed-locked) and inner **K-fold CV on the train portion**, stratified by configuration, for curves. Repeats with **R ≥ 5 random seeds** to get mean ± a confidence band.

**Metrics:**
- Primary: **R²**, **RMSE** (in original Cd units).
- Secondary: **MAE**, and per-configuration error breakdown (config-stratified R² & RMSE) — required to answer "differ across configurations" if asked later.
- All curves plotted as **mean ± 1 std / 95% CI band over seeds** vs. log10(training size).

**Controls for confounding:**
- **Parameter normalization** (z-score on train fold only, applied to val/test) — same scaler fit on inner-train only.
- **Configuration balance**: stratified sampling at every fraction; also report **per-config error panels**.
- **Target transform**: drag is positive — consider log1p only if skew is empirically large; decision deferred until data is seen.
- **Identical seeds, split indices, and scalers across all architectures** for a given (fraction, repeat) so curve differences reflect architecture, not sampling noise.
- **Single shared hyperparameter budget per family** (e.g., n_estimators / depth / epochs fixed or short random search ≤ 10 trials; this decision is noted under uncertainties).

**Analysis plan:**
1. Plot **learning curves** R² and RMSE vs. training set size, one panel per architecture.
2. **Architecture comparison**: at each fraction, run paired statistical test across seed pairs (e.g., **paired t-test or Wilcoxon on per-fold errors**, or **bootstrap CI on Δ-error**) between every pair of architectures; correct for multiple comparisons (Holm–Bonferroni).
3. **Saturation test**: fit simple parametric learning-curve models (log-linear, power-law) per architecture; test whether the slope differs significantly.
4. **Per-configuration breakdown** as a sensitivity check.
5. **Interpretation guards**: distinguish "more data closes the gap" (red-shift of curves) from "architectures asymptote at different ceilings".

### 3) Assumptions & uncertainties — marked load-bearing vs routine

**Load-bearing (could meaningfully change the answer — researcher input recommended):**
- **L1. Per-configuration sample counts & imbalance** in DrivAerNet++'s parametric subset. If notchback >> estateback, "improvement with N" may be dominated by the smallest class. Need to fix a stratification policy that doesn't artificially inflate any class.
- **L2. Train-fraction grid exact values.** Different grids change curve shape and saturation point. A standardised 5-point log-spaced grid is proposed.
- **L3. Number of repeats R.** Too few → noisy comparisons; too many → compute blow-up. R = 5 proposed as default.
- **L4. Hyperparameter protocol.** Whether each architecture gets a **short** tuned setup or a **fixed default**. Choice biases the "architecture comparison" hugely; MLP especially varies with epochs/lr. Proposal: **one short, equal-cost random search per family (~10 trials)** to avoid hand-favouring any.
- **L5. Selection of test/train split ratio and seed.** Affects absolute numbers; curves remain comparable internally.
- **L6. Installation / availability of ML libraries** (currently not installed; network disabled). Proposal: prefer `scikit-learn` + `numpy` + `scipy` only (CPU-only, pip-installable offline if needed), include XGBoost/LightGBM only if already present to avoid installation issues.

**Routine (low-risk, but worth recording):**
- R1. Random seeds list (e.g., 0–4).
- R2. Error bars: 95% CI vs ±1 std.
- R3. Plot styling.
- R4. Whether to shuffle inside the train pool.
- R5. File naming convention of outputs.

**Cross-cutting unknown (affects almost every load-bearing item):**
- **U1.** The actual DrivAerNet++ release ingested: parameter list, units, total sample count, configuration labels, and whether a precomputed parametric subset exists or whether the 26 features must be re-derived from the mesh/geometry. The whole experiment plan grid (especially L1, L2, L5) depends on this. **Without this, the design carries assumptions; with it, all assumptions become facts.**

I am **not** ready to commit a full design yet because L1–L6 and U1 are open. Please indicate (a) whether class balance / sample counts are known to you, (b) preferred architecture families, (c) exact train-fraction grid and number of repeats acceptable, and (d) any hyperparameter protocol preference, so the full design can be locked.

# Experiment Design — Surrogate Drag Models on DrivAerNet++ 26-Param Subset
## Learning curves by architecture (Design-only document; no execution; no fabricated numbers)

---

## 1. Scope and research questions

This document specifies an experiment that answers two questions using DrivAerNet++'s released parametric 26-dimensional subset of aerodynamic car designs:

- **RQ1 (size effect).** Does surrogate-model predictive performance on aerodynamic drag (Cd) improve as the training-set size increases?
- **RQ2 (architecture effect).** Does the size-vs-error *trajectory* differ across model architectures, and if so, in which regime (low-N, mid-N, or the asymptote)?

The design explicitly distinguishes RQ1 from RQ2 by holding every non-architectural factor identical per (fraction, seed) cell across all architectures.

**Operational hypotheses (pre-registered so the analysis doesn't drift):**
- **H1 (size).** For each architecture, test-set error decreases monotonically (in expectation) as train fraction grows; this is testable with a one-sided Page-style trend test on the R = 5 seed means per fraction and visually as a downward curve.
- **H2 (architecture).** At least one pair of architectures has a non-zero paired Δ-error at one or more train fractions after Holm–Bonferroni correction across the 6 architecture pairs.
- **H3 (interaction, optional, pre-declared).** The size-vs-error slope differs across architectures, testable by comparing the fitted power-law exponent α across families (see §11.3).

---

## 2. Locked experimental setup

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Parameter space | D = 26 (continuous, predefined by DrivAerNet++ schema) |
| Target | scalar Cd (unitless) |
| Configurations | fastback, notchback, estateback (3-class stratification label) |
| Architectures | {Ridge, RandomForestRegressor, HistGradientBoostingRegressor, MLPRegressor} — **4 families, no Tabular Transformer** |
| Train fractions f | {0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.40, 0.80} — 5 log-spaced points |
| Seeds | R = 5, seeds = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4} |
| Inner CV | k = 5, stratified by configuration |
| Outer test set | 15% of full set, configuration-stratified, **frozen across all cells and seeds** |
| Scaler | z-score on inner-train fold only; identical scaler fit reused per cell |
| Sampling | stratified subsampling to preserve full-set configuration ratio at every f |
| Hyperparameter protocol | one equal-cost 10-trial random search per family at f = 0.40 with seed 0; recipes frozen thereafter |
| Multiple comparisons | Holm–Bonferroni on the 6 architecture pairs |
| Curve parametric fit | power-law first; log-linear fallback if power-law fit R² < 0.7 |
| Curve bands | mean ± 95% CI over R = 5 seeds via bootstrap (10 000 resamples) |

---

## 3. Inherited assumptions (separate from task-given facts)

These are **not** confirmed by visible sources in `/workspace`; they are explicitly carried forward from the researcher's approval and flagged as working premises. If reality differs, it is a *known limitation*, not a retrofit.

- **A1.** A precomputed tabular file exists with 26 numeric feature columns + a `configuration` column + a scalar `Cd` column. No re-derivation from meshes/STLs.
- **A2.** The three configurations coexist in the subset; per-class counts may be imbalanced (stratification in §6 handles this).
- **A3.** Target is scalar Cd only; no Cl / Cs / Cm / side-force.
- **A4.** No author-released split is mirrored; the design uses its own stratified outer test. **Results are internal-comparable across architectures but not literature-comparable.**
- **B1.** `numpy`, `scipy`, and `scikit-learn` are available (CPU wheels) in the execution environment. No GPU dependency. No `torch`, no `xgboost`, no `lightgbm`.
- **B2.** Soft cap ≤ ~10 CPU-min per (architecture × fraction) cell, global ceiling ~4 hours on a 24-CPU box; downscale within a cell (e.g., reduce MLP `max_iter` or RF `n_estimators`) before changing the architecture set or fraction grid.

These are stated **separately** from any value that the task brief or `task.json` (the only visible sources) makes mandatory.

---

## 4. Architectural specifications

For every family, both **search space** (used only during the §7 frozen random search) and **frozen default recipe** (used in every other cell) are defined. The frozen default is the search-trail winner at f = 0.40 / seed 0.

### 4.1 Ridge (linear baseline)

- Class: `sklearn.linear_model.Ridge`.
- Search space: α ∈ {10⁻³, 10⁻², 10⁻¹, 1, 10, 10², 10³}; solver = {`auto`, `lsqr`}; with/without intercept (true by default).
- Frozen default: search-winner α, `solver = auto`, `random_state = seed`.
- Notes: cheapest fit in the panel; serves as a linear-separability floor.

### 4.2 RandomForestRegressor (tree baseline)

- Class: `sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestRegressor`.
- Search space: `n_estimators ∈ {200, 400, 800}`; `max_features ∈ {sqrt, log2, 0.5}`; `max_depth ∈ {None, 12, 20}`; `min_samples_leaf ∈ {1, 5, 20}`; `bootstrap = True`.
- Frozen default: search-winner config; `n_jobs = min(24, max(2, N_train // 200))` to honor §B2's CPU-minute cap; bags are single-threaded for fair CPU accounting, or parallelised only if a real wall-clock measurement confirms headroom.
- Notes: tagged "tree baseline" to disentangle *any tree model* from *boosting* in §11.

### 4.3 HistGradientBoostingRegressor (boosted tree, primary strong learner)

- Class: `sklearn.ensemble.HistGradientBoostingRegressor`.
- Search space: `learning_rate ∈ {0.01, 0.03, 0.1}`; `max_iter ∈ {300, 800, 1500}`; `max_depth ∈ {None, 6, 10}`; `min_samples_leaf ∈ {10, 30, 100}`; `l2_regularization ∈ {0.0, 1.0}`; `early_stopping = True` with `validation_fraction = 0.15` and `n_iter_no_change = 50`.
- Frozen default: search-winner config; `random_state = seed`.
- Notes: chosen over XGBoost to stay inside the locked software floor.

### 4.4 MLPRegressor (neural baseline)

- Class: `sklearn.neural_network.MLPRegressor`.
- Search space: `hidden_layer_sizes ∈ {(64,), (128, 64), (256, 128, 64)}` (≤ 3 hidden layers, as locked); activation = `relu`; `alpha ∈ {10⁻⁵, 10⁻³, 10⁻¹}`; `learning_rate_init ∈ {10⁻³, 10⁻²}`; `early_stopping = True`; `validation_fraction = 0.15`; `n_iter_no_change = 20`; `max_iter ∈ {200, 500}`; `solver = adam`.
- Frozen default: search-winner config; `random_state = seed`.
- **Known risk (declared up front):** MLPRegressor can fail to converge or reach different local minima across seeds. Mitigation: (a) use `early_stopping`; (b) record whether `converged_` was reached for every fit (per-cell diagnostic); (c) treat MLP means across seeds as long as ≥ 3 of R = 5 seeds converged; otherwise flag the cell as "MLP non-convergent at this fraction" and do **not** impute — the cell is reported in tables but excluded from cross-architecture paired tests.

---

## 5. Sourcing, schema, and pre-processing

**Step 5.1 (planned, design-only).** Load the parametric 26-d file. Columns expected: 26 numeric feature columns `x_1 … x_26`, a `configuration ∈ {fastback, notchback, estateback}` column, a `Cd` target column. If the actual schema uses alternative names, surface them in an "actual-snapshot-vs-plan" appendix (no retrofit to assumptions).

**Step 5.2.** Cast `configuration` to a pandas categorical; one-hot encode it for **Ridge and MLP** (tree models can ingest the integer encoding, but the locked recipe feeds both tree and linear models the same `X = [x_1 … x_26, configuration_one_hot]` to remove a confounding vector between linear and tree models).

**Step 5.3.** Split off the outer 15% test set with `train_test_split(..., test_size=0.15, stratify=configuration, random_state=0)` — **this split happens exactly once** and is never re-run. The remaining 85% is the "train pool" used for everything else.

**Step 5.4.** Audit and log: per-configuration counts in the full set and in the outer test; number of missing values per column (expected: 0); Cd distribution (mean, std, min, max, skew). Skew > 1.5 ⇒ flag a possible target transform, but the locked recipe trains on raw Cd; a log1p variant is a **sensitivity analysis** in §12.4, not a default.

---

## 6. Data split and stratified sampling

- **Outer test set.** 15% of full N, stratified by `configuration`, seed 0, frozen. Used **only** for the §11.5 final "outer test numbers" comparison at the end.
- **Inner CV.** k = 5 stratified by `configuration`. Performed **inside the train pool only** — i.e., the test set never enters a fold or a scaler.
- **Configuration-stratified subsampling at each fraction f.** For each (f, seed), draw a stratified subsample of the train pool of size `round(f × 0.85 × N)` such that the class ratio is **identical to the full-set ratio** (not the train-pool ratio, which is identical anyway because stratification carries through). This guarantees that stratified downsampling never artificially favors a configuration.
- **Scaler.** Fit `StandardScaler` on the inner-train fold only; apply to inner-val and (when relevant) the outer test. Re-fit per fold. Identical across architectures — the same scaler object (and same `random_state`s) for every fit in a (fraction, seed) cell.

---

## 7. Hyperparameter protocol (locked; one-time random search at f = 0.40)

- **Where the search happens.** On the train pool at f = 0.40, seed 0, repeated 10 trials per family using K-fold CV inside the train pool only.
- **Equal-cost enforcement.** Each trial is budgeted approximately equally in CPU seconds per family. For Ridge/MLP/HGB, this is straightforward (single fit cost). For RF, scale `n_estimators` so that each trial's RF fit cost is roughly the same wall-clock order.
- **Selection criterion.** Mean of `−RMSE` over the 5 inner folds (higher is better).
- **Freezing.** Once the per-family winner is set, that **single frozen recipe** is reused at every other fraction f ∈ {0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.80} and every seed ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3, 4}. **No per-cell retuning.** This is the rule that makes the architecture comparison interpretable.
- **Why search at f = 0.40 and not at every fraction.** Searching at every fraction would encode "amount of data" into hyperparameter choice, contaminating the curve. Searching at the middle of the curve picks a recipe that is neither starved nor saturated; the recipe's transferability to other fractions is itself a finding worth noting (e.g., RF may overfit at f = 0.05 even with frozen hparams — flagged as a known limitation in §15).

---

## 8. Learning-curve design

For each fraction f, each architecture, each seed r ∈ {0..4}:
1. Draw a stratified subset `Train_pool_r_f` from the train pool.
2. For each inner fold k ∈ {0..4} of `Train_pool_r_f`:
   - Fit scaler on inner-train portion, transform both inner-train and inner-val.
   - Train the architecture with frozen hparams and `random_state = r`.
   - Predict on inner-val; record `RMSE_inner(r, f, k, arch)` and `R²_inner`.
3. The per-cell statistic for (r, f, arch) is the **mean** of the 5 inner-fold RMSEs.

Outer test is **not** used for the curve points — only the 95% CI bands on the inner-CV statistics feed the curve. The outer 15% test enters only at the end (§11.5), with all R = 5 seed means averaged into a single number per (f, arch).

**Reproducibility hook.** Every random operation consumes seed `r` of the {0..4} sequence: random subsampling, scaler shuffling, RF and HGB `random_state`, MLP `random_state`. K-fold assignment uses `KFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=r)` so the inner fold partition varies across seeds exactly as prescribed.

---

## 9. Metrics

| Metric | Primary / Secondary | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **R² (test set)** | Primary | Standard comparability; tells fraction of Cd variance explained. |
| **RMSE (Cd units)** | Primary | Scale-aligned interpretability (drag engineers reason in Cd). |
| **MAE (Cd units)** | Secondary | Robustness check; less sensitive to tails than RMSE. |
| **Per-configuration R² & RMSE** | Secondary (required deliverable) | Answers "differ across configurations" with a printable table/panel. |
| **Convergence flag (MLP only)** | Diagnostic | Tag unstable fits; does not enter numerical aggregation if exclusion criterion of §4.4 fires. |

All four metrics are computed on inner-val folds (for curve points) and on the outer 15% test set (for the final table).

---

## 10. Controls for confounding

- **C1 — Parameter normalization.** Standard z-score, fit on inner-train only. Without this, MSE/relative contribution of each parameter depends on its units, biasing the architecture comparison.
- **C2 — Configuration balance.** Stratified subsampling at every fraction (see §6). Without this, "more data improves accuracy" can be confounded by "more data of the majority class improves accuracy on the majority class only".
- **C3 — Identical seeds/splits/scalers.** Across architectures in the same (f, r) cell, identical subsample, identical fold partitions, identical scaler. Curve differences therefore reflect architecture, not sampling noise.
- **C4 — Identical hyperparameter budget.** Equal-cost 10-trial search per family at f = 0.40 with seed 0; recipes frozen. Prevents "we tuned MLP more carefully than RF".
- **C5 — Fixed outer test.** Outer 15% test is defined once and never re-sampled. Prevents two architectures being implicitly graded on different test distributions.
- **C6 — No target transform (by default).** Raw Cd is the locked target. log1p is a sensitivity experiment (§12.4) to confirm that the rank order of architectures is not an artifact of skew.
- **C7 — No test-set feedback.** Outer test enters no model selection, no hyperparameter selection, no scaler fit. The only way outer test is used is for the §11.5 report table.
- **C8 — Software & RNG hygiene.** `numpy` and `random` seeded per cell; `PYTHONHASHSEED` fixed; sklearn `random_state` set. Lockfile pinned where possible.

---

## 11. Analysis plan

### 11.1 Learning-curve plots

Two panels:
- **Panel A.** RMSE (Cd units) on the y-axis, `log10(training_set_size)` on the x-axis. One curve per architecture. Mean of R = 5 inner-CV RMSEs as the point, 95% bootstrap CI (10 000 resamples over the R = 5 seed means at that fraction) as the band.
- **Panel B.** R² mirror image of Panel A. Same bands.

A **dual x-axis** (fraction and absolute N) is printed on the figure for interpretability, but fractions are the primary independent variable.

### 11.2 Pairwise architecture comparison

At each f, compute Δ-error per (architecture A, architecture B) per (seed r): `Δ_r = RMSE_r_A − RMSE_r_B`. Six pairs from C(4, 2).

- **Normality check.** Shapiro–Wilk on the R = 5 Δ values per pair per fraction. If p > 0.05 for the pair across fractions, use the **paired t-test**; otherwise use the **Wilcoxon signed-rank** with `zero_method = "wilcox"`.
- **Effect size.** Cohen's `d_z` on paired Δ values (standardized mean difference of Δ); reported alongside the p-value. Magnitude labels qualified verbally (small / medium / large) without false numeric thresholds.
- **Within-pair multiplicity.** Per pair, six tests (one per f). **Holm–Bonferroni correction** across the six fractions **per pair** keeps family-level error controlled.
- **Across-pair multiplicity.** A second Holm step is applied across the C(4, 2) = 6 pairs **at the smallest fraction only**, since that is where the architecture effect is most likely to differ. (Documented choice; the primary narrative is per-pair curve-trajectory.)
- **Visualization.** For each pair, a forest plot of `d_z` over fractions; the curve-pair panel as a small multiple.

### 11.3 Saturation / fit of power-law

For each architecture, fit
`RMSE(N) = a − b · N^{−α},   α > 0, a > 0, b > 0`
over the 5 points (fractions), where `N = round(f × 0.85 × N_full)`. Use non-linear least squares bounded as above.

- **Fallback.** If the power-law fit fails to converge or in-fold `R² < 0.7`, fit the log-linear surrogate `RMSE(N) = a + b · log10(N)` and report the fit used in a footnote on the panel.
- **Slope comparison.** Bootstrap CIs (10 000 resamples over the 5 seed means at each f it-self) on a, b, α per architecture. An architecture's CI on α that does not overlap another architecture's CI is a **declaration of slope difference**; otherwise declared inconclusive.
- **Asymptote comparison.** Same bootstrap procedure on `a`. Architectures with non-overlapping `a` CIs are declared to asymptote at different floors.

### 11.4 Per-configuration breakdown

For each arch × f × configuration, report R² and RMSE on inner-val (curve) and on outer test (table). Two visualizations:

- A heatmap (rows = architecture, columns = configuration) of R² at f = 0.80 (the highest-fidelity cell).
- A grouped bar chart at f = 0.05 and f = 0.80 showing per-config RMSE.

If a configuration is rare (e.g., estateback ≪ fastback), its CIs will be wider — reported honestly, not "balanced away".

### 11.5 Outer-test final table

A single fixed table reporting, for each architecture at f ∈ {0.40, 0.80} (the two highest-information cells), the **outer-test** RMSE and R² (averaged across the R = 5 seed-refits, each refitting on the full 85% train pool with the frozen recipe and using seed r). This table anchors the truth-points of the inner-CV curves at the right-hand side without re-touching the curves themselves.

### 11.6 Interpretation guards (declared up front)

- **Gap closing vs. ceiling shift.** A red-shift of two architecture curves on the same asymptote = "more data closes the gap"; a vertical separation maintained at f = 0.80 = "the architectures have different ceilings". Both will be reported as separate findings.
- **Cross-seed variance dominance.** If at any f, the 95% CI band of one architecture fully contains the others' means, declare the architectures **statistically indistinguishable at that fraction** (after Holm).
- **MLP non-convergence.** If the MLP exclusion criterion of §4.4 fires, declare the architecture **not-applicable at that fraction** and do not back-substitute an imputed point.
- **Configuration-rare class.** Declare estateback's CIs wider if its N_div < N_fastback / 4 (post-pilot; otherwise state "no rare-class observed").

---

## 12. Pre-registered sensitivity / robustness checks

These exist to make claims robust, not to inflate them.

- **§12.1 — Seed-sweep.** R = 5 already implemented as the primary sensitivity scale. If the band still detects curves crossing, we declare that "rank order at this fraction is uncertain". A secondary R' = 10 sweep is permitted *only if global wall-clock allows* (B2 cap).
- **§12.2 — k sweep.** Re-run with k = 10 on the f ∈ {0.20, 0.40} subset and check that curve levels shift uniformly (CV choice should not change relative architecture ordering).
- **§12.3 — Outer-test split size sweep.** Replace 15% with 20% as sanity; not a primary run.
- **§12.4 — log1p(Cd) target transform.** If the §5.4 skew audit exceeds 1.5, retrain all 4 architectures with log1p target and compare rank order; report only if rank order flips.
- **§12.5 — Without configuration in X.** Refit without the one-hot `configuration` to quantify how much of each curve is configuration-information vs. parameter-information.

---

## 13. Software and compute feasibility

### 13.1 Libraries required

| Package | Role | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `numpy` | numerics | required |
| `scipy` | stats, optimization, power-law fit | required |
| `scikit-learn` | all 4 architectures and StandardScaler | required |
| `pandas` | CSV load, schema audit | strongly preferred |
| `matplotlib` | panels and forest plots | strongly preferred |

Not used: `torch`, `xgboost`, `lightgbm`, `catboost` (kept off the software floor by design).

### 13.2 Compute budget (as locked in B2)

Per-cell soft cap: ≤ ~10 CPU-min. Global ceiling: ~4 hours.

- Per (architecture, fraction, seed, fold) = 4 × 5 × 5 × 5 = **500 fits** + 4 × 5 = 20 random-search trials = **520 fits** as the primary run. × 4 architectures in search = 80 trial-fits. Plus per-cell MLP early-stopping overhead. Estimated primary wall-clock below 4 hours on a 24-core box for D = 26 and small-to-mid N; if it isn't, §13.3 downscales.

### 13.3 Downscale policy (preserves architecture set and fraction grid)

In priority order (each step logged with before/after timing):
1. **RF.** Reduce `n_estimators` from 800 → 400 → 200, disable parallelism for fair CPU accounting.
2. **HGB.** Reduce `max_iter` from 1500 → 800 → 500; keep `early_stopping = True`.
3. **MLP.** Reduce `max_iter` from 500 → 300 → 200; reduce hidden width by 25%; keep `early_stopping = True`.
4. **Ridge.** Negligible cost — no downscale needed.

Only as a last resort: drop the largest fraction f = 0.80 and rerun with f ∈ {0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.40}; this is documented as a deviation from the locked grid.

---

## 14. Feasibility assessment

- **Within B2 for a typical DrivAerNet++ subset.** D = 26 is small; all four scikit-learn architectures comfortably handle ~50 000 rows on CPU for these hyperparameters; the dominant cost is RF `n_estimators` and HGB `max_iter`. At the largest fraction (≈ 0.85 × N_full) and a fully-stocked subset, one RF cell can plausibly reach ~10 CPU-min on 24 cores; MLP and Ridge are well below. **Bucket verdict:** the locked soft-cap is feasible; the global ceiling is feasible provided the downscale policy of §13.3 is honored when a cell tips past its per-cell cap.
- **Schema risk (A1 assumption).** If the actual DrivAerNet++ parametric subset is in a different format (e.g., per-configuration columns or one row per simulation rather than per-design), a one-shot schema-adapter script is added to §5.1; no algorithmic change.
- **Class-imbalance risk (A2 assumption).** If the configuration balance is severely skewed, the strata with few counts will have wide inner-CV CIs at small f; reported honestly per §11.6.
- **Convergence risk.** MLP (declared) and HGB (mitigated by early stopping). Both have R = 5 seed medians as the headline, so a single non-convergent seed does not poison the cell.

---

## 15. Limitations (declared here, not later)

- **Internal-comparable only (A4).** No author-released split is mirrored, so results do not compare to published DrivAerNet++ benchmarks. Cross-paper comparability is out of scope.
- **Single 10-trial search (E).** Recipes may not be globally optimal; this is a deliberate design choice to keep the architecture comparison unbiased by per-fraction retuning. The trade-off is acknowledged: the locked MLPs may be undertrained relative to RF.
- **Random search noise.** 10 trials is small; there is non-trivial risk of "winning recipe" instability on a different random sample of 10 trials. Documented as a known limitation.
- **DRIVAERNET++-specific (A1–A4).** If the actual param file differs from the inherited assumptions in material ways, the curve *shape* conclusions likely hold but per-cell numbers will need re-running.
- **Stratified subsampling at low f.** At f = 0.05 with imbalanced classes, a configuration with few samples may have < 5% × its proportion × N < 1 sample in some folds; reported as right-censored rather than smoothed.
- **No model interpretability angle.** This design answers *predictive* questions only; SHAP/Permutation-importance narratives are an extension, not part of the locked plan.

---

## 16. Source-supported facts vs. inherited assumptions

### Source-supported (visible in `/workspace` or the task brief — these can be claimed as fixed)

- Input dimensionality D = 26 (from the researcher's brief).
- Target = aerodynamic drag (Cd) (from the brief).
- Three configurations: fastback, notchback, estateback (from the brief).
- Task is design-only; no run required (from `task.json`).
- `/workspace` contains only `task.json`; no DrivAerNet++ files present.
- No `track.md` file exists on disk; reference is only a literal string inside `task.json`.
- Python 3.12.3 is the interpreter; 24 CPUs; no GPU.
- Network disabled; no `pip install` was attempted because none was needed for this turn.
- `numpy`, `scipy`, `scikit-learn`, `pandas`, `matplotlib`, `torch`, `xgboost`, `lightgbm` are all absent; only stock system packages are installed.

### Inherited assumptions (carried forward from the researcher's approval — flagged as working premises)

- DrivAerNet++ parametric subset is a precomputed 26-d tabular file with a 3-class `configuration` scalar `Cd` schema (A1, A3).
- Configuration counts may be imbalanced; stratification handles it (A2).
- No author-released split is mirrored; results internal-comparable only (A4).
- `scikit-learn` + `numpy` + `scipy` are available in the execution environment; no GPU (B1).
- Soft cap ≤ ~10 CPU-min per cell; global ceiling ~4 hours (B2).
- 4 families locked, no Tabular Transformer, XGBoost out (C-choice-1, C-choice-2).
- Power-law fit on curve with log-linear fallback; Holm–Bonferroni; 95% CI via bootstrap — as defined in §2/§11.

---

## 17. Next steps if executed (plan, not findings)

If and when compute and data are available, the following concrete actions run, in order, with no deviation from the locked setup unless §13.3 fires:

1. **D0 — Audit.** Load the parametric file; audit schema, missingness, configuration counts, Cd distribution. Produce a one-page "actual-snapshot" appendix (no retrofit; deviations from §5 are flagged).
2. **D1 — Outer split.** Stratified 15% / seed-0 outer-test split. Persist splits to disk for transparency.
3. **D2 — Random search.** For each architecture, 10 equal-cost trials at f = 0.40 / seed 0; save frozen recipe.
4. **D3 — Curve sweep.** For each (architecture, f, seed): stratified subsample, 5-fold CV, mean RMSE / R².
5. **D4 — Bootstrap bands.** At each f, 10 000 resamples over R = 5 seed means; 2.5% / 97.5% quantiles for each architecture.
6. **D5 — Power-law fit.** Per architecture; log-linear fallback if `R² < 0.7`. CI on `a`, `b`, `α`.
7. **D6 — Pairwise tests.** Shapiro normality, paired t / Wilcoxon, Cohen's `d_z`, Holm–Bonferroni per pair across fractions; Holm step across pairs at the smallest fraction.
8. **D7 — Per-configuration breakdown.** R² and RMSE tables and heatmaps.
9. **D8 — Outer-test table.** Refit on full 85% train pool at f ∈ {0.40, 0.80}, averaged over R = 5 seed refits.
10. **D9 — Sensitivity bundle.** §12.2 only if D8's claims about ranking need reinforcement.
11. **D10 — Report rendering.** Learning-curve panels (§11.1), forest plots (§11.2 / §11.3), per-config panels (§11.4), outer-test table (§11.5), and interpretation guards (§11.6). A limitations section that mirrors §15 verbatim.
12. **D11 — Reproducibility artefacts.** Lockfile, seeds JSON, frozen recipes JSON, scaler mean/std CSV, per-cell metric CSV, downscaling trace from §13.3 if triggered.

No claim is made in this document about the outcome of any of these steps; they are described as a plan, not as findings.

---

*End of design document.*

## 1. Workspace inspection — what is present and any constraints

Observed:
- `/workspace` contains only `task.json` (question + design-only directive). No source code, no cloned repositories, no datasets, no readmes.
- `/home/actor` is empty. No JAX/JaxMARL/SMAX installed (`pip3 show jax jaxmarl` returns "not found").
- Network is **disabled**, so I cannot clone JaxMARL or fetch any docs/papers. PyPI/git commands are unavailable for this brief.
- Python 3.12.3 available; `git`, `wget`, `curl` are present but unusable for network fetches.
- Environment spec: 24 CPU cores visible, GPU disabled, "bubblewrap" sandbox.

Constraints this implies for the design:
- The design cannot assume I will read released JaxMARL hyperparameters, SMAX reward constants, or published score tables inline; those must be treated as **citation-required inputs the implementer retrieves**.
- No "I ran it" evidence is possible — all numbers in the final design document must be placeholders / illustrative.

---

## 2. Proposed high-level experimental approach

### 2.1 Candidate SMAX maps / scenarios
Pick three that span the difficulty / heterogeneity axis and are in JaxMARL's headline set:
- **3m** — homogeneous, symmetric, small (baseline / lower-difficulty).
- **3s_vs_5z** — heterogeneous unit types *and* asymmetric team sizes (test of credit assignment / sample efficiency).
- **5m_vs_6m** — asymmetric sizes, often harder convergence (tests off-policy advantage).

(Add **2s_vs_1sc** as an optional fourth "super-hard" map if budget allows; otherwise drop.)

### 2.2 Algorithms under comparison
- **PPO branch (JaxMARL)**: use **MAPPO** as the primary PPO reference, because it is the strongest PPO in JaxMARL and the one reported in the JaxMARL paper. Run **IPPO** as a PPO ablation to clarify how much the centralized critic is worth.
- **Q-Learning branch**: use **QMIX** as the primary Q-Learning reference. **VDN** and **IQL** run as Q-Learning-family ablations to attribute gains to credit assignment (mixing net) vs. off-policy per se.

### 2.3 Shared vs. differing components
- **Shared**: JaxMARL's SMAX environment wrappers (e.g., `SMAXLogWrapper`), obs/action spaces, episode length, reward function (JaxMARL's default mixed sparse+shaped reward — to be confirmed against the JaxMARL repo at execution time), evaluation protocol, MLP body architecture (2-layer 64-unit ReLU), GRU encoder either **disabled in both** for the headline comparison (cleaner) or **enabled in both** (recurrent ablation), total environment step budget per (algorithm, map, seed).
- **Differing (algorithmic, not "balanced")**: optimizer (Adam with algorithm-specific lr/clip), rollout-vs-replay data pipeline, target-network update schedule (Q-Learning only), central value head vs. mixing network.

### 2.4 Training-time and normalized-score measurement

**Training time — report both**:
- *Wall-clock seconds to first reach a threshold normalized score* (e.g., 0.8 of expert); computed on a single fixed machine and a single fixed JAX backend (GPU if present, CPU otherwise — declared up front).
- *Environment steps to the same threshold* (hardware-portable secondary metric).
- Also record: mean per-step wall-clock (µs / env step) and total wall-clock to budget cap.

**Normalized score**:
- Per-episode shaped return from the configured reward.
- Define `normalized_score(τ) = (score(τ) − score_random) / (score_expert − score_random)` per (map). `score_random` from a no-op / uniform-random policy run on the same wrapper, same number of episodes (e.g., 32). `score_expert` either (a) the published JaxMARL-paper best score for that map, or (b) the best score observed across our own runs on the same hardware; the choice must be declared and **identical across both algorithms**.
- Aggregate metrics: AUC of the learning curve (env-step-normalized), final-eval score (mean over last 100 eval episodes), and threshold-hit time.

### 2.5 Controls
- **Seeds**: ≥ 5 independent seeds per (algorithm, map); 3 is the absolute floor.
- **Hardware normalization**: lock everything to one machine, one JAX backend, one process layout; record JAX backend string and device count in every run's metadata.
- **Environment wrappers**: identical across algorithms; identical eval episodes per checkpoint.
- **Network capacity**: identical MLP body in actors / critics / mixer-encoder; embed dimension constant.
- **Episode budgets**: identical total env steps; identical eval frequency; identical checkpoint cadence.
- **Hyperparameters**: start from JaxMARL defaults; deviations logged in a per-run override table.
- **Evaluation protocol**: deterministic policies (argmax for Q-Learning, mean for PPO) over a fixed set of eval seeds independent from training seeds.

### 2.6 Analysis / comparison plan
- **Per-run outputs**: per-seed CSV of (env_step, wallclock, eval_return, normalized_score). Learning-curve plot with shaded 95% CI across seeds.
- **Aggregate tables**: per (algorithm × map) — mean ± 95% CI of (a) AUC of normalized score, (b) wall-clock-to-threshold, (c) env-steps-to-threshold, (d) final normalized score.
- **Statistical tests**: Wilcoxon signed-rank across per-seed deltas (PPO − QMIX) on each metric, per map; complement with bootstrap CIs. Holm-Bonferroni correction across the family of metrics.
- **Reporting format**: one results table per metric, one line plot per map, one summary paragraph.
- **Ablations**: (i) IPPO vs MAPPO (centralized-critic effect), (ii) IQL vs VDN vs QMIX (mixing-net effect), (iii) GRU on/off (recurrence effect), (iv) shared vs separate body encoder between actor and value/critic head.

---

## 3. Consequential assumptions and uncertainties

### Assumptions (would lock if approved)
- A1. Compute budget sufficient for 5 seeds × 3 maps × {IPPO, MAPPO, IQL, VDN, QMIX} — that's 75 runs at 2×10⁶ steps each; will likely require a GPU and multi-day runtime.
- A2. Q-Learning primary = **QMIX**; PPO primary = **MAPPO**.
- A3. SMAX maps = **3m, 3s_vs_5z, 5m_vs_6m** (3 maps, fixed).
- A4. Identical MLP body (2×64, ReLU); **no GRU** in the headline comparison; GRU as a separate ablation.
- A5. Identical total env-step budget per (run) and identical eval/ckpt cadence.
- A6. Training time measured as wall-clock on a fixed single-machine JAX backend (GPU if present) **and** as env-steps-to-threshold for portability.
- A7. Reward function = JaxMARL SMAX defaults (sparse + shaped, **to verify** against the repo at execution).
- A8. "Normalized score" uses a self-measured random baseline; "expert" baseline is either JaxMARL-paper published numbers OR the best across our own runs — whichever is chosen, it is the same for both algorithms.
- A9. Deterministic eval using argmax (Q-Learning) / mean (PPO) over fixed eval seeds.
- A10. No shared-encoder trick in headline runs; flagged as a separate ablation.

### Uncertainties / decisions the researcher should make
- U1. Is MAPPO acceptable as the "PPO" arm, or must the comparison be IPPO-only (IPPO is weaker and arguably unfair to PPO on cooperative tasks)?
- U2. Is QMIX acceptable as "Q-Learning," or should the comparison extend to C/WQMIX or SHAQ-equivalents that also leverage a centralized critic (a more even match to MAPPO)?
- U3. How many seeds: 3 vs 5 vs 10 (3 is underpowered, 10 may bust the compute budget)?
- U4. Hardware and compute budget to declare up front so the design document can state runtime expectations precisely.
- U5. Exact env-step budget per run (2e6 vs 5e6 vs until plateau) — drives runtime directly.
- U6. Threshold for "time-to-score" (e.g., 0.6, 0.7, 0.8 of expert?) — sensitivity to this choice should be reported.
- U7. Whether to declare which fields of the global state the QMIX mixer hypernet sees (SMAX exposes it; this biases the comparison in Q-Learning's favor and should be acknowledged, not removed).
- U8. Whether to pin specific JaxMARL config files (algorithms/smax/{ippo,m apppo,qmix,...}) verbatim or re-tune; my recommendation is pin-and-report unless a brief smoke test shows defaults are broken.
- U9. Reporting granularity: one figure per map or one aggregate-with-metric figure — affects how progress is communicated.

I will wait for explicit approval (and decisions on at least U1–U6) before producing the full stage=result design document.
