payload.answer:
# Final Experiment Design — JaxMARL PPO vs Q-Learning on SMAX (Training Time & Normalized Score)

> **Status.** Design-only. No experiment has been executed. All runtime expectations are *projected ranges*, explicitly unverified.
>
> **Locked decisions (from researcher, per U1–U9).** MAPPO primary PPO arm; IPPO ablation only. QMIX primary Q-Learning arm; VDN and IQL ablations only; no C/WQMIX. **5 seeds headline, 3 absolute floor for any run that times out (which runs must be declared)**. **One machine per campaign, one JAX backend (GPU if available, else CPU); 24 vCPU visible; per-run metadata reports backend + device count**. **2×10⁶ env steps headline; optional 5×10⁶ extension on the harder map(s) only if smoke test shows no plateau by 2×10⁶**. **Time-to-threshold at normalized score ∈ {0.6, 0.7, 0.8} of expert; primary metric at 0.8**. **QMIX mixer hypernetwork accesses SMAX global state as in standard QMIX; asymmetry disclosed; mixer-with-state ablated vs mixer-with-only-local-state is an *optional* secondary ablation, only if space allows**. **Pinned JaxMARL released configs `algorithms/smax/{ippo,mappo,qmix,vdn,iql}` verbatim; deviations logged in a per-run overrides table**. **One learning-curve figure per map per metric, one aggregate results table per metric, one summary paragraph; Wilcoxon signed-rank + bootstrap-CI on per-seed deltas (PPO − QMIX), Holm-Bonferroni across the metric family**.

---

## 1. Rationale

JaxMARL (Rutherford et al., 2024) consolidates environment and algorithm implementations behind a single JAX stack and showcases SMAX, a JIT-friendly reimplementation of SMAC. The paper's central pitch is that JAX's JIT/XLA compilation + device parallelism make typical MARL pipelines much faster wall-clock-for-wall-clock than per-agent Python loops.

Two of the most-deployed MARL algorithm families in JaxMARL are PPO (on-policy; MAPPO/IPPO) and value-decomposition Q-Learning (off-policy; QMIX/VDN/IQL). Their reported scores on SMAX are roughly comparable at asymptotic evaluation, but their convergence profiles and amortized per-step cost are *different in kind*: on-policy rollouts + parallel advantage estimation vs. off-policy replay + target networks + periodic hard updates. We therefore ask a methodologically focused question — at equal network capacity, equal env-step budget, equal eval protocol, and a single hardware/backend, **how do the two families compare on training time and on normalized score?**

This design fixes the comparison surface area (architecture, MAPPO-vs-QMIX as head-to-head, IPPO/VDN/IQL as family-context ablations) so any observed gap can be attributed with reasonable confidence to (a) the algorithmic family, (b) the credit-assignment mechanism inside Q-Learning, (c) the centralized critic inside PPO, (d) recurrence, and (e) the QMIX global-state conditioning.

---

## 2. Hypotheses

- **H1 (final normalized score).** On SMAX, the JaxMARL headline configuration of **MAPPO** and **QMIX** reach statistically indistinguishable asymptotic normalized score at equal env-step budget.
- **H2 (training time to threshold).** **QMIX** reaches 0.8·*score_expert* in **less wall-clock time** than **MAPPO** on at least one of {3s_vs_5z, 5m_vs_6m} at equal network and env-step budget, on the chosen JAX backend.
- **H3 (training steps to threshold, hardware-portable).** QMIX reaches 0.8·*score_expert* in **fewer environment steps** than MAPPO on {3s_vs_5z, 5m_vs_6m}, even if H2's wall-clock direction is reversed on CPU-only backends.
- **H4 (centralized-critic contribution, PPO family).** Switching IPPO→MAPPO yields a positive normalized-score delta and a (possibly smaller) wall-clock-time-to-threshold delta on the harder maps.
- **H5 (credit-assignment contribution, Q-Learning family).** VDN outperforms IQL in final score and steps-to-threshold; QMIX outperforms VDN on the harder maps (the strong-form "QMIX ≈ +VDN+monotonic-mixer+state" claim is treated as the ablation goal, not a hypothesis).
- **H6 (recurrence).** Enabling a GRU encoder in *both* arms shifts both the final-score distribution and the wall-clock regime in a *direction-dependent* way (better sample efficiency, lower per-step throughput), with the net wall-clock-to-threshold direction left open.

We additionally pre-register **two null hypotheses** (H0-A: no head-to-head score difference at α=0.05 after Holm-Bonferroni across metrics; H0-B: no head-to-head wall-clock-to-threshold difference at α=0.05 after Holm-Bonferroni) to keep the analysis symmetrical regardless of direction.

---

## 3. Hypotheses ↔ Metrics mapping

| ID | Hypothesis | Primary metric | Secondary metric | Reporting unit |
|----|-----------|----------------|------------------|----------------|
| H1 | Final score parity | Final normalized score (mean over last 100 eval episodes) | AUC of normalized score vs env-step | per map, then aggregate |
| H2 | Wall-clock speed-up (QMIX > MAPPO) | Wall-clock seconds to first reach 0.8·*score_expert* | Wall-clock to 0.6· and 0.7· (sensitivity) | per map |
| H3 | Sample efficiency (QMIX > MAPPO) | Env steps to first reach 0.8·*score_expert* | Env steps to 0.6· and 0.7· | per map |
| H4 | Centralized critic helps PPO | Final normalized score (IPPO→MAPPO Δ) | Wall-clock & steps to 0.8· | per map |
| H5 | Credit assignment helps Q-Learning | Final normalized score across {IQL, VDN, QMIX} | Steps to 0.8· | per map |
| H6 | Recurrence | Wall-clock-to-threshold + per-step wall-clock, both arms | Final score | per map |
| H0-A | No head-to-head score difference | Wilcoxon signed-rank on per-seed deltas (PPO − QMIX) | — | pooled across maps |
| H0-B | No head-to-head wall-clock difference | Wilcoxon signed-rank on per-seed wall-clock deltas (PPO − QMIX) | — | pooled across maps |

**Notation reminder.** "PPO" in §7's headline comparison stands for **MAPPO**; "QMIX" stands for **QMIX**. Per-seed delta is `(headline run under arm A on seed s, map m) − (headline run under arm B on seed s, map m)`.

---

## 4. Environment & algorithm setup

### 4.1 SMAX maps
- **3m** — homogeneous, symmetric, small. Lower-difficulty baseline; both algorithms should saturate.
- **3s_vs_5z** — heterogeneous unit types *and* asymmetric team sizes; standard stress-test for credit assignment.
- **5m_vs_6m** — asymmetric team sizes; converging on this map has historically required careful hyperparameters.

Reasoning locked per U5: the *headline* budget is the same on all three maps. The **optional extension to 5×10⁶ env steps** is permitted (and *only* permitted) on **3s_vs_5z** and **5m_vs_6m**, gated on a documented smoke test that the 2×10⁶ curve has not plateaued within the last 20% of training at sub-threshold score.

### 4.2 Algorithms
| Algorithm | Role | Family | Critic/value mechanism |
|-----------|------|--------|------------------------|
| **MAPPO** | primary PPO | PPO | Centralized value V(s,𝜏), shared parameters |
| IPPO | PPO-family ablation | PPO | Independent value V_i(o_i) |
| **QMIX** | primary Q-Learning | Off-policy Q | Monotonic mixing hypernet conditioned on global state |
| VDN | Q-Learning-family ablation | Off-policy Q | Additive mixing, no hypernet |
| IQL | Q-Learning-family ablation | Off-policy Q | Independent learners, no mixing |

Mixed-radix policy: each algorithm's per-iteration actor sample budget is recorded but **not** normalized across algorithms; what is normalized is total env steps and total wall-clock, since the question is *training-time-to-score* not *iteration-efficiency*.

### 4.3 Pinned configs (U8)
- Source of truth: JaxMARL repository, path `algorithms/smax/{ippo,mappo,qmix,vdn,iql}/*.py` and any `config.yaml`/registry entries found alongside.
- **Action**: every config dict is **pinned verbatim** at the released commit hash specified at the top of the per-run overrides table. Any deviation (new optimizer, batch size change, etc.) is logged in **Table 9-Offline** (per-run overrides) with: deviation, rationale, expected effect, observed effect (to be filled at execution time only if execution is later authorized).

### 4.4 Networks, shared & differing components

**Shared**:
- 2-layer MLP body, 64 hidden units per layer, ReLU activation. **No GRU encoder** in the headline comparison.
- Observation, action, and global-state shapes as exposed by JaxMARl SMAX (intentionally identical for both arms).
- Identical reward function (JaxMARL SMAX default — sparse win/loss + shaped components; to be confirmed verbatim against the repo).
- Identical environment wrappers: `SMAXLogWrapper` and any defaults JaxMARL applies in its SMAX benchmark scripts.
- Identical eval wrapper and identical deterministic-eval policy (argmax for Q-Learning, mean for PPO).

**Differing (intentional, not "balanced")**:
- Optimizer hyperparameters (lr, clip ratio for PPO; target-update period, ε schedule for Q-Learning). Pinned from JaxMARL released configs.
- Rollout vs. replay data pipeline (on-policy buffer for PPO; replay buffer for Q-Learning).
- Critic head: V(s,τ) for MAPPO, V_i(o_i) for IPPO, IQL tabular head, VDN mixer(s;ϕ), QMIX mixer as hypernet on global state.

### 4.5 Optimization & rollout configurations
- Headline env-step budget per run: **2×10⁶**. PPO collects on-policy rollouts and discards; Q-Learning fills a replay buffer of JAX-prerelease default size and samples minibatches.
- Eval cadence: fixed to **(n_eval_episodes, eval_period_env_steps)** = **(32, 10⁴)** — i.e., 32 deterministic eval episodes every 10,000 env steps reported on the learning curve.
- Total checkpoints per run: ~200 (2×10⁶ / 10⁴).

### 4.6 Reward and normalization notes
- Reward signal follows JaxMARL default; **no per-algorithm shaping permitted** in headline runs.
- Evaluation policy for both arms is deterministic on the eval seed set.

### 4.7 Global state disclosure (per U7)
- The **QMIX mixer hypernetwork is allowed to access SMAX's global state** as in standard QMIX (Rashid et al.). This is **disclosed as an asymmetry** in the final report: MAPPO's centralized critic also uses global state, IPPO does not, VDN/IQL do not. Therefore the head-to-head QMIX-vs-MAPPO test is *symmetric* on global-state exploitation; the head-to-head against IPPO/VDN/IQL is *asymmetric in QMIX's favor* and is the reason those ablations exist as family-context, not as head-to-head.

---

## 5. Controls

### 5.1 Seeds (U3)
- Headline: **5 seeds per (algorithm × map)**, fixed seed set published in the design document.
- If any run exceeds a documented runtime threshold (declared in the design as "PLANNED BUDGET CAP, NOT MEASURED"), reduce it to **3 seeds** and add the run to a per-run **SeedFloorRunLog** table that records: which run fell to 3 seeds, what its actual wall-clock was, and which statistical-analysis pools it is excluded from.
- Eval seeds are a separate, published set and are *not* reused for training.

### 5.2 Hardware (U4)
- **One machine per campaign**; one JAX backend per run (`jax` with platform string pinned at run start), one process layout (no distributed).
- If a GPU is available: declare GPU model, VRAM, CUDA/cuDNN version, JAX build SHA. **Per-run metadata records `jax.devices()` and the platform string.**
- If only CPU: pin to the visible 24 vCPU budget, set `XLA_FLAGS` to disable thread pool oversubscription, and use `jax_platforms=cpu`.
- **No claim of measured wall-clock.** Runtime figures in §9 are *projected ranges*, explicitly unverified.

### 5.3 Eval protocol
- Fixed eval seed set of 32 seeds, distinct from training seeds.
- Deterministic policy (argmax for categorical Q-Learning; mean action for PPO stochastic policies).
- 32 episodes per checkpoint ⇒ confidence intervals reported with at least 32-sample normality-safe bootstrap.

### 5.4 Per-run overrides table headers
- **(run_id, map, algorithm, seed, train_env_steps, eval_seed_set, jax_backend, device_count, pinned_config_sha, deviations, jax_build_sha, run_started_utc, run_ended_utc, wallclock_seconds, normalized_score_final, AUC_env_steps, time_to_0p6, time_to_0p7, time_to_0p8)**.
- The "deviations" column is empty unless U8 forecloses-by-default; any non-empty entry triggers a per-deviation note.

---

## 6. Measurement protocols

### 6.1 Normalized score (per episode, per map)
- Compute **score_random** = mean ± 95% CI of episode return under a uniform-random policy over 32 eval seeds (per map).
- Compute **score_expert** as the larger of: (a) the JaxMARL paper's published best normalized score for that map, or (b) the best score achieved by **any** of our runs for that map (including un-run failures discounted). Apply *the same `score_expert`* to both PPO and QMIX (and ablations) — no asymmetric normalization is permitted.
- `normalized_score(τ) = (score(τ) − score_random) / (score_expert − score_random)`, clipped to [0, 1] for reporting (clipping only for display, not for statistical tests).
- `AUC_env_steps` = ∫ normalized_score d(env_step) / (final eval time × env_step_normalization).

### 6.2 Training-time metrics
- **Wall-clock seconds to first reach 0.8·*score_expert*** (primary): linear interpolation between the first checkpoint ≥ 0.8 and the immediately preceding checkpoint; interval mid-point reported as `time_to_0p8`.
- **Same for 0.6 and 0.7** (sensitivity sweep per U6); reported alongside.
- **Env steps to threshold** computed identically between the same two checkpoints; interval mid-point reported.
- **Per-step wall-clock** = total training wall-clock / total env steps (μs/env-step figure).
- **Total wall-clock to budget cap** — reported but not the primary metric.

### 6.3 Eval cadence & checkpoints
- Fixed: 32 episodes × every 10,000 env steps ⇒ ~200 checkpoints per headline run.
- An optional extension run exists per map at 5×10⁶ env steps for 3s_vs_5z/5m_vs_6m only (per U5). Checkpoint policy scales to match.

---

## 7. Statistical analysis plan (U9)

### 7.1 Per-map analysis
For each map and each metric M ∈ {final normalized score, env-steps-to-0.8, wallclock-to-0.8, AUC}:
- Compute per-seed scalar `M_{arm, s}`.
- Compute per-seed delta `ΔM_s = M_{MAPPO, s} − M_{QMIX, s}` (sign convention: positive Δ means MAPPO is better *in the metric's preferred direction*; direction is declared at the top of the results table).
- **Wilcoxon signed-rank test** on ΔM_s, exact permutation distribution when n=5 seeds.
- **Bootstrap CI**: 10,000 resamples of (run_id, not seed) with replacement; report 95% percentile interval; this is in addition to the Wilcoxon test, never a substitute.

### 7.2 Aggregate analysis
- Pool per-seed deltas across maps and run a Wilcoxon signed-rank + bootstrap on the pooled set; declare stratification by map as a robustness check.
- Aggregate effect size: Hodges–Lehmann estimator at the pooled level.

### 7.3 Correction and reporting
- **Holm–Bonferroni** is applied across the family of headline metrics: {final normalized score, time-to-0.8, steps-to-0.8, AUC}. Each comparison reports (p_raw, p_adjusted, CI_95).
- Any *secondary* sensitivity-sweep metrics (time-to-0.6, time-to-0.7) are *not* included in the Holm family to avoid double-counting; they are reported as supplementary sweep without confirmatory language.

### 7.4 Reporting artifacts (U9)
- **One learning-curve figure per map per metric**: 3 maps × 2 metrics (normalized score vs env-step; wallclock-to-threshold bar plot) = 6 figures. Each curve is mean ± 95% bootstrap CI across seeds. Wallclock-to-threshold bar plot is one figure *per metric per map*, replicated.
- **One aggregate results table per metric**: rows = (algorithm × map), columns = (mean_estimate, 95% CI, Δ vs MAPPO if applicable, p_raw, p_adjusted).
- **One summary paragraph**: pre-registered indirect-effect summary, hypothesis-by-hypothesis yes/no/indeterminate, with explicit reveal of which SeedFloorRunLog entries limited power.

---

## 8. Ablations table

| Ablation | Variates | Held constant | What it identifies | Mandatory? |
|----------|----------|---------------|--------------------|------------|
| IPPO ↔ MAPPO | Centralized critic present/absent | Body, env, seeds, eval | Centralized-critic contribution to PPO (H4) | **Yes** |
| IQL ↔ VDN ↔ QMIX | Mixing mechanic (none / additive / monotonic-hypernet) | Body, env, seeds, eval | Credit-assignment contribution inside Q-Learning (H5) | **Yes** |
| GRU on/off (applied to both arms) | Recurrence | Body, env, seeds, eval, episode length | Sample-efficiency vs throughput trade-off and direct effect on headline (H6) | Optional, only if budget allows |
| Optional: state-stripped QMIX (U7) | Global-state access prohibited in mixer hypernet | Body, env, seeds, eval, hypernet architectural params untouched | Net state-conditioning contribution to QMIX | **Optional**, only "if space allows" per U7 |
| Optional: 5×10⁶ env-step extension on 3s_vs_5z & 5m_vs_6m (U5) | Env-step budget | All else | Plateau behavior on harder maps (H1 robustness) | Optional, gated on smoke test |
| Reward-shape sensitivity | Turn off shaped component for one map × MAPPO × QMIX | All else | Score fragility to reward signal | **Optional** |

---

## 9. Feasibility / cost estimate

> **All runtimes below are PROJECTED RANGES, NOT MEASURED. They are placeholders for budget planning only.**

### 9.1 Run matrix (headline)
Each row is a (algorithm × map) cell × 5 seeds ⇒ each cell = 5 runs.

| Map | MAPPO | QMIX | IPPO (abl.) | VDN (abl.) | IQL (abl.) | Cell subtotal |
|-----|-------|------|-------------|------------|------------|---------------|
| 3m | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 25 |
| 3s_vs_5z | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 25 |
| 5m_vs_6m | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 25 |
| **Total** | **15** | **15** | **15** | **15** | **15** | **75 runs** |

### 9.2 Per-run projected wall-clock envelope (2×10⁶ env steps)

| Backend | Map | Projected range per run (NOT MEASURED) |
|---------|-----|----------------------------------------|
| GPU (e.g., A100-40GB) | 3m | TBD_estimate_low .. TBD_estimate_high |
| GPU (e.g., A100-40GB) | 3s_vs_5z | TBD_estimate_low .. TBD_estimate_high |
| GPU (e.g., A100-40GB) | 5m_vs_6m | TBD_estimate_low .. TBD_estimate_high |
| CPU (24 vCPU, JAX CPU backend) | 3m | TBD_estimate_low_C .. TBD_estimate_high_C |
| CPU (24 vCPU, JAX CPU backend) | 3s_vs_5z | TBD_estimate_low_C .. TBD_estimate_high_C |
| CPU (24 vCPU, JAX CPU backend) | 5m_vs_6m | TBD_estimate_low_C .. TBD_estimate_high_C |

The actual placeholder numbers are *not* inserted here because the design brief explicitly forbids stating runtimes. **At execution time the implementer fills in TBD_estimate_* from a 30-minute smoke run on each (backend, map) combo before scaling to the full 5-seed matrix.**

### 9.3 Aggregate cost envelope (2×10⁶ step headline only)

- **Total headline runs**: 75.
- **Total headline env steps**: 75 × 2×10⁶ = 1.5×10⁸ env steps.
- **Total headline wall-clock**: 75 × "single-run projected range" ⇒ generated at execution time only.
- **Optional extensions**: ≤ +10 to +20 runs (5×10⁶-step extension on harder maps × 2 algorithms × 5 seeds, subject to budget).
- **Optional state-stripped QMIX** (U7): ≤ +9 runs.
- **Random-baseline runs**: 3 maps × 5 seeds × 32 episodes ⇒ negligible.

### 9.4 Compute environment (U4)
- One fixed machine per campaign; visible 24 vCPU.
- Run table records `jax_platforms` and `len(jax.devices())` per row.
- No multi-machine distributed training; no implicit scale-out.

### 9.5 Storage & logging footprint
- Per run: per-checkpoint eval return + per-episode normalized score + metadata ≈ low single-digit MB → aggregate of order GB; final storage footprint to be measured at execution, not claimed here.

---

## 10. Threats to validity

1. **Family asymmetry in CTDE access (U7).** QMIX and MAPPO both see global state during training; IPPO, VDN, IQL do not. Head-to-head comparisons of *asymmetric* pairs are biased in the global-state-accessor's favor. **Mitigation**: report the head-to-head PPO-vs-QMIX as the headline (symmetric), label any *cross-family* claim with this caveat, and log an optional state-stripped QMIX if budget allows.
2. **Hardware normalization (U4).** Wall-clock is only meaningful on a fixed backend with a fixed device count. **Mitigation**: env-step-to-threshold is the hardware-portable secondary metric; per-run metadata pins both `jax_platforms` and device count.
3. **Expert-score provenance.** Whether `score_expert` is JaxMARL-paper published or self-observed changes the absolute reading of normalized scores. **Mitigation**: declare which one, freeze the choice, apply identically to both arms, and report both normalized and raw return in the supplementary table.
4. **Hyperparameter pinning vs. re-tuning (U8).** Verbatim-pinned configs may favor one family if not jointly tuned. **Mitigation**: deviations table is mandatory and any deviation is conservatively treated as a known confound; no re-tuning in the headline comparison.
5. **Seed-floor collapses (U3).** If any run falls back from 5 to 3 seeds, power is materially reduced. **Mitigation**: SeedFloorRunLog names the affected runs; affected cells are excluded from headline Holm testing and reported with a power caveat.
6. **Curriculum / map difficulty ceiling.** On 5m_vs_6m, both algorithms may fail to reach 0.8·*score_expert* even at 5×10⁶ steps. **Mitigation**: report "did not reach" as a censored observation rather than capping; use Tobit-style interpolation on the time-to-threshold metric with explicit handling of non-events.
7. **GPU vs. CPU scaling discontinuity.** Some MARL implementations have non-monotonic throughput on CPU large-batch JIT. **Mitigation**: declare backend once, do not cross-compare CPU and GPU results.
8. **JAX non-determinism.** Despite `jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", False)` and seeded PRNGKeys, JAX's asynchronous dispatch and per-device ordering can introduce non-determinism. **Mitigation**: seed every PRNGKey explicitly, record `JAX_PRNG_KEYSET_SHA`, and report seed sensitivity in the supplementary appendix.
9. **Implementation version drift.** JaxMARL is under active development; minor API changes could break pinning. **Mitigation**: the pinned `algorithms/smax/{...}` SHA at the top of the overrides table is the single source of truth; deviations are the most-common expected event and are logged not hidden.
10. **Generalization beyond SMAX.** The same conclusion may not transfer to other JaxMARL environments (MPE, Overcooked, etc.). **Mitigation**: explicitly out of scope of this design and not claimed.

---

## 11. Reproducibility checklist

Every run produces a self-describing artifact. The header of each per-run log file must contain:

- [ ] `run_id` (unique)
- [ ] `algorithm` ∈ {MAPPO, IPPO, QMIX, VDN, IQL}
- [ ] `map` ∈ {3m, 3s_vs_5z, 5m_vs_6m}
- [ ] `seed_train`, `seed_eval_set`
- [ ] `jax_version`, `jax_platforms`, `jaxlib_version`
- [ ] `cuda_version_if_any`, `libtpu_version_if_any`
- [ ] `devices_count`, `device_kind`
- [ ] `jax_pinned_config_sha`, `jaxmarl_repo_sha`, `jaxmarl_config_filename`
- [ ] `numpy_seed_root`, `python_hash_seed`
- [ ] `git_status_dirty` (bool), `docker_image_or_venv_spec_sha`
- [ ] `commit_message_of_pinned_config`
- [ ] Per-checkpoint: `(env_step, wallclock_seconds, eval_return, normalized_score, eval_seed_batch_id)`
- [ ] Per-run aggregate scalars: `final_normalized_score`, `AUC_env_steps`, `time_to_0p6`, `time_to_0p7`, `time_to_0p8` (each with "reached" boolean if censored)
- [ ] Empty `deviations` list if no overrides; otherwise per-deviation (replaced, by, reason, observed_directional_effect)
- [ ] `SeedFloorRunLog` flag if applicable (true ⇒ only 3 seeds; declares reduced statistical power)

A separate **campaign-level summary file** aggregates: campaign_id, machine_id (without PII), backend declaration, jaxmarl_repo_sha, list of run_ids, count of SeedFloor runs, count of deviated runs, count of censored time-to-threshold runs.

A **single summary paragraph** in the final report answers the four research questions:

1. Does MAPPO match QMIX in final normalized score on SMAX? *(H1 yes/no)*
2. Does QMIX reach 0.8·*score_expert* in fewer wall-clock seconds than MAPPO? *(H2 yes/no)*
3. Does QMIX do so in fewer environment steps? *(H3 yes/no)*
4. How much of the answer is attributable to (a) centralized critic, (b) mixing, (c) recurrence, (d) global-state access? *(H4–H6 filled)*

The final paragraph is reviewed against the SeedFloorRunLog and the deviations table **before publication** so any reduced-power or revised-hyperparameter caveat is in the same sentence as the claim it qualifies.

---

## Pre-registered lock-ins (re-statement for implementer hand-off)

- **Primary comparison arms**: MAPPO and QMIX.
- **Ablation arms**: IPPO, VDN, IQL.
- **Maps**: 3m, 3s_vs_5z, 5m_vs_6m.
- **Headline seeds**: 5 (3 absolute floor under documented seed-floor policy).
- **Headline env-step budget**: 2×10⁶; optional 5×10⁶ on harder maps gated by smoke test.
- **Primary training-time metric**: wallclock-to-0.8·*score_expert*; sweep at 0.6/0.7/0.8.
- **Pinned JaxMARL configs**: `algorithms/smax/{ippo,mappo,qmix,vdn,iql}` verbatim.
- **Hardware**: one machine per campaign, one JAX backend, 24 vCPU visible, per-run metadata reports backend + device count.
- **No claim** of an executed experiment or measured runtime.
- **Statistical reporting**: Wilcoxon signed-rank + bootstrap CI on per-seed deltas (PPO − QMIX); Holm-Bonferroni across headline metrics; one learning-curve per (map, metric), one results table per metric, one summary paragraph.

**Algorithm arms**
- **PPO arm:** IPPO (Independent PPO) as the JaxMARL-canonical on-policy baseline. (MAPPO exists but adds a centralized-critic trick — I would exclude unless the researcher requests it, to keep the comparison a clean on-policy vs. independent off-policy contrast.)
- **Q-Learning arm:** three JaxMARL candidates — **IQL**, **VDN**, **QMIX**. I recommend starting with **IQL** (cleanest independent-Q counterpart to IPPO) and, if budget allows, adding **QMIX** (strongest value-decomposition baseline). VDN sits between them and adds little on this question.

**Maps / scenarios**
- Default proposal: **3 small SMAX maps spanning easy / asymmetric / hard** — e.g. `3m` (easy symmetric), `2s_vs_1z` (asymmetric), `3s_vs_5z` or `5m_vs_6m` (hard). With the supplied budget three maps is already aggressive; happy to drop to 1–2 maps.

**Operationalization of training time**
- Wall-clock total to a fixed env-step budget (e.g. a few × 10⁶ env steps, to be sized to budget).
- Wall-clock per 10⁶ env steps (throughput).
- **Env-steps-to-threshold** (e.g. to reach normalized score = 0.5 and 0.8).
- **Wall-clock-to-threshold** (user-facing; differs from steps-to-threshold if env throughput differs between algorithms).
- JIT-compile cost is excluded / logged separately so it does not bias comparison.

**Operationalization of normalized score**
- Anchor: `(score − random) / (expert − random)`, clipped to `[0, 1]`.
- Report learning curves vs. **env-step x-axis** AND vs. **wall-clock x-axis** (they answer different questions).
- Report final-step normalized score; report steps-to-0.5 and steps-to-0.8 where reachable; otherwise explicitly state "neither algorithm reached threshold within budget" and report best-reached value.

**Seeds / replicates**
- Default **3 seeds per (algorithm × map) cell**, raised to 5 if budget allows. The tiny `question_budget=6` / `actor_step_budget=60` figure means I expect 3 seeds × {IPPO, Q-arm} × 3 maps = 18 runs is the upper bound; trimming to 1–2 maps and/or 2 Q-Learning arms is the first lever to pull.

**Controls / confound isolation**
- Identical across both arms: SMAX env wrapper (guaranteed by JaxMARL), MLP backbone + hidden size, discount γ, parallel actor count, total env-step budget, hardware (single 24-CPU machine), parameter sharing setting, random-seed discipline.
- Intentionally different (algorithm-intrinsic, not bugs): replay buffer / target-net cadence / ε-schedule for Q-Learning; GAE λ / clip ε / update epochs / entropy coef for IPPO.
- Flagged confounds:
  - JaxMARL's `vmap`-batched environment favors large GPU/TPU batches; on **CPU-only** the relative throughput advantage seen in the paper may not reproduce — must report hardware prominently and treat relative wall-clock claims as CPU-specific.
  - JIT warm-up time — logged and excluded.
  - Q-Learning variants in JaxMARL ship PyMARL-style replay defaults that differ from IPPO defaults; these are algorithm-intrinsic, not removed.

**Feasibility-aware analysis plan**
- Per cell: mean and IQR across seeds; shaded-band learning curves.
- Per map: Welch's t-test (or Mann-Whitney U if non-Gaussian) on final normalized score and on steps-to-threshold; multiple-comparison correction across maps (Holm if 3 maps).
- Variance reporting: 95% CI on the mean + inter-seed min/max.
- If budget is exhausted before either algorithm converges on a hard map: compare at the latest common env-step and report an explicit "did-not-converge" call rather than overclaiming.
- Two x-axis conventions are non-negotiable: env steps and wall-clock. Reporting only one of them is a known failure mode for this kind of comparison.

## (3) Consequential Assumptions and Uncertainties

**Stated assumptions (would be locked into the full design unless the researcher objects)**
- Q-Learning identity = **IQL** primary, **QMIX** optional second arm. VDN dropped unless asked.
- On-policy identity = **IPPO** (not MAPPO).
- Normalization anchors = SMAX **random-policy floor** and a published **expert ceiling** (mix of SMAX heuristic-AI baseline + widely-cited SMAC numbers as a sensitivity check); floor and ceiling values to be re-verified against the paper at execution time.
- Map set = {`3m`, `2s_vs_1z`, `3s_vs_5z` or `5m_vs_6m`}, trimmed to 1–2 if budget forces it.
- Identical MLP backbone, identical γ, identical parallel actor count across arms.
- Hardware = the provided 24-CPU, no-GPU box; this is reported, not normalized toward paper claims.
- Use of JaxMARL registered defaults for algorithm-extrinsic hyperparameters, unless the researcher overrides.
- Parameter sharing = **on for both arms** (default in JaxMARL; if off, must be held constant across arms).

**Open uncertainties for the researcher to resolve before I write the full design**
1. **Which Q-Learning?** IQL only, IQL+QMIX, or all three (IQL/VDN/QMIX)?
2. **Which SMAX maps**, and how many? My default is 3 small maps; budget may force fewer.
3. **Normalization ceiling anchor** — SMAX heuristic-AI, SMAC published numbers, or both as a sensitivity check?
4. **Budget interpretation** — is `actor_step_budget=60` literally 60 actor steps total (then we can do at most a handful of short runs and convergence is unlikely) or 60 minutes of actor time / a larger unit? This single number dominates feasibility.
5. **PPO flavor** — IPPO only, or include **MAPPO** as a second on-policy arm?
6. **Convergence criterion** — train to a fixed env-step budget, train until a normalized-score threshold, or both?
7. **Whether identical-defaults is acceptable** — strict "use JaxMARL defaults for each algorithm as a registered config" (cleanest for "JaxMARL's PPO vs Q-Learning") vs. hand-tuning both to a shared hyperparameter budget (cleaner scientific comparison but diverges from "as-shipped" framing).
8. **Should I plan to also report episode-level / step-level sample efficiency curves** in addition to final score, given the training-time framing?

I will not write the full experiment design until these are resolved.

(2) PROPUESTA DE ENFOQUE PRELIMINAR

(a) Algoritmos a comparar con su variante exacta en JaxMARL:
- PPO-JaxMARL: por defecto se proponen dos sub-condiciones, IPPO (Independent PPO, sin parameter sharing, cada agente con su propia red) y SPPO (Sharing PPO, parameter sharing entre agentes con ventaja centralizada). Estas representan las dos respuestas clasicas a la no-estacionariedad. La inclusion simultanea evita atribuir un sesgo a un esquema de comparticion en concreto.
- Q-Learning-JaxMARL: por defecto IQL con parameter sharing; si el repositorio expone VDN o QMIX, queda ABIERTO incluyirlos como variante alternativa. La eleccion final dependera de la disponibilidad efectivamente documentada en JaxMARL al momento del design-review.
- Inclusion justificada: PPO y Q-Learning representan las dos familias dominantes en MARL (policy-gradient frente a value-based).

(b) Mapas SMAX y criterio:
- Mapa facil (simetrico, pocos agentes): 3m (3 Marines vs 3 Marines).
- Mapa medio (simetrico, escala mayor): 8m (8 Marines vs 8 Marines).
- Mapa asimetrico (heterogeneidad de tipo o numero): 2s_vs_1sc (2 Stalkers vs 1 Spine Crawler; ventaja numerica aliada) y, si el presupuesto lo permite, 3s_vs_5z (3 Stalkers vs 5 Zealots; desventaja numerica aliada frente a heterogeneidad enemiga).
- Criterio: cubrir gradiente de dificultad, equilibrio frente a asimetria, escala de equipo y heterogeneidad de tipo de unidad. Cuatro mapas mantienen potencia estadistica razonable sin exceder el presupuesto.
- ABIERTO: reduccion a 3 mapas o ampliacion, segun decision del equipo.

(c) Metricas operativas:
- Tiempo de pared total por corrida (segundos), registrado por update.
- Tiempo-hasta-umbral: segundos y pasos de entorno hasta alcanzar norm_score igual o mayor que 0.9 sobre ventana movil de 100 episodios. Secundario: 0.8.
- Pasos de entorno totales (environment steps) por corrida; 2M como ancla propuesta (ABIERTO).
- FPS/IPS agregados por corrida y por fase (rollout vs update).
- Retorno medio por episodio en ventana movil de 100 episodios.
- Win-rate en ventana movil de 100 episodios cuando el entorno lo exponga.
- Puntaje normalizado propuesto: norm_score = (mean_return - baseline_return) / (max_return - baseline_return); baseline_return = retorno de politica aleatoria por mapa; max_return = techo observado. Forma final ABIERTA.

(d) Semillas:
- N igual o mayor que 5 semillas distintas por condicion (algoritmo x mapa x variante). Minimo recomendado: 5. Justificacion: la varianza tipica de MARL en SMAX es alta; con N=5, una prueba no parametrica tipo Wilcoxon tiene potencia razonable para detectar diferencias medianas a grandes y el IC95% bootstrap es estable. Si el presupuesto permite, N=10 mejora la precision.

(e) Criterio de parada:
- Primario (ancla): presupuesto fijo de 2M environment steps totales por corrida, independiente del algoritmo, para hacer wall-clock comparable.
- Secundario: convergencia — 50 evaluaciones consecutivas sin mejora del norm_score medio en ventana movil de 100 episodios; opcionalmente paro si norm_score igual o mayor que 0.95 en 5 evaluaciones consecutivas.

(f) Hiperparametros compartidos y especificos:
- Compartidos entre PPO y Q-Learning: learning_rate (mismo optimizador y schedule), gamma (descuento), grad_clip (norma del gradiente), arquitectura (MLP dos capas ocultas 64 unidades, activacion tanh), semillas de entorno y de buffer, y tamano de batch cuando sea tecnicamente posible.
- Especificos PPO (justicia): clip_eps, ent_coef, vf_coef, train_iters, num_minibatches, epochs.
- Especificos Q-Learning (justicia): epsilon o politica de exploracion, target network update interval, replay buffer size, gradient steps por environment step, tau (si usa soft updates).
- Justificacion: lo compartido evita que diferencias provengan de choices ajenos al algoritmo; lo especifico refleja componentes intrinsecos de cada familia y por tanto es justo afinarlos por separado.

(g) Manejo de no-estacionariedad multi-agente:
- IPPO: cada agente aprende en presencia de los demas como entorno; los otros forman parte de la dinamica no-estacionaria.
- SPPO: parameter sharing entre agentes; red compartida con ventaja centralizada (CTDE parcial).
- IQL: parameter sharing con valor Q individual por agente y red compartida; mixing opcional.
- VDN/QMIX: descomposicion del valor conjunto con mixing network centralizada, CTDE puro.
- Justificacion: comparar IPPO/SPPO frente a IQL/VDN/QMIX permite observar como cada familia responde a la no-estacionariedad inherente del micromanejo en SMAX.

(h) Plan de analisis estadistico preliminar:
- Descriptivo: media, desviacion estandar, mediana e IQR por mapa y por condicion; IC95% bootstrap (10k muestras) sobre la media.
- Comparacion pairwise por mapa: Wilcoxon signed-rank si semillas apareadas (mismo seed entre algoritmos) o Mann-Whitney U si independientes; eleccion segun presencia de pareo. Justificacion: distribucion esperada no normal; N pequena.
- Correccion por comparaciones multiples sobre los 4 mapas: Holm-Bonferroni.
- Tamano de efecto: Cliff delta o rank-biserial.
- Visualizacion: curvas norm_score-vs-steps y norm_score-vs-wall-clock por mapa; tabla resumen con p-valores ajustados y tamano de efecto.

DOCUMENTO DE DISEÑO EXPERIMENTAL
Titulo: Comparacion de PPO y Q-Learning de JaxMARL en SMAX: eficiencia de entrenamiento y puntaje normalizado

(a) TITULO Y RESUMEN EJECUTIVO

Este documento presenta el diseño de un experimento comparativo entre las variantes de PPO provistas por JaxMARL (IPPO y SPPO) y una variante de Q-Learning (IQL por defecto, con VDN/QMIX sujetos a disponibilidad documentada) sobre cuatro mapas de SMAX que cubren un gradiente de dificultad y equilibrio frente a asimetría (3m facil, 8m medio, 2s_vs_1sc asimetrico, 3s_vs_5z asimetrico). El objetivo es caracterizar dos ejes de comparacion: (i) tiempo de entrenamiento hasta un umbral de desempeno predefinido y (ii) puntaje normalizado final, bajo un ancla comun de 2 millones de pasos de entorno por corrida. La entrega se limita al diseno en si, sin ejecucion, sin simulaciones y sin resultados numericos fabricados; la red esta deshabilitada por el track.md, las dependencias no estan preinstaladas (jax y jaxmarl no se encuentran en el runtime) y el repositorio /workspace no contiene codigo fuente, por lo que cualquier validacion empirica queda fuera del alcance de esta entrega.

(b) RACIONAL DEL DISEÑO, ANCLADO A FACT_IDS

El estudio responde a la pregunta declarada en /workspace/task.json y en el fact_id neurips2024/97649/0:setup_2, que establece el objetivo comparativo PPO vs Q-Learning en SMAX con foco en eficiencia y desempeno. La eleccion de JaxMARL como entorno de implementacion se respalda en neurips2024/97649/0:setup_4, que define a JaxMARL como biblioteca JAX para MARL con paralelizacion a escala y aceleracion por GPU; en este diseno, dado que el runtime tiene gpu_enabled=false, se planifica una ejecucion en CPU 24 nucleos con paso a GPU solo cuando el equipo lo autorice. La eleccion de SMAX como banco de pruebas se respalda en neurips2024/97649/0:setup_12, que describe a SMAX como reimplementacion en JAX del StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge para micromanejo multi-agente.

Elecciones marcadas como SUPUESTOS ABIERTOS que requieren confirmacion explicita del equipo antes de ejecutar:
- Variante exacta de Q-Learning efectivamente disponible en el repositorio JaxMARL: IQL por defecto, VDN/QMIX como alternativas a confirmar.
- Inclusion simultanea de IPPO y SPPO o seleccion de una sola sub-condicion PPO.
- Conjunto final de mapas SMAX a evaluar.
- Numero de semillas por condicion (propuesto N>=5, ideal N=10).
- Presupuesto exacto de pasos de entorno por corrida (propuesto 2M como ancla).
- Forma final del puntaje normalizado y sus baselines.
- Politica de exploracion de Q-Learning y numero de episodios de evaluacion.
- Lista auditable final de hiperparametros.

(c) CONDICION EXPERIMENTAL COMPLETA

Factores y niveles:

Factor Algoritmo:
- Nivel PPO-IPPO: PPO independiente, cada agente con su propia red actor-critic, sin parameter sharing.
- Nivel PPO-SPPO: PPO con parameter sharing entre agentes y ventaja centralizada.
- Nivel QL-IQL: Independent Q-Learning con parameter sharing (nucleo de la comparacion).
- Nivel QL-VDN: Value Decomposition Network, suma lineal del valor (ABIERTO a disponibilidad documentada).
- Nivel QL-QMIX: Mixing network monotona (ABIERTO a disponibilidad documentada).

Factor Mapa SMAX:
- Nivel 3m: 3 Marines vs 3 Marines, simetrico, facil.
- Nivel 8m: 8 Marines vs 8 Marines, simetrico, medio.
- Nivel 2s_vs_1sc: 2 Stalkers vs 1 Spine Crawler, asimetrico en tipo y numero.
- Nivel 3s_vs_5z: 3 Stalkers vs 5 Zealots, asimetrico en tipo y desventaja numerica.

Factor Semilla: N>=5 semillas distintas por condicion; recomendado N=10 si presupuesto disponible. Se enumeran como s in {1,...,N}.

Factor Variante de no-estacionariedad:
- Nivel agentes-independientes (correspondiente a IPPO y a IQL sin sharing explícito de inputs).
- Nivel parameter-sharing (correspondiente a SPPO y a IQL con sharing).
- Nivel CTDE-con-mixing (correspondiente a VDN/QMIX, ABIERTO).

Tabla resumen de la poblacion de corridas minima:
- IPPO x 4 mapas x N semillas = 4N corridas.
- SPPO x 4 mapas x N semillas = 4N corridas.
- QL-IQL x 4 mapas x N semillas = 4N corridas.
- Opcional QL-VDN o QL-QMIX si disponibles, mismo tamano de celda.
Total minimo con N=5: 60 corridas; con SPPO agregado: 60 corridas; con VDN o QMIX agregados: 80 corridas por variante adicional.

(d) CONTROLES Y COMPARABILIDAD

Hiperparametros compartidos entre PPO y Q-Learning para fairness:
- learning_rate y schedule de learning rate.
- gamma (descuento).
- grad_clip (norma del gradiente).
- arquitectura de red: MLP con dos capas ocultas de 64 unidades y activacion tanh.
- semillas de entorno y de buffer de replay (cuando aplique).
- tamano de batch de actualizacion, cuando sea tecnicamente posible igualarlo entre algoritmos.

Hiperparametros especificos por algoritmo (fairness: reflejan componentes intrinsecos de cada familia, por tanto es justo afinarlos por separado):

Para PPO (tanto IPPO como SPPO):
- clip_eps: epsilon de clipping de PPO.
- ent_coef: coeficiente de bonus entropico.
- vf_coef: coeficiente de la perdida de la funcion de valor.
- gae_lambda: parametro de Generalized Advantage Estimation.
- train_iters: iteraciones de entrenamiento por rollout.
- num_minibatches: numero de mini-batches por iteracion.
- epochs: numero de pasadas por mini-batch.

Para Q-Learning (IQL por defecto; VDN/QMIX si disponibles):
- epsilon o politica de exploracion con su schedule de decaimiento.
- target network update interval (hard update) o tau (soft update).
- replay buffer size.
- gradient steps por environment step.
- para VDN/QMIX: arquitectura de la mixing network (profundidad y unidades), dado que es un componente estructural propio de la variante.

Justificacion de fairness: los compartidos controlan variables que afectan por igual a ambas familias en terminos de optimizacion y representacion; los especificos se permiten variar porque son pieza constitutiva del algoritmo y modificarlos supondria dejar de comparar PPO frente a Q-Learning en sentido estricto. Toda eleccion final se recogerá en una tabla de hiperparametros auditables previo a la ejecucion.

(e) PROTOCOLO DE ENTRENAMIENTO Y EVALUACION

- Ancla de presupuesto: 2 millones de environment steps totales por corrida, comunes a todos los algoritmos y mapas. Esto fija el esfuerzo computacional y permite comparacion de wall-clock.
- Criterio de parada secundario: convergencia operacionalizada como 50 evaluaciones consecutivas sin mejora del norm_score medio en ventana movil de 100 episodios.
- Cierre por saturacion (opcional): si norm_score alcanza 0.95 o mas en 5 evaluaciones consecutivas, se permite cierre temprano registrado como tal.
- Evaluacion determinista: cada 100k pasos, se ejecutan 10 episodios deterministas con semilla fija para reportar norm_score, win-rate y retorno medio en esa ventana.
- Ventana movil de desempeno: 100 episodios para retorno medio, win-rate y norm_score.
- Checkpoints: cada 100k pasos se persiste snapshot de pesos, optimizador y metricas agregadas, para permitir reanudar y analizar la curva de aprendizaje.
- Manejo de semillas: cada corrida se identifica con una semilla maestra s in {1,...,N}. A partir de s se derivan semillas hijas para entorno, buffer y pesos mediante un esquema deterministic splitting (por ejemplo s + offset hash) para garantizar reproducibilidad sin colision.

(f) METRICAS Y DEFINICION OPERATIVA DE PUNTAJE NORMALIZADO

Metricas de desempeno:
- Retorno medio por episodio en ventana movil de 100 episodios.
- Win-rate en ventana movil de 100 episodios, cuando el entorno lo exponga.
- norm_score por ventana (definicion abajo).

Metricas de eficiencia:
- wall_clock_total_seconds: tiempo de pared total de la corrida.
- wall_clock_time_to_threshold: segundos hasta alcanzar norm_score por encima del umbral (primario 0.9, secundario 0.8) en una ventana de los ultimos 100 episodios.
- environment_steps_to_threshold: pasos de entorno hasta el mismo umbral.
- IPS agregados por corrida y por fase (rollout y update por separado) para diagnosticar cuello de botella.
- FPS/IPS_por_agente como derivado, para inspeccion.

Definicion operativa de puntaje normalizado (SUPUESTO ABIERTO a confirmar):
norm_score(m, s) = (mean_return(m, s) - baseline_random(m)) / (max_return(m) - baseline_random(m))
donde:
- mean_return(m, s) es la media de retorno por episodio bajo la politica aprendida, en el mapa m y semilla s.
- baseline_random(m) es el retorno medio empirico de una politica uniforme/aleatoria en el mapa m, estimado con al menos 5 semillas independientes y 1 rollout completo por semilla.
- max_return(m) es el techo observado en una corrida corta de referencia o el maximo teorico documentado para el mapa m, lo que el equipo prefiera citar.
- Denominador acotado por epsilon positivo para evitar division por cero si baseline_random y max_return coinciden.
Forma final ABIERTA; alternativas aceptables incluyen win-rate como sustituto o normalizacion contra un baseline de literatura citado.

(g) ANALISIS ESTADISTICO

- Descriptivo por condicion (algoritmo x mapa): media, desviacion estandar, mediana e IQR de norm_score, wall_clock_total_seconds, wall_clock_time_to_threshold, IPS.
- IC95% bootstrap con 10k muestras sobre la media de cada metrica por condicion.
- Comparacion pairwise por mapa: Wilcoxon signed-rank si las semillas estan apareadas entre algoritmos (mismo seed s asignado a ambas condiciones); Mann-Whitney U si son independientes. La decision se hara en funcion del esquema final de semillas.
- Correccion por comparaciones multiples sobre los 4 mapas: Holm-Bonferroni.
- Tamano de efecto: Cliff delta (alternativa rank-biserial si se prefiere paramétrico).
- Visualizaciones:
  * Curvas norm_score-vs-steps y norm_score-vs-wall-clock por mapa, una figura por mapa con todos los algoritmos en la misma grafica.
  * Boxplots de wall_clock_time_to_threshold y de norm_score final por mapa.
  * Tabla resumen por mapa con p-valor ajustado, Cliff delta y estadisticos descriptivos.

(h) FACTIBILIDAD Y RESTRICCIONES DE ENTORNO

Restricciones del runtime declaradas en el track.md anexo a /workspace/task.json:
- CPU de 24 nucleos disponible (verificado: nproc reporta 24).
- GPU deshabilitada por la metadata del entorno (gpu_enabled=false).
- Red deshabilitada (network=disabled).
- Dependencias no preinstaladas (jax, jaxmarl y numpy ausentes en el runtime, verificado).
- Repositorio /workspace contiene unicamente /workspace/task.json; no se clonea ni se descarga nada en esta fase de diseno.

Nota de factibilidad sobre orden de magnitud de wall-clock: a titulo estrictamente indicativo y claramente etiquetado como estimativa pendiente de validacion, una corrida de 2M pasos en CPU con JAX es plausiblemente del orden de horas por condicion (por ejemplo decenas de horas para mapas pequenos y posiblemente dias para mapas asimetricos de mayor escala), pero este rango no se reporta como resultado empírico, se anota como cota de planificacion que el equipo debera validar con una corrida piloto corta en hardware autorizado antes de confirmar el tamano poblacional.

(i) LISTA FINAL DE PREGUNTAS PENDIENTES PARA EL EQUIPO

1. Confirmar que el repositorio JaxMARL efectivamente expone IPPO, SPPO e IQL; en caso afirmativo, indicar si VDN y QMIX tambien estan disponibles para inclusion como variantes alternativas de Q-Learning.
2. Confirmar inclusion simultanea de IPPO y SPPO como sub-condiciones de PPO, o seleccionar una.
3. Confirmar el conjunto final de mapas SMAX: el propuesto es {3m, 8m, 2s_vs_1sc, 3s_vs_5z}; cualquier ampliacion o reduccion debe decidirse aqui.
4. Confirmar numero de semillas por condicion: propuesto N>=5, ideal N=10 si presupuesto lo permite.
5. Confirmar el presupuesto de pasos por corrida: propuesto 2M como ancla.
6. Confirmar la definicion operativa del puntaje normalizado, incluyendo la forma de estimar baseline_random(m) y la fuente de max_return(m).
7. Confirmar politica de exploracion de Q-Learning (epsilon-greedy con decaimiento por defecto) y numero exacto de episodios de evaluacion deterministas por checkpoint.
8. Confirmar la lista auditable de hiperparametros compartidos y especificos, especialmente gae_lambda (compartido por convencion pero no obligatorio en Q-Learning), target update interval y replay buffer size.
9. Confirmar umbrales de tiempo-hasta-umbral (0.8 secundario, 0.9 primario) o ajustar.
10. Confirmar si el diseno debe ejecutarse exclusivamente en CPU o si se autoriza una corrida posterior en GPU para reportar tiempo absoluto, dado que neurips2024/97649/0:setup_4 senala aceleracion por GPU como capacidad de JaxMARL.
11. Confirmar si existe contenido adicional en project_brief, submission_contract o study_context que deba incorporarse y que no esta adjunto a /workspace/task.json.

FIN DEL DOCUMENTO DE DISEÑO
Esta entrega se limita al documento de diseno. No se reportan corridas, no se inventan curvas, no se citan metricas agregadas de papers ni resultados numericos no presentes en /workspace/task.json o en los fact_ids neurips2024/97649/0:setup_2, setup_4 y setup_12.

## (1) Workspace check and external dependencies

**Supplied inputs actually present in `/workspace`**
- `task.json` only. It contains: the research question, the context sentence "Design an experiment that answers the question...", a `documents.track.md` field whose literal value is `"Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."`, and no other reference material.
- No `track.md` file exists on disk; no JaxMARL/SMAX/JAX/RL source, configs, seeds, or prior runs are present.

**External reference types the design will likely rely on, conditional on design-only intent and approval**
| Source type | Role in the design | Status |
|---|---|---|
| JaxMARL public documentation / paper | Confirms env API surface, observation/action spaces, default episode terminations, default agent groupings for SMAX maps; supplies the canonical PPO baseline config that PPO runs mirror. | **Proposer-assumed**: existence only is claimed; no in-context copy is available to verify specific names/defaults. Researcher confirmation needed. |
| SMAX environment spec (paper / JaxMARL docs) | Identifies which maps (e.g., 3m, 8m, 2s_vs_1sc) are available, agent counts, episode horizons, reward structure needed to define a sensible "normalized score" denominator. | **Proposer-assumed**: existence is general knowledge; specific map list and reward ranges are not verified here. |
| MARL PPO convention references (e.g., MAPPO / IPPO writeups used by JaxMARL) | Cross-check for matched-shared-variable policy (clip ratio, GAE, minibatch/epochs, entropy coeff., value loss coeff., optimizer/schedule). | **Proposer-assumed**. |
| Q-Learning conventions in MARL (IQL vs. value-decomposition VDN/QMIX) | Determines *which* Q-Learning family is being compared against PPO — these are structurally different algorithms, so the choice materially changes the comparison. JaxMARL ships both, so the choice is treated as a researcher decision. | **Proposer-assumed**: needs explicit researcher choice. |
| Statistical comparison references (paired tests across seeds, bootstrap CIs, Wilcoxon) | Justifies the analysis plan only; no in-workspace copy relied upon. | **Proposer-assumed for methodology**; no document support. |

I will not treat any spec, default hyperparameter, or numerical constant as "confirmed" until the researcher supplies or approves it.

## (2) High-level proposed-approach framework (directional only — not final design)

1. **Operational decomposition of the research question.** Split the headline question into four sub-claims, each tied to a measurable quantity on SMAX: (i) does PPO reach a higher asymptotic normalized score than Q-Learning; (ii) does PPO reach a given score threshold in fewer environment steps; (iii) which algorithm has lower wall-clock training time to a fixed score threshold; (iv) is the ranking consistent across SAX maps of differing agent counts, and if not, where does it flip. Each sub-claim is answerable with the same run matrix but different summary statistics.
2. **Controlled (algorithm-specific) vs. shared variables.** *Shared*: total environment-step budget per run, number of independent seeds, SMAX map, episode horizon, observation/action interface, network capacity/order, optimizer family and learning-rate schedule family, evaluation protocol, random-seed spacing. *Algorithm-specific (deliberately varied)*: update rule (PPO clipped surrogate vs. Q-Learning temporal-difference target), value-head vs. Q-head loss, replay buffer/GAE storage, off-policy vs. on-policy sample reuse. Hyperparameter *fairness* will be defined as equal environment-step budget and equal network capacity, not equal hyperparameter count.
3. **Measurement of training time and normalized score.** *Training time* logged three ways to disambiguate: (a) wall-clock seconds to a fixed score threshold, (b) environment steps to threshold, (c) gradient/actor updates to threshold. *Normalized score*: episode return divided by a map-specific reference (proposal: per-map best-of-baselines or a published SMAX reference return), reported as a percentage; reporting will explicitly state which reference value is used and why it is appropriate. Time-to-threshold is reported conditional on the threshold being reached at all within the budget.
4. **Control groups and random-seed strategy.** Three run arms per SMAX map: PPO (JaxMARL canonical config, params to be confirmed), Q-Learning (sub-family to be chosen), and a trivial control (e.g., random-policy or scripted heuristic acting from the same observation interface) to sanity-check that the evaluation pipeline discriminates signal from noise. Seed strategy: ≥ 5 seeds per arm (researcher-confirmable), seeds drawn from a single RNG stream with fixed stride so all arms share a baseline seed schedule; pairing seeds across arms enables paired statistical tests.
5. **Initial feasibility and resource/compute assessment.** Directional estimate: with network disabled and no GPU, this sandbox cannot execute runs — the design stage itself is feasible here, but actual training would require an environment with network access (to fetch `jax`, `jaxmarl`, `flashbax`) and a JAX-capable accelerator (GPU/TPU) for acceptable wall-clock; CPU-only is feasible for short SMAX maps and small seed counts but is expected to be slow. The plan therefore treats execution as out of scope for this design-only task and budgets only for the design artifacts.
6. **Analysis and statistical methods.** Per sub-claim: report median and interquartile range across seeds; use paired tests across seed-pairs (Wilcoxon signed-rank for n=5, paired-bootstrap CIs otherwise) rather than independent-samples tests; pre-register the threshold for "reached"; visually compare learning curves with shaded seed-variance bands; if a sub-claim cannot be answered because neither arm reaches threshold within budget, report that as a distinguishable outcome rather than as missing data.

## (3) Key assumptions and uncertainties, ranked by importance

Each item is tagged **D** (document/context-supported) or **P** (proposer-assumed). Higher items matter more for design correctness.

1. [P] **The "Q-Learning" arm uses a specific MARL sub-family (IQL independent learners vs. value-decomposition VDN/QMIX vs. centralized-training-decentralized-execution variants).** This is a category-level decision that changes what the comparison actually means. *Needs explicit researcher choice before main design.*
2. [D-from `task.json`] **The task is design-only; the sandbox cannot execute real training runs.** All quantitative claims in the result artifact will be design-stage projections/placeholders, not measured numbers.
3. [P] **The set of SMAX maps to include (e.g., homogeneous 3m/8m vs. heterogeneous 2s_vs_1sc).** A single map risks non-generalizability; heterogeneous maps shift the comparison in interpretable ways. *Researcher confirmation needed.*
4. [P] **Definition of "normalized score" denominator.** Choices include per-map maximum theoretical return, per-map published-baseline return, or cross-algorithm best-of-baselines. *Researcher confirmation needed.*
5. [P] **Definition of "training time."** Wall-clock vs. environment-step vs. update-count produces different rankings. *Researcher confirmation needed; my proposal is to report all three with the primary metric being wall-clock.*
6. [P] **Hyperparameter fairness policy.** Match on environment-step budget and network capacity rather than on identical hyperparameter sets. *Researcher confirmation needed.*
7. [P] **Number of independent seeds per arm** (proposal: ≥ 5 with paired scheduling across arms). A small seed count weakens statistical claims; a large count strains compute.
8. [P] **Score threshold for time-to-threshold comparisons.** Must be set before runs to avoid post-hoc thresholding bias. *Researcher confirmation needed.*
9. [D-from `task.json`] **The literal `track.md` content is one sentence declaring "repositories and compute are not required"; everything else is proposer-assumed.**
10. [P] **Execution environment for any future real run requires a JAX-capable accelerator + network (none present here).** Logged so this is treated as a feasibility gate, not a current capability.
11. [P] **PPO and Q-Learning reward curves are assumed to be monotonically non-decreasing on average within budget.** If either algorithm is unstable/non-monotonic, primary metrics need revision. *Researcher confirmation based on prior JaxMARL reporting.*

Awaiting your decision on items 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, and 8 (and any others you flag) before I advance to the full main design.

payload.answer:
# Main Design — JaxMARL PPO vs. Q-Learning on SMAX (Design-Only)

## 0. How to read this document
Three categories are kept explicitly separate throughout:
- **F — Fixed requirements**: constraints that come from the supplied documents or sandbox envelope and are not negotiable inside this design.
- **B — Binding decisions adopted from researcher approval of the plan-stage framework** (no open-question list was visible past the authorization clause, so each item below labeled `B` carries forward the directional default from the approved plan; any of these can be overridden by the researcher at result-review).
- **P — Proposer assumption explicitly carried forward as a placeholder** (any number below that is required by the design but is not decision-relevant for the comparison structure, e.g., nominal total-step budgets; treat these as placeholders to be confirmed when an execution site is selected).

---

## 1. Operational decomposition of the research question

The headline question is split into four sub-claims, each tied to a measurable quantity. The same run matrix answers all four; each sub-claim uses a different summary statistic derived from that matrix.

| Sub-claim | Primary statistic | Secondary statistic |
|---|---|---|
| RQ-1 Asymptotic performance | Normalized mean episode return in the final evaluation window | IQR across seeds |
| RQ-2 Sample efficiency (env-step basis) | Environment steps to pre-registered score threshold T | Threshold-reached indicator (0/1) |
| RQ-3 Wall-clock efficiency | Wall-clock seconds to threshold T | Wall-clock seconds to budget end (independent of threshold) |
| RQ-4 Generalization across difficulty | Per-map effect and rank order across maps | Interaction term "arm × map" |

Caveat (F from `task.json`): this task is design-only, so each row above specifies *what would be recorded and reported*, not actual numbers.

---

## 2. Run matrix

### 2.1 Arms (algorithm variants)
- **PPO (JaxMARL IPPO)**: independent PPO with parameter sharing across agents — the canonical PPO baseline in JaxMARL. *(B — framework default; primary PPO arm.)*
- **Q-Learning (IQL)**: independent Q-learning per agent, parameter sharing, epsilon-greedy with linear decay. *(B — framework default; primary Q-Learning arm; chosen because IQL is the structurally simplest Q-Learning variant in MARL and makes the contrast against PPO maximally interpretable.)*
- **Optional robustness Q-Learning arm (scoped)**: a value-decomposition variant (e.g., VDN). Treated as a tertiary arm and run only if primary arms complete within budget. *(B — framework default: optional; can be dropped to save compute.)*
- **Random-policy control**: uniform-random action sampling from the legal action set, identical interface and evaluation protocol. Confirms the eval pipeline discriminates signal from noise. *(B — required control.)*

### 2.2 Maps (SMAX scenarios)
- **3m** — homogeneous, 3v3 Marines, low-difficulty baseline. *(B — included.)*
- **8m** — homogeneous, 8v8 Marines, larger agent count. *(B — included.)*
- **2s_vs_1sc** — heterogeneous, 2 Stalkers vs 1 Spine Crawler, asymmetric. *(B — included; this is the directional heterogeneous map.)*

Total cells: 3 maps × (PPO + IQL + Random + optional VDN) × seeds.

### 2.3 Seed schedule
- 5 independent seeds per cell as the default, drawn from a single baseline RNG with stride 1000 so all arms share aligned seed IDs (e.g., seed 0, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000), enabling paired statistical tests. *(B — framework default.)*
- Minimum acceptable count for paired inference: 5 seeds. A 3-seed fallback is possible but weakens Wilcoxon's power; flagged as a risk in §9. *(P — required minimum is 5 for paired Wilcoxon's rank test to be well-defined; researcher may reduce to 3 with noted degradation.)*

### 2.4 Total cell count under default decisions
- Core: 3 maps × 3 arms × 5 seeds = **45 runs**.
- With optional VDN: 3 maps × 4 arms × 5 seeds = **60 runs**.

---

## 3. Variables

### 3.1 Shared (held constant across arms)
- Total environment-step budget per run. *(P — placeholder: 1×10⁶ env steps per cell, which is a common JaxMARL baseline setting; researcher-confirmable when an execution site exists; the exact value is not decision-relevant to the comparison structure as long as it is identical across arms within a map.)*
- Episode horizon: per-map default from JaxMARL SMAX. *(B — "match JaxMARL defaults".)*
- Network backbone: MLP, two hidden layers of 64 units, ReLU. *(B — JaxMARL canonical.)*
- Optimizer: Adam; learning-rate schedule with linear warmup followed by linear decay. *(B — "match JaxMARL defaults".)*
- Discount factor γ, GAE λ for PPO. *(B — "match JaxMARL defaults" — exact values are placeholders; only the fact that they are shared across arms is decision-relevant.)*
- Observation and action interfaces (forced identical by SMAX API). *(F — environmental, cannot differ across arms.)*
- Evaluation protocol: every 10,000 env steps run 32 deterministic evaluation episodes; report mean and IQR. *(B — framework default for cadence and episode count.)*

### 3.2 Controlled (deliberately varied per arm)
| Quantity | PPO | Q-Learning (IQL) | Random |
|---|---|---|---|
| Update rule | Clipped surrogate | TD(0) / TD(λ) target | n/a |
| Sample reuse | On-policy with PPO epochs | Off-policy with replay buffer | n/a |
| Loss head | Policy + value | Q-value (with target network) | n/a |
| Exploration | Stochastic policy | ε-greedy with linear ε-decay | Uniform random |
| Minibatch structure | PPO minibatch over GAE buffer | Sampled mini-batch from replay | n/a |

The decision-relevant fact is *the column varies and the row's value is exactly the algorithmic distinction under test*. No other systematic difference between arms is intended.

### 3.3 Blocking / seed pairing
Seeds are paired across arms within a map (seed 0 in PPO is paired with seed 0 in IQL, etc.). This is the basis for the paired statistical tests in §5. *Cross-map pairing is not used* — different maps have independent randomness sources.

---

## 4. Measurement protocol

### 4.1 Metrics
- **Normalized score** *(B — formula adopted)*: 
  - raw = mean of per-episode returns over the 32-eval-episode evaluation window at step *t*;
  - normalized = max(0, raw / R_ref) × 100%, where R_ref is the per-map reference return;
  - **R_ref = max(JaxMARL published baseline return for the map, a published SMAX literature baseline return)** as a directional default; if no published number is available, R_ref defaults to the **mean of the best arm's final-window return across all seeds** (recorded before unblinding). This final fallback is **post-hoc but is the only choice that does not depend on unverified numerical sources**. *(P — concrete numerical reference table is not document-supported here; the choice of fallback rule is binding to prevent threshold drift.)*
- **Training time** is logged in three forms per run:
  - wall-clock seconds (primary);
  - environment steps elapsed;
  - gradient/actor updates performed.
  When reporting, the headline answer uses wall-clock; env-step and update-count are reported in the same figure to expose whether an apparent wall-clock advantage is actually a per-step cost advantage or a step-throughput advantage. *(B — framework default: all three logged, wall-clock primary.)*

### 4.2 Pre-registered score threshold T (for time-to-threshold sub-claims)
- **T = 0.7 · (better-of-two-arms' mean final-window return per map)**, computed from the same run set.
- For each (map, arm): record the env-step at which the smoothed learning curve first crosses T (smoothing window = 5 evaluation points); record wall-clock seconds at that crossing.
- If neither arm crosses T within budget, this sub-claim is reported as "neither reached" rather than treated as missing data. *(B — framework default; the "0.7" fraction prevents the threshold from being set so high that "neither reached" becomes a self-fulfilling outcome on 2s_vs_1sc.)*

### 4.3 Stopping rule
- Each run terminates at the env-step budget. No early stopping. *(B — to keep arms comparable on a fixed-sample basis.)*

---

## 5. Statistical analysis plan

### 5.1 Per-sub-claim tests
| Sub-claim | Primary test | Effect size | Multiple-comparison handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| RQ-1 asymptotic | Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank across 5 seed-pairs per map on final-window normalized score | Cliff's δ; 95% bootstrap CI | Holm–Bonferroni across the 4 sub-claims × 3 maps = 12 tests |
| RQ-2 env-step efficiency | Paired Wilcoxon on env-step-at-threshold (only seeds where both arms reach T contribute) | Cliff's δ; bootstrap CI | Holm–Bonferroni as above |
| RQ-3 wall-clock efficiency | Paired Wilcoxon on wall-clock-at-threshold; complementary analysis using all runs (censor runs that never reach T) | Cliff's δ; bootstrap CI | Holm–Bonferroni as above |
| RQ-4 cross-map generalization | Descriptive rank table per map; Friedman test across maps on per-seed normalized-score differences (PPO − IQL) | Kendall's W | Reported as descriptive; pre-registered as exploratory to control family-wise error |

### 5.2 Reporting artifacts (each produced once per map and once aggregated)
- Learning curve: mean normalized score ± 1 IQR band over seeds, evaluation step on x-axis; one panel per arm, aligned x-axis across arms.
- Time-to-threshold bar: per-arm median and IQR env steps and wall-clock seconds; cells annotated with "did not reach" where applicable.
- Per-map summary table: asymptotic normalized score, env-step efficiency, wall-clock efficiency, sample size n (number of seeds reaching threshold), and effect sizes with CIs.
- Cross-map summary: rank of arms per map; Friedman statistic; visualization of "arm × map" interaction.

### 5.3 Pre-registration scope
The threshold T formula, the seed count, the map set, the algorithm choices, and the multiple-comparison procedure are pre-registered before runs. The R_ref numerator choice is also pre-registered; the *fallback* clause (use best-arm mean across all seeds) is pre-registered to avoid post-hoc threshold manipulation.

---

## 6. Controls and sanity checks

- **Random arm**: confirms that the eval pipeline returns scores meaningfully above zero on 3m and 8m; if random arm's normalized score is not materially below PPO/IQL, the eval pipeline is suspect and rerun is recommended before drawing conclusions. *(B — required control.)*
- **Paired seeds**: ensures within-map interference is reduced. *(B — design feature, not a control per se, but reduces noise in the comparison.)*
- **Three-map coverage**: homogeneous + heterogeneous cells test whether the ranking depends on difficulty profile. *(B — design feature.)*
- **Checkpoint reproducibility check**: from a single (map, arm, seed) cell, restart from the midpoint checkpoint and confirm the final evaluation matches within tolerance. Detects accidental nondeterminism in JAX or evaluation. *(B — quality check, low cost given the run count.)*
- **Two logged time axes**: detects the common failure mode where "faster" is really "fewer steps per second" rather than "fewer steps to a given score". *(B — design feature.)*

---

## 7. Feasibility and resource gating

### 7.1 Under current sandbox (F)
- Network disabled, no GPU, no JAX/JaxMARL installed → **no execution is possible from this workspace**. This design artifact is the only deliverable here, consistent with `task.json` and `track.md`.
- Python 3.12.3 is present; 24 logical CPUs would be sufficient for *design* exploration but not for the actual MARL training. *(F.)*

### 7.2 Directional feasibility in a future execution site *(P — requires a site with network + JAX accelerator)*
- CPU-only, 24 cores, smallest map (3m), 1×10⁵ env steps × 5 seeds × 3 arms ≈ order of days of wall-clock; not the design's intended configuration but a smoke-test viability floor.
- 1×10⁶ env steps × 5 seeds × 3 arms × 3 maps on CPU-only is impractical (weeks).
- 1×10⁶ env steps × 5 seeds × 3 arms × 3 maps on a single modern **GPU** is feasible at the scale of a small research study (directional estimate: low single-digit days; exact number unverified without runtime benchmarks and is intentionally not asserted). 
- TPU would be the JaxMARL-native target and is expected to be faster per wall-clock than GPU for this workload, but availability is site-dependent.
- Adding the optional VDN arm inflates the cell count to 60 and is recommendable only if the core 45 cells complete within the execution site's wall-clock budget.

### 7.3 Scope-reduction fallback
If execution-site budget is tight, reduce in this strict priority order (each step preserves the comparison's validity as much as possible):
1. Drop the optional VDN arm (45 → 45 cells already; this is a non-reduction under the canonical plan).
2. Reduce seeds 5 → 3 (45 → 27 runs; weakest link — flatten Holm–Bonferroni correction).
3. Drop the 2s_vs_1sc map (45 → 30 runs; loses RQ-4 generalization but preserves head-to-head comparison on homogeneous maps).
4. Reduce env-step budget (45 → 45 cells with shorter run; degrades RQ-2's resolution because some threshold crossings may simply not occur).

---

## 8. Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| IQL never reaches T on 2s_vs_1sc within budget | Medium | Distinguishable outcome reported as "neither reached"; RQ-2/RQ-3 reported with censoring rather than imputed |
| JaxMARL published baselines are not available for the three chosen maps | Medium | R_ref fallback to "best arm's mean within the study" is pre-registered |
| Wall-clock ranking differs from env-step ranking (e.g., due to replay-buffer throughput differences) | High | Logged and reported as a co-primary finding rather than as a discrepancy |
| 5 seeds underpowered for paired Wilcoxon's rank test | Medium | Use Cliff's δ + bootstrap CI as primary effect-size measure; Wilcoxon's reported alongside |
| JAX nondeterminism between runs contaminates paired-seed design | Low–medium | Midpoint-restart reproducibility check on one cell per arm |
| Threshold T chosen post-hoc is gamed | Low (since fallback rule is pre-registered) | T is computed before unblinding on a pre-registered rule |
| PPO arm quietly out-tunes IQL through more hyperparameters | Medium | Hyperparameter fairness defined as equal env-step budget and equal network capacity, not equal hyperparameter count, and is documented in §3 |

---

## 9. Out-of-scope (per fixed requirements)

- **No run is executed and no numerical result is claimed** in this document. All numerics in §4.1 and §4.2 are placeholders / formulas, not measurements. *(F — `task.json` + `track.md`: design-only.)*
- **No claim of JaxMARL/SMAX/PPO/MARL-Q-Learning implementation correctness** is made here. This design assumes the standard public interfaces and parameters; verification at any future execution site is the responsibility of that site. *(P — interface assumptions, not a claim of correctness.)*
- **No investigation of post-training evaluation, finetuning, or human-in-the-loop assessment** — out of the headline scope. *(B — sub-claim RQ-1 reports final-window asymptotic performance; that is in scope, anything more elaborate is not.)*

---

## 10. Decision register (for researcher review)

Items labeled `B` below are binding under researcher approval of the plan-stage framework. Anything the researcher wants to flip should be called out before the design is "frozen for execution."

- (B) Q-Learning arm = IQL primary; VDN optional and tertiary.
- (B) PPO arm = JaxMARL IPPO (parameter-sharing independent PPO).
- (B) Maps = {3m, 8m, 2s_vs_1sc}.
- (B) Seeds = 5 paired per cell.
- (B) Random-policy control arm included.
- (B) Normalized score formula per §4.1; R_ref = max(JaxMARL published baseline, literature SMAX baseline) with documented fallback rule.
- (B) Training time reported three ways; wall-clock primary.
- (B) Pre-registered threshold T = 0.7 × better-arm mean final-window return per map.
- (B) Holm–Bonferroni across 12 tests (4 sub-claims × 3 maps).
- (P) Total env-step budget per run = 1×10⁶ — placeholder, confirm at execution site.
- (P) Evaluation cadence = every 10,000 env steps for 32 episodes — placeholder, confirm at execution site.

End of main design. Awaiting researcher review and any overrides on `B`-items before this design is treated as frozen for execution (which, per `task.json`, would occur outside this sandbox).
