## पूरा प्रयोग-डिज़ाइन — "Does Zero-shot CoT improve LLM-agent task-solving on WorkArena++?"

यह दस्तावेज़ केवल डिज़ाइन है; कोई प्रयोग निष्पादित नहीं हुआ। अनुमोदित defaults का पालन: Zero-shot CoT × frozen open-weights LLM (Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct वर्ग) × 30×3×2 paired, stratified WorkArena++ × success-rate Δ primary, step-efficiency Δ secondary।

---

### (a) शोध-प्रश्न + उप-परिकल्पनाएँ

**RQ:** क्या Zero-shot CoT prompting, No-CoT की तुलना में LLM-आधारित एजेंट का WorkArena++ पर task-solving सुधारता है?

**H1 (प्राथमिक):** H1: `succ_CoT − succ_NoCoT > 0` paired संरचना में।
- **H1a (compositional-depth moderation):** CoT-लाभ compositional depth के साथ बढ़ता है (लंबे, बहु-उप-लक्ष्य कार्यों पर अधिक)।
- **H1b (budget moderation):** CoT-लाभ slack वाले कार्यों पर अधिक — जब actor_step_budget=60 के भीतर चरण-हेडरूम बड़ा हो।
- **H1c (page-complexity moderation):** जब अवलोकन (observation) जटिल/अस्पष्ट हो (अधिक affordances, dynamic DOM), CoT-लाभ अधिक।

**H0 (शून्य-परिकल्पना):** कोई अंतर नहीं।

**H2 (द्वितीयक, direction-agnostic):** `stepEff_CoT ≠ stepEff_NoCoT` जहाँ stepEff = 1/steps-to-success। दिशा पूर्व-निर्धारित नहीं — दोनों संभव: (i) प्रति-चरण reasoning से total चरण बढ़ सकते हैं (downward), (ii) बेहतर योजना से waste steps घट सकते हैं (upward)।

**Negative predictions (जहाँ CoT के विफल होने की संभावना — ये विफलता-मोड भी तय पूर्व-पंजीकरण हैं):**
- N1: एकल-क्रिया atomic कार्यों पर कोई लाभ नहीं (cohens g ≈ 0)।
- N2: अत्यंत छोटे step-budget (≤5 चरण) वाले कार्यों पर CoT सिर्फ overhead है — overhead संभावित रूप से λ-step limit में degrade कर सकता है।
- N3: कार्य जहाँ अवलोकन direct action unique करता है (information-rich page → no reasoning needed) — flat या negative Δ।

---

### (b) प्रक्रिया

#### b.1 दो शर्तों के पूर्ण prompt templates

साझा-विन्यास:
- HISTORY truncated to K=10 most recent (obs, action, reward) tuples।
- Observation serialization: accessibility-tree text dump + flat list of `[bid] element_label` interactive elements।
- Action space defined as a deterministic JSON-string DSL listed in §b.3।

**शर्त A — No-CoT (Control)**

`system`:
```
You are an autonomous ServiceNow agent. Each turn you receive the
current page observation and a task description. Respond with exactly
one action in the prescribed format. Do not explain.
```

`user` (template, में {…} फील्ड्स चर हैं):
```
GOAL: {task_natural_language}
HISTORY (most recent last, up to 10 steps):
{history_block}
CURRENT OBSERVATION:
{obs_text}
LIST OF INTERACTIVE ELEMENTS:
{elements_block}
NEXT ACTION (single line, format: action_type(args)):
```

**शर्त B — Zero-shot CoT (Treatment)**

`system`:
```
You are an autonomous ServiceNow agent. Each turn you receive the
current page observation and a task description. Think step by step
about the current state, what still needs to be done toward the goal,
and which action best advances it. Then output exactly one action in
the prescribed format.
```

`user` (template):
```
GOAL: {task_natural_language}
HISTORY (most recent last, up to 10 steps):
{history_block}
CURRENT OBSERVATION:
{obs_text}
LIST OF INTERACTIVE ELEMENTS:
{elements_block}
THINK STEP BY STEP ABOUT WHAT TO DO NEXT, THEN OUTPUT ONE ACTION
(format: action_type(args)):
```

दो टेम्पलेट्स का इरादा-निर्धारित एकमात्र अंतर: `system` में "Think step by step…" वाक्य (CoT) बनाम "Do not explain" (No-CoT), और `user` के अंत में THINK… वाक्य (CoT) बनाम NEXT ACTION… (No-CoT). संरचना, अनुभाग-क्रम, इतिहास-लंबाई, अवलोकन-स्रोत सर्वथा समान। (Prompt-length औपचारिक मिलान §c में।)

#### b.2 Tool / API interface assumptions

LLM एक प्रति-चरण JSON-रहित DSL उत्पन्न करता है (regex-पार्स किया जाता है):
```
click(bid=<int>)
type(bid=<int>, text="<str>")
select_option(bid=<int>, option="<str>")
press_key(key="<str>")
submit()
goto(url="<str>")
finish(answer="<encodable>")
FAIL(reason="<str>")
```
LLM-output parser: regex + `bid` integer-cast + whitelisted action names; parse failure ⇒ re-query LLM once with "Your previous response was malformed; output strictly action_type(args)." दूसरी विफलता ⇒ §b.4 Termination E.

#### b.3 Observation / Action space सार

- **Observation type:** Playwright `aria_snapshot()` + linearized DOM string + flat `[bid] role "label"` enumeration। bid ↔ Playwright DOM node handle; बाइंडिंग deterministic per page-load।
- **Action semantics:** synchronous; browser automation returns updated observation + reward float (0/1 for terminality per WorkArena++ verifier, 0 for intermediate)।

#### b.4 Episode-समाप्ति नियम

| टर्मिनेशन | ट्रिगर | स्थिति |
|---|---|---|
| A: `finish(answer)` | एजेंट स्वयं बताता है | verifier चलता है; success binary |
| B: `FAIL(reason)` | एजेंट give-up | failure |
| C: step budget | actions ≥ 60 | failure (जब तक oracle पहले ही satisfied न हो) |
| D: loop detector | (obs, action) identical for K_loop = 3 consecutive steps | failure |
| E: parse failure | दो क्रमिक regex parse विफलताएँ | failure |

सभी terminations पर ServiceNow-side deterministic verifier §b.5 चलता है।

#### b.5 Verifier (success determination)

प्रत्येक शर्त के अंत में WorkArena++ कनॉनिकल oracle verifier लागू: pre/post state के incumbent form-मान, list-निकाय, या visibility-check से सत्य binary verdict। Success = 1 iff oracle = PASS; अन्यथा 0।

---

### (c) नियंत्रण (Controls)

#### c.1 Decoding determinism
- `temperature=0`, `top_p=1.0`, `top_k=-1`, `repetition_penalty=1.0`, `max_new_tokens=512`
- अनुमोदित: frozen pinned SHA — single open-weights Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (या equivalent) का निश्चित revision।

#### c.2 Seed pinning
- vLLM `--seed 42`; PyTorch `torch.manual_seed(42)`; NumPy `np.random.seed(42)`; Python `random.Random(42)` for trial seeds (1, 2, 3)।
- Async scheduling: Python `random.Random(43)` (separate RNG) for run-order randomization — task/seed/condition shuffle Latin-square से।

#### c.3 Prompt-length matching
- दो system prompts के लिए pre-execution tokenizer-length logging।
- लक्ष्य: दोनों शर्तों के system+user prompts की token-लंबाई ≤ 5% deviation; यदि deviation > 5% हो तो No-CoT instruction-text में neutral content-pad (e.g., repetition of policy lines) — पर यह अंतिम-उपाय; पहले prompt-engineering से alignment।
- §b.1 के टेम्पलेट्स structurally matched हैं; verification के बाद कोई padding अपेक्षित नहीं।

#### c.4 Token-budget equivalence
- Generation-time `max_new_tokens=512` दोनों शर्तों में। CoT अधिकतम 512 tokens उपभोग कर सकता है (thinking + final action); No-CoT कम उपभोग करेगा। Episode-level token-उपयोग लागत के रूप में report होगा (secondary, exploratory)।
- प्रति-चरण पूर्व-allocated reasoning budget नहीं — CoT को अपने natural length पर चलने दिया जाता है; bounded by max_new_tokens।

#### c.5 Order-effect counterbalancing
- 90 task-instances (= 30 tasks × 3 seeds) को 45 AB + 45 BA में split; assignment नियम: `(task_id mod 2)` → 0 ⇒ AB, 1 ⇒ BA; पर प्रत्येक stratification stratum के भीतर counterbalanced (Pearson chi-square test pre-handover)।
- एक task-instance के दो रन एक ही wall-clock window में (दूसरे unrelated कार्य-उदाहरण interlaced) चलाने के लिए shuffle किया जाता है, ताकि A→B bias या B→A bias symmetric हो।
- Stateless LLM calls का अर्थ है model-side carry-over नहीं; पर ServiceNow/instance-state carry-over रोकने के लिए प्रत्येक रन-से पहले clean session reset (देखें c.6)।

#### c.6 Instance / browser-stack assumptions
- Browser automation: Playwright (Chromium headless) — preferred, accessibility-tree उत्कृष्ट।
- ServiceNow backend: Personal Developer Instance (PDI) default; Lite Mode contingency (देखें §f contingencies)।
- प्रत्येक episode से पहले: fresh browser context, fresh ServiceNow user session, baseline-state re-seeded via canonical pre-task setup function (WorkArena++ कन्वेंशन)।
- Episode के बाद: context destroyed, session logout, state-revert to baseline।

#### c.7 Contamination checks
1. **Model-version screen:** model snapshot की release-date WorkArena++ की public release-date से पहले की होनी चाहिए — यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि tasks open-source training corpus में नहीं गए।
2. **Canary tasks:** 5 कार्य जो pilot sample में शामिल नहीं हैं — उन पर बिना-कार्य-पाठ के या paraphrased-पाठ के model probe। यदि model बिना संदर्भ के भी canonical answer / action उत्पन्न करता है ⇒ contaminated ⇒ exclusion।
3. **Prompt-template screen:** prompts में WorkArena++ का कोई उदाहरण/वाक्य verbatim नहीं।
4. **Post-hoc:** कार्य-स्तर पर Δ का distribution विश्लेषण — outlier-task जहाँ Δ ≈ 1.0 और अन्यथा viability जाँचें।

#### c.8 Lesser-confound controls
- HISTORY-K identical for both conditions।
- Observation serialization identical (same accessibility-tree dump)।
- बीच में mid-run re-prompt नहीं; system prompt दोनों शर्तों में एक ही episode में नहीं बदलता।
- Image / multimodal token नहीं (WorkArena++ text-based tasks मानते हैं)।

#### c.9 "Few-shot source" आंतरिक निर्णय का समाधान
- शर्त Zero-shot चुनी गई है ⇒ कोई few-shot उदाहरण नहीं ⇒ यह डिज़ाइन-बिंदु पर कोई संसाधन-चयन लागू नहीं होता। दस्तावेज़ में explicit किया गया है कि few-shot confounding इस design में absent है।

---

### (d) प्रतिचयन (Sampling)

#### d.1 Population
WorkArena++ की सभी compositional tasks (लगभग 200+ कार्य across multiple categories) — अनुमोदित defaults के अनुसार इनका प्रतिनिधि-सबसेट लिया जाएगा।

#### d.2 Randomization procedure
- एकल seed (42) के साथ `random.sample` चलाया जाता है।
- Stratification per compositional category।
- Allocation proportional: हर श्रेणी से `max(3, ceil(total_tasks × category_share))` कार्य, बड़ी श्रेणियों को 6 कार्यों पर capped (balance maintain करने के लिए)।
- Total = 30। यदि allocation 30 को over/undershoot करती है तो निकटतम multiple balanced (lasso)।

#### d.3 Inclusion / Exclusion नियम

**Inclusion:**
- WorkArena++ कार्य-परिभाषा फाइल parseable।
- Oracle verifier deterministic।
- Compositional (multi-step / multi-app)।
- कार्य 60 steps के भीतर theoretically-completable (operational cap)।

**Exclusion:**
- Contamination flag (per §c.7 step 2) — task excluded if canary positive for paraphrase-oracle match।
- Non-deterministic verifier instances (frequency empirically seen across test reruns)।
- Compliance / external-network keying (no exogenous API permitted under sandbox)।

**Replacement rule:**
- यदि excluded > 3 कार्य (10%): same stratification frame से replacement draw (same seed)।
- यदि excluded > 6 कार्य (20%): sample redesign report in supplement; primary analysis proceeds on whatever available but flagged।

#### d.4 Final sample figure
30 कार्य × 3 trials × 2 conditions = 180 paired runs। यह actor_step_budget=60 के per-episode constraint के भीतर रहता है।

---

### (e) विश्लेषण योजना

#### e.1 प्राथमिक परीक्षण

**Success-rate Δ = p_CoT − p_NoCoT**
- सांख्यिकीय परीक्षण: McNemar's exact test (paired binary, discordant cells पर) — 90 task-instances पर।
- 2×2 contingency: discordant pair counts `(0,1)` और `(1,0)` (उनमें से `(1,0)` = No-CoT wins; `(0,1)` = CoT wins)।
- यदि discordant sum < 25: exact test underpowered — fallback asymptotic McNemar with continuity correction, Fagerland adjustment।
- Effect size estimator: matched-pairs proportion difference; 95% CI via paired-bootstrap B=10,000 task-instance-level resamples।
- **Pre-registered p-value threshold:** α = 0.05, single primary endpoint; कोई multi-test correction नहीं।

#### e.2 द्वितीयक परीक्षण

**Step-efficiency Δ = log(steps_NoCoT) − log(steps_CoT) (sign-free; both-direction supported)**
- Restricted to runs जहाँ दोनों शर्तों ने success प्राप्त किया — ताकि extra-success bias न आए।
- Sign convention: positive Δ ⇒ CoT तेज़ (कम चरण पर success); negative Δ ⇒ CoT धीमी।
- परीक्षण: Wilcoxon signed-rank (non-parametric, paired)।
- 95% CI via paired-bootstrap B=10,000 (resample over task-instances)।
- **Effect size:** matched-pairs Cohen's d_z, CI via bootstrap।
- Multiple-comparison handling: Holm-Bonferroni with k=2 tests (primary + secondary)। Step-down procedure: smallest p first; reject if p ≤ α / (k − rank + 1) where α=0.05, k=2 ⇒ secondary α_threshold = 0.025; primary अपरिवर्तित। यदि researcher केवल single primary चाहते हैं यह कदम पूरी तरह वैकल्पिक है — डिफ़ॉल्ट दोनों endpoints पर report।

#### e.3 Pre-registered effect-size thresholds
| Endpoint | Meaningful threshold |
|---|---|
| Success-rate Δ | |Δ| ≥ 0.10 (10 percentage points) |
| Step-efficiency (log steps) | |d_z| ≥ 0.30 |

Practical significance corroboration के लिए — p-value independently applicable नहीं।

#### e.4 Subgroup analyses (exploratory, α-controlled नहीं)

1. **Category breakdown:** प्रत्येक compositional category पर success-rate Δ का forest plot (point + 95% CI via per-stratum bootstrap); श्रेणियों में Bonferroni = nominal, exploratory only।
2. **Difficulty strata:** pre-tagged WorkArena++ difficulty (easy/medium/hard)। प्रति-stratum Δ + interaction test (logistic regression with condition, difficulty, condition×difficulty)।
3. **Step-budget utilization split:** median-completed-under-30-steps vs between-30-and-60। Moderation test: interaction condition×budget-slack।
4. **Compositional depth:** task definition से sub-goal count extract; Spearman correlation of Δ vs depth, with bootstrap CI।

#### e.5 Missing-data / non-convergence handling
- Episode जो parse-failure या OOM से drop हुआ: exclude और record as "episode_non_completion" — separate-from-verifier outcome।
- यदि किसी task के 3 trials में से > 0 episode_non_completion हो: pair-level reporting uses available pairs; sensitivity analysis with imputed values (worst-case for primary endpoint)।

#### e.6 Visualization & reporting deliverables
- 2×2 contingency heatmap (CoT × No-CoT success)।
- Forest plot of subgroup Δs with CIs।
- Per-task Δ scatter with marginal histograms।
- Pre-registration (OSF/AsPredicted, researcher-discretion) में frozen endpoint definitions और thresholds।

---

### (f) Feasibility

#### f.1 Execution environment (design-level forecasts, not run here)
- **ServiceNow instance:** PDI (Personal Developer Instance) default — resets between episodes, no persistent multi-task state। यदि किसी कार्य द्वारा session persistence की आवश्यकता हो: Lite Mode / LM में switch (contingency-2)। अनुमोदित defaults के अनुकूल — instance-प्रकार निष्पादन-समय पर confirm होगा।
- **Browser automation stack:** Playwright + Chromium default; Selenium + Chrome fallback (contingency)। BrowserGym abstraction layer दोनों के ऊपर काम करता है — experimental logic अपरिवर्तित रहता है।
- **LLM serving:** vLLM (preferred — deterministic seeding support) या sglang/TGI fallback; open-weights pinned SHA; max_new_tokens=512; temperature=0।
- **Orchestration:** WorkArena++ कार्य-लोडर + BrowserGym agentic-protocol bindings; Python 3.11+ virtualenv।

#### f.2 Compute / runtime बजट अनुमान
| घटक | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Step latency, avg (LLM 70B + browser step) | ~1.5 sec/step |
| Steps/episode (typical medium task) | ~10–25 |
| Wall-clock/episode (typical) | ~15–40 sec |
| Wall-clock/episode (worst, budget-cliff) | ~90 sec |
| Total episodes | 180 |
| Wall-clock total (typical) | ~90 min |
| Wall-clock total (worst incl. retries) | ~5–6 hours |
| GPU memory | 70B in fp16 ≈ 140 GB या INT4 ≈ 40 GB |
| Disk | 140 GB model + ~10 GB artifacts |

यह सब एक single 8xA100 या 4xH100 node पर ~6h में पूरा हो सकता है; यदि serving bottleneck हो तो queue स्कीम लागू।

#### f.3 Contingencies (दो मुख्य अनिश्चितताएँ)

**C-1: ServiceNow instance प्रकार**
- Default: PDI। Limitations: session resets between episodes — एक कार्य-उदाहरण जो coarse cross-episode state साझा करता है, समर्थित नहीं।
- Trigger to switch: कोई 30 में से कार्य "execute steps handoff to next user session" प्रकार का हो — switch to Lite (persistent state)।
- Documentation: switch होने पर उस कार्य-स्तर पर instance-type reported; in protocol drift document।

**C-2: Browser-automation stack**
- Default: Playwright (Chromium) — best-in-class accessibility-tree APIs।
- Fallback: Selenium + Chrome (jdk-headless) — broader availability, slightly-less-reliable ax-tree। अंतर: DOM-extraction fidelity, action-mapping reliability; observable side effect logging detects regressions।
- Trigger to switch: Playwright BOM/DOM quirks जो कार्य-विशिष्ट UI पर fail; switch logged in protocol drift。

#### f.4 Sandbox vs. execution-वातावरण-मान्यताएँ
- यह design-only टास्क bubblewrap + network-disabled sandbox में किया गया; actual experiment के लिए network-enabled local GPU server, ServiceNow Internet-reachable PDI, और browser-engines के access आवश्यक होंगे। यह design उन परिवेशों के लिए तैयार है; यहाँ निष्पादित नहीं होगा।

---

### ग) Quick-reference design summary

```
RQ: does Zero-shot CoT improve LLM-agent success on WorkArena++?
Population: WorkArena++ compositional tasks (≈200+)
Sample: stratified n=30 tasks × 3 trials × 2 conditions = 180 paired
Model: single frozen Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-class, pinned SHA
Conditions: A=No-CoT, B=Zero-shot CoT (only-prompt manipulation)
Sampling: stratified random, seed=42
Decoding: temperature=0, top_p=1, top_k=-1, max_new_tokens=512
Order: AB/BA counterbalanced within strata
Loop/parse guards: K_loop=3, 2 retries, then FAIL
Ep. termination: finish/FAIL/step≥60
Verifier: WorkArena++ oracle, binary
Primary test: McNemar exact on 90 paired binary outcomes; α=.05 single-endpoint
Secondary test: Wilcoxon signed-rank on log-steps; Holm-Bonferroni k=2
Effect thresholds: |Δ|≥0.10 success, |d_z|≥0.30 steps
CIs: paired-bootstrap B=10,000
Subgroups: category × difficulty × budget-slack (exploratory)
Contingencies: PDI vs LM, Playwright vs Selenium
```

## 1) INPUT / REPOSITORY INSPECTION

The `/workspace` directory contains a single file, `task.json`. No code, configs, scripts, datasets, or external documents are present; the in-file `track.md` field simply states "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required." The `researcher_topics` entry ("neurips2024/97713/3:setup_1") has no retrievable document content in this environment (no `track.md`/PDFs on disk, no network, no installed packages — `python3`, `workarena*`, `browsergym` are not present). In short: there is nothing in the repository that constrains the design, so every concrete setup choice below is an assumption the researcher must ratify rather than an observation from supplied material.

Compact list of what is actually present:
- `/workspace/task.json` — only artifact; contains the question, a `design-only` context note, and a `track.md` field that is a one-line placeholder (not a fetched document).
- No `*.py`, `*.yaml`, `*.json` configs, no benchmark tasks, no agent/eval scripts, no environment manifests, no model prompts.
- No installed dependencies; no GPU; no network. Confirmed `python3` is not on PATH and no WorkArena/BrowserGym packages are importable.

## 2) PROPOSED APPROACH (terse)

Hypothesis (operational). Primary: adding explicit chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning to an LLM agent's per-step prompt on WorkArena++ increases mean task success rate at fixed task-set, fixed model, and fixed observation/action interface. Primary endpoint = mean success-rate Δ (CoT − No-CoT), paired by task. Secondary endpoints: (a) cost-adjusted score = success per 1k total tokens, (b) median steps-to-success, (c) reasoning-error/hallucination/loop rate from a failure-mode taxonomy, (d) calibration (Brier score on the agent's own "I am done" confidence, optional), and (e) effect-size heterogeneity across task tiers.

Conditions (cells). Factor 1: Reasoning style — within-subject across every task: C0 No-CoT (direct action emission, control); C1 Zero-shot CoT ("Let's think step by step" before action); C2 Few-shot CoT (k=3–5 worked thinking/action/observation exemplars drawn from the same tier, disjoint from the test set); C3 Self-consistency (C1 sampled at temperature 0.7 with N=5, majority-vote on the emitted action); optional C4 Tool-augmented CoT (explicit scratchpad sub-tool such as `plan` / `verify` between thought and action with matched token budget to C1). Factor 2 (blocking): WorkArena++ tier — list/lookup, search/navigation, forms, configuration, plus any composite "plan" tier (provisional; unverified). Tasks are stratified by tier to support within-tier paired analysis.

Platform. WorkArena++ (ServiceNow atomic + composite tasks, served via BrowserGym). One ServiceNow instance per worker, deterministic reset between trials. Task selection: run all tasks of each selected tier; otherwise a stratified random sample of N tasks per tier with tier share proportional to population. Because the exact tier names and task IDs are NOT verified from the workspace, the design treats the tier list as a parameter to be filled in by the researcher.

Agent stack. Base LLM: a single frontier chat model (researcher's choice; default proposed = a current mid-size model such as GPT-4-class / Claude-3-class) with deterministic decoding: temperature 0 for C0/C1/C2, 0.7 for C3, top-p 1, fixed seed. Same model identity across all conditions. Browser driver: BrowserGym over headless Chromium controlling a ServiceNow instance. Observation → prompt: HTML ax-tree (or DOM-pruned) snippet + last action + last error + current goal string + chat history of (thought, action, observation) tuples. Action format = BrowserGym's discrete action enum. CoT is inserted immediately before the action token, in a dedicated `<think>...</think>` channel that is also logged for later failure coding; length-controlled by an instruction "Use ≤ N tokens of reasoning, N≈120"; cost-budget matched across conditions where possible. Prompt template: one shared system prompt; only the reasoning-instruction block differs between C0 and C1/C2/C3.

Protocol. Trials: 3 independent trials per (task × condition) to absorb stochasticity; median used for paired tests. Max steps: 25 per task (or tier-specific cap); wall-clock timeout 10 min/trial. Retry policy: no retries inside a trial; an infrastructure error triggers at most one rerun and is flagged. Seeding: Python/NumPy seeds, BrowserGym instance snapshot ID, ServiceNow user fixed. State reset: hard rollback to a known post-login ServiceNow state before every trial; verified by a sentinel page load. Randomization: Latin-square ordering of conditions across tasks; exemplars in C2 shuffled per trial from a fixed pool of k.

Controls & confounders. Prompt-length and token cost: C0 receives a filler "state your plan in 1 short sentence then act" instruction of comparable verbosity so prompt length is not a free parameter. Exemplar shuffle and exemplar-pool identity held fixed. Identical temperature across deterministic conditions (C0/C1/C2). Tool access identical (same BrowserGym action set; no extra retrievers). HTTP caching disabled for the agent's calls; enabled for static prompt scaffolding to control cost. Antitampering: a held-out "canary" task in which the No-CoT prompt is patched to include the literal CoT phrase — must NOT change its behaviour, validating that gains in C1–C3 are not instruction artefacts leaking. Order effects: counterbalanced with Latin square; "first-trial contamination" analysed as a covariate.

Metrics beyond success rate. Step efficiency = steps / optimal-steps (where an upper bound is known from task definitions). Tokens = input + output per trial; success per 1k tokens; $ per success. Latency = wall-clock seconds per trial and per step. Reasoning-error taxonomy (manual coding of failed trials): wrong goal interpretation; hallucinated UI element; action-format/parse error; loop/repeat of identical (state, action); premature stop; incorrect post-condition check. Calibration: Brier score on self-reported "done" confidence (only if the prompt asks for it, with identical instruction across conditions).

Analysis plan. Primary tests: paired (task-level) two-sided test of success between C1 and C0, C2 vs. C0, and C3 vs. C0 (subject-level pairing because every task sees every condition). Correction: Holm–Bonferroni across the 3 primary CoT contrasts. Effect sizes: Cohen's d for paired proportions + bootstrap 95% CI on Δ; same for cost-adjusted score. Stratified breakdown: by tier (interaction test); pre-registered "where does CoT help / hurt" decomposition. Ablations: drop scratchpad (C1 vs. C4); few-shot count k ∈ {1, 3, 5}; prompt-length-matched sub-analysis inserting equivalent filler in place of CoT. Robustness: rerun top 10% of tasks from each tier with seed variation to estimate variance. All analyses are registered in advance of execution against this design.

Feasibility check. No execution is attempted here. Risks to feasibility when run: API cost (mitigated by ≤ N tasks/tier and 3 trials; C3 self-consistency is ≈5× the C1 token bill), BrowserGym instance provisioning (requires a ServiceNow PDI or shared testing tenant), and evaluation wall-clock (mitigated by parallelisation across the available CPU cores).

## 3) ASSUMPTIONS & UNCERTAINTIES

Assumptions:
- A1 WorkArena++ is interpreted as the BrowserGym/ServiceNow benchmark with broad tiers (list/lookup, search/navigation, forms, configuration, plus composite "plan" tasks). Exact tier names and task counts are NOT verified and must be confirmed by the researcher.
- A2 "Improve" is read primarily as paired task-level success-rate Δ and secondarily as cost-adjusted success per 1k tokens; both are reported because CoT inflates tokens and may shift which metric favours CoT.
- A3 The baseline (No-CoT) prompt is a direct-action prompt with a matched-verbosity filler, not a vacuous one-liner; this controls for prompt length as a confound.
- A4 The base LLM is held fixed across conditions (single-model design), isolating CoT as the causal factor; cross-model transfer of any finding is left as future work.
- A5 Three trials per (task × condition) is the budget–quality trade-off; a formal power analysis will be in the full design.
- A6 CoT is inserted as a single <think>…</think> step immediately before action emission (the most common and least-confounded variant).
- A7 Statistical unit is the task; pairing is by task across conditions, with Holm–Bonferroni correction over the 3 primary CoT contrasts.
- A8 No external network, package installs, or execution are required or performed in this design-only task.
- A9 All cited WorkArena++ / BrowserGym / CoT facts are either common public knowledge or explicitly flagged as unverified-and-to-be-confirmed; no specific task IDs, exact success-rate numbers, or paper-level magnitudes from prior work are claimed.

Uncertainties:
- U1 Exact WorkArena++ tier taxonomy and task-pool sizes — must be confirmed before the full design can fix sample-size allocation per stratum.
- U2 Which LLM serves as the base model — affects absolute performance and the headroom for CoT to help.
- U3 Definition of "improve" — success-rate Δ vs. cost-adjusted score vs. requiring both. Single most consequential choice.
- U4 CoT condition set — whether to compare only Zero-shot CoT to No-CoT (headline), or to include Few-shot and Self-consistency as first-class cells.
- U5 Whether the agent stack should mirror a specific published setup (e.g., BrowserGym's default reuse-style loop) or be designed from scratch; affects reproducibility.
- U6 Whether failure-mode coding is performed manually, by a judge LLM, or both; affects metric validity.
- U7 Whether WorkArena++ tasks permit multiple valid solutions (would change the success criterion and the calibration analysis).
- U8 Construct-validity check: a canary task that injects CoT phrasing into the No-CoT prompt must remain unchanged in difficulty — design choice to confirm.

Top items I would like you to confirm before I produce the full design:
1. Primary endpoint definition — does "improve" mean success-rate gain, cost-adjusted gain, or "must improve on both"? This single choice can flip the conclusion and dictates the analysis hierarchy.
2. Scope of CoT conditions — is the contrast set C0/C1/C2/C3 acceptable, or do you want only one CoT variant (e.g., Zero-shot only) as the headline comparison, with the others as ablations?

(Secondary, also worth a sentence: which base model and which WorkArena++ tier list to use as the default.)

payload.answer:
# Experiment Design - Does Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Prompting Improve LLM-Agent Task-Solving in WorkArena++?

This is a design-only deliverable. Nothing has been executed and no measurements are reported. Every concrete number that depends on an unverified assumption is flagged inline as [assumption X / pending confirmation].

## A. Research Question and Operational Hypotheses

Research question (operational). Within a fixed agent stack and a fixed base LLM, does inserting explicit chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning immediately before action emission improve task-solving on WorkArena++?

| # | Hypothesis | Test direction | One-line pre-registered decision rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 (primary, headline) | CoT (C1) greater than No-CoT (C0) on paired task-level success rate. | one-sided, delta greater than 0 | Declare C1 improves over C0 iff (i) Wilcoxon signed-rank p less than or equal to alpha after Holm-Bonferroni, (ii) paired delta greater than 0, and (iii) its 95% bootstrap CI excludes 0 with at least 80% of resampled mass above 0. |
| H1c (co-primary) | C1 greater than C0 on cost-adjusted success (success per 1k total tokens). | one-sided, delta greater than 0 | Same template as H1, applied to the second metric in the same Holm family. Two co-primaries are reported; a disagreement is narrated by tier-stratified delta and a dominance plot, not by gating them. |
| H2 (secondary) | C2 (Few-shot CoT, k=3) differs from C1. | two-sided | Report sign, magnitude, and Holm-adjusted p; the narrative question is whether few-shot exemplars add, subtract, or match zero-shot CoT. |
| H3 (secondary) | C3 (Self-consistency, N=5, T=0.7) differs from C1. | two-sided | Report sign, magnitude, and Holm-adjusted p; the narrative question is whether the five-times token spend yields a measurable success gain over C1. |

Holm family for primary inference equals {H1, H1c, H2, H3}. A pre-registered dominance plot (delta success on x-axis, delta cost-adjusted score on y-axis, one point per tier) is the canonical visual for telling the success-vs-cost story.

## B. Platform - WorkArena++ Tier Taxonomy

WorkArena++ is assumed to be the BrowserGym-served ServiceNow benchmark. The exact tier list is ratified-by-researcher and pending confirmation; no specific task IDs from the suite are used in this design.

Adopted candidate tier list (the design treats these as parameters to be locked pre-execution):

| Tier code | Candidate name | Example capability | Sample-size stratum |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | list / lookup | read-only retrieval on ServiceNow records | small-to-mid |
| T2 | search / navigation | multi-page traversal, filter/sort | mid |
| T3 | forms | create or edit record via form fields | mid |
| T4 | configuration | change system settings or workflows | small |
| T5 | composite or plan | multi-step, cross-page objectives | small (hardest) |

If the ratified list differs, the only knob that must change is per-tier sample allocation in Section H; everything downstream is tier-symbolic. Counters external to the design are revisited once the ratified tier set is in hand.

## C. Agent Stack

Base LLM. Single fixed chat model across all cells. Default proposal, pending confirmation of API access and pinning: a current frontier chat model in the GPT-4o or Claude-3.5-Sonnet class with at least 128k context, function- or tool-calling disabled (WorkArena++ uses a discrete action enum, not tool calls). The exact model id is pinned in a single model.lock file before execution and never changed mid-run. All four cells C0, C1, C2, C3 use that same id.

BrowserGym / ServiceNow. BrowserGym (release: assumption - use the most recent stable BrowserGym that ships with the adopted WorkArena++; pending confirmation) over headless Chromium controlling a ServiceNow Personal Developer Instance or shared testing tenant. Assumption: one instance per worker; instance snapshot id is fixed. UI locale: en-US (see Section L).

Observation to prompt interface.
- Page observation equals pruned HTML accessibility tree, capped at about 6k tokens.
- Action format equals BrowserGym's discrete enum.
- Prompt payload per step is a tuple of system, goal, observation tree, last action, last error, and chat history of (thought, action, observation) tuples. History is windowed to the last K turns (K=10 by default).

CoT insertion slot. A single think-block immediately before the action, channel-separated and logged verbatim for failure-mode coding (Section E).

Length-control mechanism. All four cells are constrained to a per-step output budget of at most 192 tokens total (think plus action), enforced by a stop sequence and a downstream parser. The Section G ablation explicitly tests what happens when this cap is doubled.

Decoding settings.

| Cell | Temperature | Top-p | Number of samples | Aggregation | Seed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C0 No-CoT | 0 | 1.0 | 1 | n/a | fixed |
| C1 Zero-shot CoT | 0 | 1.0 | 1 | n/a | fixed |
| C2 Few-shot CoT | 0 | 1.0 | 1 | n/a | fixed |
| C3 Self-consistency | 0.7 | 1.0 | 5 | majority action (think discarded) | fixed, plus per-sample index |

Prompt template skeleton (literal slots). Slots R and F are the only differences across cells; everything else is identical.

SYSTEM:
You are an agent controlling a ServiceNow instance. You observe an accessibility tree, you think if asked, and you emit exactly one BrowserGym action. Never exceed 192 output tokens.

GOAL: {goal}
OBSERVATION: {ax_tree}
LAST_ACTION: {last_action}
LAST_ERROR: {last_error}

R is the reasoning-instruction block (differs per cell).
F is the exemplar block (only present in C2).

NOW EMIT ONE ACTION.

R per cell:

- C0: Plan in one short sentence, then act. This is a no-reasoning filler to match verbosity.
- C1: Think step by step about the goal and the current page before acting.
- C2: inherits C1 R, exact same text.
- C3: inherits C1 R, exact same text; only temperature and N change.

F per cell:

- C0: none.
- C1: none.
- C2: k=3 worked think-action-observation exemplars drawn from the same tier, disjoint from the test set (see Section D).
- C3: none (no exemplars; reasoning sampled 5 times).

C4 (tool-augmented scratchpad) is included only if its R can be length-matched to C1 within plus or minus 10 percent of output-token expectation on a 50-step dry run; otherwise it is dropped from the run. The design is built so C4 can be added or removed without touching anything else.

## D. Protocol

Trials per task times cell: 3 (absorbs stochasticity for paired tests). Median of 3 trials is the task score. Max steps per trial: 25 (T5: 40). Wall-clock timeout per trial: 10 min. Per-step HTTP timeout: 30 s. Retry policy inside a trial: none. Trial rerun on infra error: at most 1, flagged. Environment reset: hard rollback to a known post-login snapshot before every trial; verified by a sentinel element. Randomization: Latin-square ordering of cells across tasks. Exemplar pool (C2): 5 held-out exemplar tasks per tier, disjoint from test tasks by construction. Exemplar sampling per trial: k=3 drawn without replacement from the tier pool, randomized per trial but pool is fixed. Seed hygiene: Python, NumPy, the LLM SDK, and BrowserGym are all seeded; seeds are logged per trial.

Exemplar-pool disjointness rule (C2). The exemplar pool is constructed once, before any test task is sampled, by selecting 5 demonstration tasks per tier from the WorkArena++ training portion or, if the suite does not ship a train/test split, from a frozen carve-out. The test task set is then drawn strictly disjoint from this pool by id. A single-bit audit (exemplar-in-test-set leads to run abort) is in CI before any result is reported. This guarantees C2 cannot leak task content into the test set.

## E. Metrics

| Metric | Tier | Definition | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| success | primary (H1) | Indicator that the trial reached the task's terminal done with the success predicate true on the post-condition check. Per trial; median of 3 per task times cell. | 0/1 |
| delta_success | primary | Paired (task-level) C1 minus C0 on the median-success-per-task summary. | proportion points |
| cost-adjusted score | co-primary (H1c) | success per 1,000 total tokens (input plus output, summed over the whole trial). | 1 per 1k tok |
| delta_cost-adjusted | co-primary | Paired C1 minus C0 on cost-adjusted score. | 1 per 1k tok |
| steps | secondary | Median steps-to-success over the 3 trials; for failed trials equals max_steps plus 1 (censored). | int |
| tokens_in | secondary | Sum of prompt tokens across all turns in a trial. | tokens |
| tokens_out | secondary | Sum of completion tokens across all turns in a trial. | tokens |
| dollar per success | secondary | (tokens_in times cost_in plus tokens_out times cost_out) divided by success. | USD |
| latency | secondary | Wall-clock seconds per trial and per step. | s |
| hallucination rate | secondary | Per-trial indicator that any step's think references a UI element not in the ax-tree. | 0/1 |
| loop rate | secondary | Per-trial indicator of at least 2 consecutive identical state-action pairs. | 0/1 |
| failure-mode code | secondary | One of 6 codes, labelled on every failed trial (taxonomy below). | categorical |
| Brier on done-confidence | secondary | Agent emits a 0 to 1 done-confidence before each done action; Brier equals mean of (confidence minus actual_success) squared. Instruction is identical across cells. | score |

Failure-mode taxonomy (6 codes). A failed trial is assigned exactly one code by manual review, with the think log as primary evidence. The codes are: wrong_goal (agent misinterpreted the instruction); hallucinated_element (agent referenced a UI element not in the ax-tree); action_format_error (agent emitted a malformed action); loop (agent repeated the same state-action); premature_stop (agent called done before goal was achieved); post_condition_check_failed (agent thought it was done but the predicate failed). Inter-rater reliability is reported for the subset double-coded by a second human; agreement target is Cohen kappa at least 0.7. If a judge LLM is the second coder (allowed only at this auditing step), the prompt is fixed and its outputs are reported alongside kappa to keep evaluator bias visible.

## F. Controls and Confounders

Prompt length as free parameter. C0 is given a matched-verbosity filler ("Plan in one short sentence, then act"). Output cap (192 tok) is identical across cells. A length-matched sub-analysis in Section G explicitly swaps CoT for filler to test whether any effect survives.

CoT leakage into C0 (instruction artefact). Canary task: 10 atomically-short look-up tasks are run with C0's prompt but with C1's literal R block pasted in verbatim. If the canary shows greater than 2 pp drift vs. plain C0, the architecture leaks and the design quarantines those 10 tasks out of H1 inference.

Temperature drift between deterministic cells. C0, C1, C2 all run at T=0; only C3 switches to T=0.7. The cost of C3 is recorded separately and is not silently averaged into the headline.

Tool or capability parity. All cells use the same BrowserGym action enum; function-calling, retrieval, and web search are disabled across the board.

Caching. LLM call-side caching is disabled; static prompt-template caching on the client side is enabled. Each trial's exact tokens are re-counted in post-processing.

Prompt-version pinning. Every prompt template is stored under a versioned path. The execution harness refuses to start if the loaded prompt's date stamp differs from the one in model.lock. No mid-run edits are permitted.

Exemplar-pool identity. Frozen before any test task is sampled (Section D).

Order effects. Latin square across cells within each task. First-trial contamination is tested as a covariate in Section G.

Random seed reproducibility. All RNGs seeded and logged per trial; failure to reproduce a trial from logs is itself a logged event.

## G. Analysis Plan

Statistical unit. The task. One observation per task times cell is the median of 3 trials.

Pairing. Every task sees every cell (within-subject). Pairing is therefore at the task level.

Primary test family.

- H1 (success delta): Wilcoxon signed-rank, one-sided C1 greater than C0; tiebreaker McNemar on per-trial success counts.
- H1c (cost-adjusted delta): Wilcoxon signed-rank, one-sided C1 greater than C0; tiebreaker paired bootstrap on the score.
- H2 (C2 vs C1): Wilcoxon signed-rank, two-sided; tiebreaker paired bootstrap.
- H3 (C3 vs C1): Wilcoxon signed-rank, two-sided; tiebreaker paired bootstrap.

Multiple-comparison correction. Holm-Bonferroni across {H1, H1c, H2, H3} at family-wise alpha equals 0.05.

Effect sizes. Cohen's d for paired proportions on the per-task median scores; Cliff's delta as the non-parametric backup. 95% bootstrap CIs on delta with 10,000 resamples (task-resampling preserves within-task pairing).

Disagreement-narration rule (H1 vs H1c). When H1 and H1c disagree, the headline paragraph narrates this using tier-by-tier delta tables, the dominance plot (Section A), and the numeric spend ratio equals median tokens(C1) divided by median tokens(C0). No claim of improvement is made on H1c alone if H1 fails; each is reported with its own corrected p-value.

Stratified breakdown by tier. A tier times cell interaction test (Friedman-style over tasks within tier, block by cell) is the primary heterogeneity report.

Ablations (pre-registered).

- A1 few-shot count k in {1, 3, 5}: exemplar dose-response on success and on token cost.
- A2 prompt-length-matched sub-analysis: replace C1's think block with same-length filler before action.
- A3 output-cap doubling (192 to 384 tok): whether CoT was cap-limited.
- A4 drop C4 (or include if length-matchable): tool-augmented scratchpad cost/value, only if Section C gate passes.
- A5 calibration volume check (Brier): whether identical done-confidence instruction produces non-degenerate confidences in all cells.

Robustness replications. A 10 percent subsample of tasks is re-run from scratch with fresh seeds per cell; the headline deltas are recomputed. A successful replication requires the original delta direction to hold on the subsample.

## H. Power and Sample-Size - Planning Sketch

Sample-size philosophy. Because no run has been executed, this is a planning sketch that is contingent on assumption Z1 (pending confirmation): per-tier task counts once the Section B tier list is ratified. The design treats tiers as stratifying blocks; sample-size allocation is proportional to tier difficulty (T5 gets the most trials per task because expected variance is largest there), with a floor of 20 tasks per tier for the headline contrasts.

Closed-form power for paired delta success. Treating each task's median outcome as a Bernoulli with per-cell success probability p_i, the effective paired test on n tasks has detection power roughly governed by:
- effect delta equals 7 pp (assumption Z2: planning target in the 5 to 10 pp band; pending confirmation that this is realistic for the chosen model).
- baseline proportion p_0 about 0.5 (assumption Z3: planning target; pending confirmation by a pre-registered pilot).
- sd of delta about sqrt(2 p_0 (1-p_0) - 2 rho sqrt(p_0 q_0 p_1 q_1)) with rho about 0.6 (assumption Z4: high within-task correlation under matched-pairs).
- alpha equals 0.05 after Holm over 4 tests, giving per-comparison alpha about 0.0127.
- power target 0.80.

Under these assumptions, a normal-approximation calculation gives n about 60 tasks per tier for the H1 contrast, and about 80 per tier if rho drops to 0.4. The 10 percent robustness replication borrows no power; it is run on top of n.

Per-tier allocation (planning).

| Tier | Planned tasks (n) | Why |
|---|---|---|
| T1 list/lookup | 40 | low variance ceiling; smaller n suffices |
| T2 search/navigation | 60 | nominal |
| T3 forms | 60 | nominal |
| T4 configuration | 60 | nominal; expect lower p_0 so delta detection harder |
| T5 composite or plan | 80 | higher variance, headroom for ceiling effects |
| Total | about 300 tasks | across cells times 3 trials yields about 3600 trials |

These n's are placeholders. The locked pre-execution document replaces them with the actual flowing numbers once the task pool sizes are known.

On the choice of delta equals 7 pp as a planning target. No prior-paper magnitudes or task-id-specific numbers are cited because they are not verifiable from the supplied workspace. The 7 pp band is a planning convenience that is plausibly detectable with n about 60 tasks per tier, paired; if model-level variance is much lower (a high-performing model), a 3 pp delta becomes detectable with the same n; if much higher, the design accepts lower power on smaller delta and reports it as a statistical-conclusion threat in Section I.

## I. Threats to Validity (each tied to a mitigation already in the design)

- Construct - CoT leak from prompt scaffold into C0 (instruction artefact): Mitigated by the C0 canary task (Section F), which flags any drift greater than 2 pp; affected tasks are quarantined.
- Construct - Improvement conflates success with cost: Mitigated by treating delta_success and delta_cost-adjusted score as both pre-registered co-primaries (Section A); tier breakdown shows where they disagree.
- Internal - Task-content leakage from C2 exemplars into test tasks: Mitigated by exemplar pool built before the test set and verified disjoint by id (Section D); canary audit runs in CI.
- Internal - First-trial contamination from random seeding: Mitigated by Latin square per task (Section D); first trial of session is a covariate in Section G.
- Internal - Infrastructure flakiness mistaken for agent failure: Mitigated by trial rerun policy (Section D) that flags infra errors distinctly from LLM-side failures.
- Internal - Verbosity confounded with reasoning presence: Mitigated by identical output token cap across cells, matched-verbosity filler in C0, and A2 length-matched sub-analysis (Section G).
- External - One model, one prompt template: Mitigated only by being documented as a Section L limitation; out of scope to fix without a model-times-condition design that quadruples compute.
- External - ServiceNow or BrowserGym version drift across runs: Mitigated by pinning BrowserGym and WorkArena++ versions in model.lock (Section C).
- External - en-US locale only: Documented in Section L.
- Statistical conclusion - Multiple comparisons across 4 hypotheses: Mitigated by Holm-Bonferroni across {H1, H1c, H2, H3} (Section G).
- Statistical conclusion - Non-normality of paired delta on small per-tier n: Mitigated by Wilcoxon as primary, Cliff's delta as non-parametric backup, and bootstrap CIs.
- Statistical conclusion - Calibration metric non-identifiability if done-confidence prompt is not actually attended to: Mitigated by A5 explicitly checking all cells emit non-degenerate confidences before any Brier comparison.
- Statistical conclusion - Pilot-derived p_0 assumption wrong by a wide margin: Mitigated by recomputing power from a small pilot (10 tasks) before main run and re-allocating n if needed.

## J. Feasibility and Compute

Token-volume order-of-magnitude estimate (assumption Z5, pending confirmation), per trial:
- prompt input per step about 4000 tokens (assumption);
- output per step: C0 about 50 tok, C1 and C2 about 170 tok, C3 about 170 tok times 5 samples equals 850 tok (assumption);
- steps per trial: median about 10, max 25.

Per-trial tokens about 40,000 in plus 500 to 1700 out. Per-trial spend is dominated by input; the C0 versus C1 token-ratio is about 1.0 to 1.04x. C3 multiplies output about five times, but output is small relative to input.

Total budget sketch (using Section H n equals 300 tasks, 3 trials, 4 cells).

| Cell | Trials | Approximate output tokens total | Approximate input tokens total |
|---|---|---|---|
| C0 | 900 | about 0.5 M | about 36 M |
| C1 | 900 | about 1.5 M | about 36 M |
| C2 | 900 | about 1.5 M | about 36 M |
| C3 | 900 | about 7.5 M | about 36 M (output times 5 dominates spend) |

Assumption Z6, pending confirmation: at an indicative frontier-model rate of about 5 USD per Mtok in and about 15 USD per Mtok out, total wall spend across all four cells is on the order of low-to-mid single-digit USD-thousands. This is a planning sketch whose numeric values are explicitly dependent on Z5 and Z6.

ServiceNow / BrowserGym provisioning. 24 CPU cores means run 24 BrowserGym jobs in parallel (one BrowserGym worker per ServiceNow PDI or shared-tenant snapshot). One ServiceNow tenant per worker avoids cross-instance interference; a pre-execution fixture script snapshots the post-login state and is replayed before every trial (Section D).

Time budget (assumption Z7). Average wall-clock per trial about 2 to 5 min (assumption, pending pilot). With 24 parallel workers and about 3600 trials, the run completes in roughly 5 to 13 hours of wall time. The bottleneck is BrowserGym rendering latency, which limit-parallelism gives directly.

Excluded from the budget: human-labour for failure-mode coding (about 300 to 900 failed trials expected; coded by 1 reviewer plus audit sub-sample) is a small, separate cost.

## K. Pre-Registration Checklist

- Fixed (locked before any execution): the four cells C0, C1, C2, C3 and their literal prompt slot diffs (Section C); the output cap; the tier list (Section B); the exemplar-pool disjointness rule and audit; the primary test family plus Holm over {H1, H1c, H2, H3}; the co-primary endpoint set; the canary task design; the seed policy; the LLM id pinned in model.lock.
- Fixed plus subject to pilot-driven n adjustment: per-tier sample-size n (Section H); the pilot recomputes power and is the only path by which n can change.
- Fixed plus conditional: including C4 (tool-augmented scratchpad) only if Section C length-match passes; otherwise C4 is dropped, not approximated.
- Exploratory, labelled as such: A1 k-dosing sweep (k in {1, 3, 5}); A3 output-cap doubling; A5 Brier volume check; failure-mode-rate stratification by tier beyond the planned interaction test; any post-hoc tier split of T5.
- Not in scope: cross-model replication; non-English locales; human-in-the-loop variants; cost-savings via model distillation; comparison to non-CoT plan-and-solve prompting families.

## L. Limitations

1. Single-model design. External validity is bounded to the locked model id; the answer may not transfer.
2. Single prompt template. The conclusions are conditional on the Section C template; small prompt-engineering changes beyond the R slot could move the headline.
3. English-only ServiceNow locale. Other locales may have different ax-tree noise characteristics; not measured.
4. Evaluator-LLM bias in failure coding. If a judge LLM is the second coder (Section E), its biases are reported alongside kappa; the primary coder is human.
5. No human-in-the-loop. All actions are model-emitted; request-for-help behavior is not modelled.
6. Task-solving versus generalization. The design measures performance on the benchmark's own tasks; it does not measure generalization to unseen ServiceNow tenants, custom instances, or post-upgrade environments.
7. Source-verifiability. No WorkArena++ task ID, no specific prior-paper success-rate number, and no model version string from outside the supplied workspace is invoked as evidence; every such detail is treated as a researcher-ratified parameter to be locked before execution.

---

## Summary for the Reviewer

This design is a complete, executable, design-only specification for a matched-pairs experiment that asks whether CoT prompting improves LLM-agent task-solving on WorkArena++. With the C0/C1 split as the canonical headline and cost-adjusted success as the co-primary pre-registered alongside it, with Holm-Bonferroni over {H1, H1c, H2, H3}, with paired Wilcoxon tests and bootstrap CIs on delta, with matched-verbosity fillers, a leak-canary, exemplar-pool disjointness, prompt-version pinning, Latin-square ordering, and a 10 percent robustness replication on fresh seeds, the experiment WOULD settle, with pre-registered decision rules per hypothesis in Section A and a pre-registered dominance plot to narrate any success-vs-cost disagreement, whether C1 outperforms C0 on this fixed model and prompt template. Secondary cells C2 (k=3 few-shot) and C3 (N=5 self-consistency at T=0.7) are scored in the same Holm family and pre-registered ablations A1 to A5 dissect the result along prompt-length, exemplar dose, scratchpad, and calibration axes. Every concrete number tied to an unverified assumption (task counts, prompt and input token sizes, exact per-Mtok rates, expected per-trial wall-clock, effective delta detection threshold) is annotated [assumption X / pending confirmation] and is the locked-parameter list that, when finalized, fully specifies execution. No measurement is, or is presented as, observed.

- No hay README, código de WorkArena++, dumps de tareas, scripts, ni CSV/JSONL de resultados.
- En `/home/actor` y `/tmp` solo hay directorios vacíos.

**Entorno (informativo, no se usará para correr nada):**
- Python 3.12.3, sin dependencias científicas instaladas (solo paquetes base del sistema: `asn1crypto`, `attrs`, `Babel`).
- Red deshabilitada (bubblewrap) → imposible clonar/instalar la suite real desde aquí.
- 24 CPU, sin GPU.

**¿Qué información falta y qué tan sólido es el insumo?**
- Insumo "esqueleto" pero internamente consistente: la propia `task.json` reza *"Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required"* y *"Do not claim that an experiment was run"* → es coherente con un brief de solo diseño.
- Falta: descripción operacional de WorkArena++ (taxonomía exacta de tareas, entorno ServiceNow simulado, métricas nativas), presupuesto de cómputo/API, modelo(s) candidatos confirmados, y criterios de parada del agente. Por eso, en la sección 3 marco explícitamente qué asumo y qué quiero que confirmes antes del plan final.

---

## 2) Enfoque de diseño experimental propuesto 🎯

### 2.1 Pregunta de investigación e hipótesis
- **Pregunta:** ¿El prompting chain-of-thought mejora la capacidad de resolución de tareas de agentes LLM en WorkArena++?
- **H1 (principal):** Una condición con CoT produce mayor tasa de éxito en tareas de WorkArena++ que una condición sin CoT, controlando por tarea e instancia.
- **H0:** No hay diferencia en tasa de éxito entre condiciones CoT y no-CoT.
- **H2 (secundaria):** El costo (pasos y tokens) de CoT es mayor, pero su relación costo/éxito domina a la condición directa.
- **H3 (secundaria, mecanismo):** Las ganancias de CoT se concentran en tareas *composicionales / multi-paso* y desaparecen en tareas atómicas triviales.

### 2.2 Variables
| Tipo | Variable | Operacionalización |
|---|---|---|
| IV (entre-intentos, intra-tarea) | Esquema de prompting | 6 niveles (ver 2.3) |
| DV principal | Éxito de tarea | Binario (1=éxito, 0=fallo) según verificador de WorkArena++ |
| DV secundarias | Pasos hasta terminar | Entero (≤ N_max) |
|  | Tokens totales (in+out) | Entero |
|  | Latencia wall-clock | Segundos |
|  | Tasa de recuperación tras error | # recuperaciones / # errores |
|  | Fidelidad de plan (composicional) | Subscore del grader nativo |
| Controles | Modelo base, temperatura, top-p, max-steps, system prompt scaffold, instancia de tarea, estado inicial del entorno, budget de tokens | Idénticos en todas las condiciones, solo varía la **instrucción de razonamiento** |

### 2.3 Condiciones a comparar (todos comparten scaffold y parseador de acciones)
1. **Direct** — emite acción sin razonamiento (baseline principal).
2. **Plan-then-Act directo** — pide planificar brevemente y luego actuar; controla el “ruido” de añadir texto sin CoT explícito.
3. **Zero-shot-CoT** — “Let’s think step by step” (Kojima et al.).
4. **Few-shot-CoT** — 3–5 ejemplos trabajados con cadenas de razonamiento.
5. **Self-Ask** — descomposición en sub-preguntas con respuestas explícitas.
6. **ReAct** — bucle Thought / Action / Observation entrelazado con llamadas al entorno.

Justificación: cubrimos tanto CoT “puro” (3 y 4) como CoT acoplado al entorno (5 y 6) y dos controles de longitud (1 y 2), siguiendo la práctica estándar de la literatura sobre prompting para agentes web/enterprise (Yao et al. 2022 ReAct; Press et al. 2022 Self-Ask; Kojima et al. 2022 Zero-shot-CoT).

### 2.4 Subconjunto de tareas / benchmark
- Trabajar sobre el **conjunto público de WorkArena++** (Drouin et al., NeurIPS 2024), estratificado por categorías canónicas del benchmark:
  1. *List/Record operations* (atómicas).
  2. *Knowledge-base lookup* (consulta).
  3. *Catalog / form-filling* (semi-estructuradas).
  4. *Workflow / approvals* (procesos).
  5. *Compositional / multi-app* (multi-paso, multi-app).
- **Subconjunto:** ≈ 50 tareas únicas (≈ 10 por categoría) con dificultad media (excluir floor y ceiling tasks).
- Criterios de inclusión: (a) tener verificador automático nativo del benchmark; (b) resolubles en ≤ 30 pasos; (c) no requerir credenciales o datos sintéticos no públicos.

### 2.5 Métricas y análisis estadístico
- **Primario (binario, pareado por tarea):** McNemar test sobre pares discordantes; IC95% bootstrap (10k remuestreos) sobre Δ de tasa de éxito. Tamaño de efecto: Cohen's *h* y odds ratio pareado.
- **Secundarias (continuas, pareadas):** Wilcoxon signed-rank con corrección Holm-Bonferroni entre las 15 comparaciones por pares (6 condiciones → C(6,2)=15).
- **Reporte:** tabla con media/mediana por condición, Δ vs. Direct, IC95% y p-ajustado; figura de rendimiento vs. costo (éxito vs. tokens).
- **Sub-análisis H3:** interacción (condición × categoría) con regresión logística mixta (éxito ~ condición × categoría + (1|tarea) + (1|seed)).

### 2.6 Modelo(s) base
- Modelo principal reproducible y razonablemente capaz: **una familia open-weights** (p. ej. Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct o equivalente disponible por API) usada en todas las condiciones.
- Modelo secundario opcional de frontera (p. ej. GPT-4o / Claude Sonnet) si el presupuesto lo permite, para chequear generalización entre familles — sin sobre-ponderar en el análisis primario.
- Decodificación fija: `temperature=0` cuando el backend lo permita, si no `≤ 0.2`; `top_p=1.0`, `max_tokens` por paso idéntico entre condiciones.

### 2.7 Corridas / trials y randomización
- **r = 5 semillas** por celda (tarea × condición). Con 50 tareas × 6 condiciones × 5 trials = **1 500 episodios** por modelo.
- **Diseño pareado intra-tarea**, con orden de condiciones contrabalanceado con cuadrado latino para controlar efectos de orden / posición (la misma instancia de tarea se sirve a todas las condiciones bajo el mismo estado inicial del entorno).
- Posible sesgo de temperatura controlado comparando además r = 5 con `temperature=0` *vs.* muestreo estocástico en una submuestra.

### 2.8 Tamaño de efecto detectable y poder
- Con N_d = 50 tareas pareadas y asumiendo π_disc = 0.20 entre pares discordantes, McNemar detecta un Δ ≈ 10 pp con α = .05 y poder ≈ 0.80.
- Diferencias ≥ **10 puntos porcentuales** entre CoT y Direct → detectable con alta confianza.
- Diferencias < 5 pp → indistinguibles de ruido sin multiplicar trials o tareas.
- Si el presupuesto lo permite, subir a N_d = 80 tareas detectaría Δ ≈ 8 pp.

### 2.9 Amenazas a la validez (y mitigaciones)
- **Validez interna:**
  - Sensibilidad a la formulación del prompt → mismo *template* base, solo cambia la cláusula de razonamiento; reportar "prompt-versión" como metadato y replicar al menos una variante de wording en una submuestra.
  - Variabilidad entre semillas → promediar sobre r ≥ 5 e IC95% bootstrap; reportar también mediana.
  - Contaminación de entrenamiento → tareas WorkArena++ son sintéticas y de octubre 2023 en adelante; documentar fecha de corte de conocimiento del modelo y, si es viable, reescribir 5–10 tareas como *paraphrasings* para un *robustness check*.
  - Estocasticidad del entorno ServiceNow → fijar semilla del simulador y snapshot del estado inicial.
- **Validez externa:**
  - Single-model bias → incluir segundo modelo si el presupuesto lo permite.
  - Generalización fuera de ServiceNow → discutir explícitamente como limitación.
- **Validez de constructo:**
  - “CoT” no es una técnica monolítica → incluir varias variantes (zero-shot, few-shot, Self-Ask, ReAct) para no atribuir el efecto a una sola formulación.
  - Métrica “éxito” no captura calidad intermedia → añadir fidelidad de plan y tasa de recuperación.
- **Construcción / comparaciones múltiples:**
  - 15 comparaciones por pares → corrección Holm; análisis primario pareado y análisis secundario con regresión mixta.

---

## 3) Suposiciones e incertidumbres ⚠️🤔

**Suposiciones que asumo para que el plan sea ejecutable (y que conviene confirmar):**
1. El benchmark a usar es **WorkArena++ público** (Drouin et al., NeurIPS 2024) servido a través de ServiceNow WAS; existe verificador automático por tarea.
2. El presupuesto permite **r = 5 trials × 50 tareas × 6 condiciones = 1 500 episodios** por modelo, corriendo en API o *self-host*. (Sin presupuesto explícito en `task.json`.)
3. El “modelo base” puede ser uno de los sugeridos (Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct o equivalente) y no es necesario comparar familias como efecto principal.
4. El entorno simulado es **estrictamente reproducible** dado una semilla del simulador y un snapshot del estado — hipótesis operacionalmente necesaria para validar el pareo intra-tarea.
5. “Mejora” se define como superioridad estadística en **tasa de éxito pareada**; el resto de métricas son secundarias.
6. La taxonomía de categorías (List/Record, KB lookup, Catalog/form, Workflow, Compositional) y la noción de “composicional” son las que maneja la librería oficial — verificar en el README del repositorio upstream.
7. Las plantillas de prompt para cada condición se pueden mantener idénticas excepto en la cláusula de razonamiento; cualquier desviación se reporta como sub-condición.

**Incertidumbres / riesgos abiertos:**
- ❓ **Presupuesto de cómputo / API no especificado** en `task.json`. Sin esta cifra no puedo fijar el cardinal de tareas, réplicas o modelo de frontera sin arriesgar sub- o sobre-dimensionar.
- ❓ **Acceso a la suite WorkArena++.** La red está deshabilitada en este sandbox; no puedo verificar la versión exacta del benchmark ni descargar el set. Habría que confirmar offline que las tareas y categorías que asumo siguen vigentes.
- ❓ **Modelo base confirmado.** Hace falta que confirmes si podemos usar API comercial (conlleva costo) o solo modelos locales/self-host.
- ❓ **Tolerancia a comparaciones múltiples y α.** ¿Quieres control fuerte (Holm) o análisis exploratorio sin corrección con FDR Benjamini-Hochberg?
- ❓ **Definición exacta de éxito.** El grader nativo puede permitir múltiples terminaciones “subóptimas pero válidas”; aclarar si se acepta el verificador black-box o si necesitas un grader custom.
- ❓ **Contaminación.** Si el modelo elegido se entrenó posterior a la liberación de WorkArena++ (post-oct-2023), hay riesgo de leakage; habría que medirlo con tareas *paraphrased held-out*.
- ❓ **Tamaño del modelo vs. efecto CoT.** En la literatura el efecto de CoT se debilita o se vuelve contraproducente en modelos pequeños; si el modelo es < 13B, el plan quizá requiera cotas más explícitas sobre esto.
- ❓ **CoT como “tratamiento”.** Distinguir entre “CoT *en prompt*” (lo que testeamos aquí) y CoT *emergente* del propio modelo; queremos dejar claro que solo evaluamos el primero.
- ❓ **Estabilidad de la hipótesis H3.** No sabemos a priori si WorkArena++ tiene suficientes tareas puramente atómicas para hacer este contraste con poder.

---

**Listo para tu revisión 🙋.** Si estás de acuerdo con el enfoque (hipótesis, 6 condiciones pareadas, 50 tareas × 5 trials, análisis McNemar + Holm + regresión mixta, dos tamaños de efecto reportados), confírmamelo y paso a la siguiente vuelta con el **diseño final** (rationale completo, plan operativo paso a paso, controles y *feasibility checks*, plan de *robustness checks* y referencias a WorkArena++ que conviene citar). Si quieres cambiar cardinales, condiciones, modelo o métricas, dime y reescribo el plan antes de la entrega final.
